Does Blaine require a rental license if I am selling a rental house?

Yes, Blaine licenses rental property every year, and a buyer who inherits your tenants takes on that duty. The city's application page lists a $190 fee for a single family rental, attached or detached, and $180 per building plus $10 per unit for multi-family. The license expires on December 31, and owners with three consecutive years without violations qualify for a reduced fee.

Single family rentals get an interior inspection every three years and an exterior inspection every year. For a rental sale, hand the buyer the license, the last inspection result and the tenant lease documents. An owner-occupied house that you are simply selling does not need any of this.

What happens at recording and closing in Anoka County?

Anoka County records the deed, and its rules decide whether the document is accepted. Its recording requirements page lists what a transfer deed must carry.

  • State deed tax of .0033 times the net consideration when the price is over $3,000, which matches Minnesota Statute 287.21.
  • A $5 agricultural conservation fee.
  • A completed electronic Certificate of Real Estate Value and its number on the deed.
  • A "Send tax statements to" line with the buyer's name and address.
  • Delinquent taxes paid in full before the transfer.
  • A well disclosure certificate with a $54 fee, or one of the two well statements the county prints on its page.

Anoka County also explains that Minnesota has two land record systems, abstract and torrens, and that most Anoka County property is abstract, so a title search should look for any documents tied to the lot. Your title company usually handles the filing, but you should know what the list asks for.

How are Anoka County taxes and the homestead handled when a house sells?

Residential homestead property in Anoka County is billed in two halves, due the middle of May and of October (the 15th of each), and the county notes that late payment brings penalties even if you never received a statement. The county's homestead rules add a point sellers miss: the owner must tell the assessor within 30 days if the home sells or stops being a primary residence, and the county can remove the homestead and impose penalties if no one does.

The county's page also says a Certificate of Real Estate Value is due at the auditor's office when a property sells, as Minnesota Statute 272.115 requires. A qualifying disabled veteran can receive a market value exclusion of up to $300,000 on homestead property, so buyers who are veterans may ask about it. Have the closing agent split the current half-year between you and the buyer by closing date.

What disclosures does a Blaine seller owe?

Before you sign a purchase agreement for a residential property, Minnesota Statute 513.55 requires written disclosure of material facts you know that could adversely and significantly affect a buyer's use and enjoyment. Section 144.496 adds a radon disclosure: whether tests were done, the latest reports, any mitigation system, a radon warning statement and the Minnesota Department of Health booklet.

The city sits on glacial sand, ponds and wetlands, so basement moisture is a fair thing to document. Gather any sump pump records, past repairs and test results before the first showing so the written disclosure is accurate and complete.

More questions about Blaine, MN

Which county records a Blaine deed?

Anoka County for most of the city. Blaine also reaches into Ramsey County, so confirm your parcel's county on your tax statement before sending any documents.

Do I need to pay deed tax when I sell in Blaine?

Minnesota's state deed tax is imposed on the deed and is calculated at .0033 of the net consideration above $3,000. Ask your title company who pays it under your purchase agreement, since the agreement decides that.

Is a rental license transferable to the buyer of my Blaine rental?

Check with Blaine Housing Services before closing. The license is issued yearly and expires on December 31, so the new owner should expect to apply for their own and schedule any inspection the city requires.

What if my Blaine house has radon or basement water problems?

Disclose what you know in writing. Minnesota law requires disclosure of known radon test results and of material facts that could significantly affect a buyer, and a seller who skips them can be held liable for damages.

How long does a Blaine house usually take to sell for cash?

It depends on the buyer and the title work, but a cash sale has no lender appraisal, so closing is often a matter of weeks. Anoka County's recording checklist is the main step that can delay a closing if something is missing.

The Shoppes at Arbor Lakes opened in 2003 on a former gravel mining area, and Maple Grove has more retail space than almost any city in Minnesota other than Bloomington.

Commuters use Interstate 94, where the I-494 and I-694 connections meet at the Fish Lake split, along with U.S. Highway 169 on the eastern edge and Highway 610 across the north. Census data puts the average commute at 24.0 minutes.

Osseo Area School District 279 covers most addresses, and Maple Grove Senior High is the only public high school inside city limits. Wayzata Public Schools serves a portion of the city, so look up the district for your street before you advertise.

Which Maple Grove permits and licenses matter when you sell?

If you are finishing a project before you list, Maple Grove requires online permits for residential and commercial work through its ePermits system, and a permit is needed before a building is built, enlarged, altered, repaired, moved or demolished. Residential plan review can take one or two weeks, and a permit expires after 180 days if no work starts or no inspection is called in.

Open or expired permits are the kind of issue a buyer's title and inspection work can find, so call the Building Inspections line at 763-494-6060 if you are unsure what is on file for your address.

  • Rental dwelling license: the city's Community and Economic Development department handles it at 763-494-6040, and apartment licenses go through 763-494-6042.
  • Short-term rental license: required for any rental under 30 days, valid for one year, and issued only after an inspection and a training presentation.
  • Name match: the owner name on a short-term rental application must match state property records.

A landlord who sells a licensed rental should ask Community and Economic Development how the license is handled at sale and tell the buyer what the city requires.

How do property taxes and deed tax work on a Maple Grove sale?

Hennepin County bills Maple Grove owners twice a year, on May 15 and October 15, and a due date landing on a non-business day rolls to the next business day. The county mails valuation notices in March, based on the assessor's value as of January 2, and tax statements follow in March of the next year. Hennepin's tax information line is 612-348-3011.

A separate state deed tax applies at recording. Minnesota Statutes 287.21 sets it at 0.33% of net consideration over $3,000, with a flat $1.65 for transfers at or below that amount. It falls due the moment the deed is handed in for recording, and your closing agent usually collects it. Your purchase agreement should say who pays.

Hennepin explains that taxes depend on the levies of the county, city, school district and other taxing districts. Two school districts share the city, so check which one levies on your parcel.

What local history and conditions can come up with buyers?

The 2020 census recorded 27,507 housing units in the city, of which 2.8% were vacant, and 60.8% of households were married-couple households. The rental vacancy rate was 5.8% and the homeowner vacancy rate 0.7%.

Maple Grove became a city in 1974 and has grown quickly since interstate and highway upgrades in the 1970s. A tornado rated F3 struck the city on July 23, 1987, and the same storm tracked into Brooklyn Park, so buyers sometimes ask about roof age and storm history on older homes.

Winters here are cold and snowy, as across the Twin Cities. Drainage, gutters and the condition of the roof are easier to document when the ground is clear.

The city's lakes include Arbor, Cedar Island, Cook, Eagle, Edward, Fish, Mud, Pike, Rice, Teal, Weaver and West Arbor. Hennepin County maintains most of the larger roads, including County Road 10 (Bass Lake Road), County Road 30, Hemlock Lane and Weaver Lake Road, so a house on one of those corridors deals with county road projects as well as city ones.

The Pierre Bottineau House, built in 1854, was the first wood-frame house in the township and now sits in Elm Creek Park Reserve. The Grove, at I-94 and Maple Grove Parkway, holds a hospital complex and shopping.

Is a cash offer worth considering in Maple Grove?

A cash offer fits when you need a fixed closing date, own a dated house, or inherited a property you would rather not prepare for market. With a typical value of $418,300, repair bills on a Maple Grove house can be large, and a buyer who absorbs them can save you time even if the number is lower.

Request the number in writing and weigh it against a realistic listing, meaning the net after repairs, staging and the months you would carry the house. Settle who pays title charges, who signs a well disclosure if the lot has a well, and how funds reach you at closing.

More questions about Maple Grove, MN

Which city office handles permit questions for a Maple Grove property?

Building Inspections at 763-494-6060 can look up your address. Permits expire 180 days after issuance if no work starts or no inspection is called in, and an open permit is worth closing before you list.

What is the Minnesota deed tax on a Maple Grove sale?

The rate is 0.33% of net consideration over $3,000, payable at recording. Your purchase agreement sets which party covers it.

What are the Hennepin County payment dates for a Maple Grove house?

May 15 for the first half and October 15 for the second half. A non-business 15th pushes the deadline to the following business day.

Can I sell a Maple Grove house that is currently a short-term rental?

Yes. Maple Grove requires a license for any rental under 30 days, valid for one year and issued after an inspection, so a buyer who wants to keep renting short term should confirm the license steps with Community and Economic Development at 763-494-6040.

Which school district serves my Maple Grove house?

Most of the city is in Osseo Area School District 279, and part is in Wayzata Public Schools. Check your address with the district before you list.

St. Cloud at a glance

Selling in St. Cloud?

How do you sell a house fast in St. Cloud, Minnesota?

St. Cloud sellers can use an agent, find a buyer privately, or accept a cash offer from someone who buys the house as-is. The cash route fits houses with repairs, tenants, or a title problem, and the listing route fits a tidy house with time to spare.

St. Cloud is a rental-heavy market. Just 48.6 percent of homes are lived in by their owners in the 2020 to 2024 Census data, and a typical owner's home is valued at $225,000. Many sellers here own an investment house or inherited one, so the rental and vacancy rules below come up more often than they do in a typical suburb.

  • List when the house shows well and you can wait for a buyer's mortgage to clear.
  • Sell yourself when you have a buyer lined up and are comfortable with the paperwork.
  • Choose cash when a rental license, a vacant house, repairs or an estate make a conventional sale slow.

What should a seller know about the city of St. Cloud?

St. Cloud serves as seat of Stearns County, and the city also reaches into Benton and Sherburne counties. It lies on both banks of the Mississippi River, with the Sauk River along its northern edge, about 65 miles northwest of the Twin Cities. Interstate 94, U.S. Highways 10 and 52, and State Highways 15 and 23 serve it (Wikipedia).

Settlers founded three separate villages starting in 1853, called Upper Town, Middle Town and Lower Town, and the city incorporated in 1856. Ravines that once divided them are still visible. Granite quarries opened in the 1880s and gave the city the nickname Granite City.

  • Counties: because parcels sit in up to three counties, find your parcel's county before asking about taxes or records.
  • Schools: most of the city is in the St. Cloud Area School District, and part of the Benton County portion is in Sauk Rapids-Rice Public Schools.
  • Higher education: St. Cloud State University and St. Cloud Technical and Community College are in the city.
  • River: about 30 undeveloped Beaver Islands sit in the Mississippi near the university, and the city owns and runs the state's largest municipally managed hydroelectric dam.
  • Water: Lake George sits just south of downtown, and in 2021 the Minnesota Pollution Control Agency credited the city's stormwater work with bringing its phosphorus levels well below the state standard.
  • Climate: a humid continental climate with cold winters, a record low of minus 43 degrees, and a record high of 107 degrees.

What do Census figures show about St. Cloud homes?

The Census Bureau estimates 72,647 residents for July 1, 2025, up 4.4 percent from the April 2020 estimates base of 69,618. Households number 27,807 and the median gross rent is $1,003 a month.

St. Cloud housing and income snapshot, Census QuickFacts

Figures come from the Census QuickFacts page for St. Cloud. Census data also shows 77.1 percent of residents lived in the same house a year earlier, so roughly one in four people moved within or into the city in a single year.

What does St. Cloud require of rental property owners?

Any owner who lets a property be occupied in exchange for rent or other goods or services needs a St. Cloud rental license. Getting the license also requires rental training, so a seller who bought a house to rent will want to confirm it is current before a buyer asks.

The free training is now virtual and is taught by the Police, Fire and Health departments, and it covers St. Cloud ordinances and policies. After signing up, an owner has three months to finish it. The property owner, manager or another person in charge of the unit can attend (City of St. Cloud).

  • Pre-rental license application: the Housing and Code Enforcement page lists it for owners starting a rental.
  • Rental self-inspection checklist: lets an owner review items such as a posted license before staff inspect.
  • Vacant property registration: the Housing and Code Enforcement page lists an application for vacant houses, which matters if you inherited a house that sits empty.
  • License revocation: the city publishes a summary titled How to Lose a Rental License, drawn from its ordinances.

How do Stearns County taxes and records work for a St. Cloud seller?

Property tax and recording questions go to the county where the parcel sits, which is usually Stearns County. Its Auditor-Treasurer pages cover tax due dates, penalties, payment options, relief options, and a senior citizen property tax deferral, and its assessor publishes an annual assessment update each year.

For a house in the Benton or Sherburne portion, call that county's treasurer instead. Whichever county applies, ask for the payoff on both halves of the current year and any special assessments, and ask the county recorder what the deed and any certificate of real estate value must include.

  • Taxes: ask the Auditor-Treasurer for current and delinquent balances in writing before closing.
  • Assessment: ask the assessor if a recent remodel, permit or new addition changed the value.
  • Utility bills: the city's Health and Inspections pages link to utility billing, and an unpaid balance is worth settling before the sale.

Many St. Cloud sales involve more than one of these offices, so list them before you start. A house that straddles a county line or sits in the Benton or Sherburne portion is where mistakes happen, because the wrong county's office will answer from the wrong records.

What local details help when selling an older St. Cloud house?

Buyers of a St. Cloud house often ask how it has been used, whether as an owner's home, a licensed rental or a vacant property, so the paper trail matters.

The city runs complaint response and routine rental inspections through its Housing and Code Enforcement division, and it publishes information sheets on accessory structures, fences, off-street parking and recreational vehicles. Check those items on your own lot, because a shed, fence or parked trailer that does not meet the rules is easy to fix before an inspection.

The city also publishes a flyer on bed bugs for owners. Rental training questions go to the Police Department's information desk at 320-345-4444. If a rental has had a past infestation, have the treatment records ready to show a buyer.

More questions about St. Cloud, MN

Can I sell a St. Cloud rental house with tenants in it?

Yes, but the buyer will want to see the rental license, the lease terms and proof the owner finished the city's rental training. A cash buyer can take the house with tenants in place or after they move out.

Do I need rental training to hold a St. Cloud rental license?

Yes. The city requires rental training as a condition of licensing. It is free and virtual, and you get three months from sign-up to finish.

Which county do I call about taxes on a St. Cloud house?

Call the county where your parcel sits, which is Stearns County for most of the city. A smaller part lies in Benton and Sherburne counties, so check the parcel before you call.

Is St. Cloud mostly renters or owners?

About half. The Census owner-occupied rate is 48.6 percent for 2020 to 2024, so slightly more than half of homes are rented.

How do I handle an inherited, vacant house in St. Cloud?

Look at the city's vacant property registration application first, then confirm who holds title and who can sign. Ask the county treasurer for the tax balance so the closing can be scheduled around it.

Eagan at a glance

Selling in Eagan?
We buy Eagan houses as-is, with no commission, no repairs and no closing costs to you.

Where is Eagan and what are its boundaries?

Eagan lies in Dakota County south of Saint Paul, with the Minnesota River forming its western edge a short way above the Mississippi confluence. Land area is 31.18 square miles, elevation is about 945 feet, and the 2025 Census estimate is 67,109 people.

The northern edge follows Interstate 494, the eastern edge runs mostly along Minnesota Highway 3, the western edge is the river, and the southern boundary lies about a mile south of Cliff Road. Interstate 35E and Minnesota Highways 13, 55, 77 and 149 are the main routes. The ZIP codes are 55121, 55122 and 55123. The sparsely populated northern part of the city is convenient to the freeways and the Minneapolis-Saint Paul airport, which is why warehouses and distribution centers cluster there.

How did Eagan grow from farmland into a city of 67,000?

The city is named for Patrick Eagan, the first chairman of the town board, who farmed 220 acres near the present town hall. It was settled as an Irish farming community and was once called the onion capital of the United States. The town was established in 1860, and the city incorporated in 1972.

The big jump came in the 1980s, after Highway 77 was relocated and a six-lane bridge was built over the Minnesota River in 1980, followed by the last stretch of Interstate 35E in the mid-1980s.

  • 565 residents in 1860.
  • 3,382 in 1960 and 10,398 in 1970.
  • 20,700 in 1980 and 47,409 in 1990.
  • 63,557 in 2000 and 68,855 in 2020.
  • 67,109 in the 2025 estimate, about 2.5 percent below the 2020 estimate base.

The count more than doubled between 1980 and 1990, so many Eagan houses are now several decades old, and the original roofs, windows and kitchens of that growth period are common in resale listings.

Which employers and school districts matter to Eagan buyers?

Eagan has a large corporate and logistics base. The city's 2025 financial report ranked its largest employers.

  • Thomson Reuters, with 4,500 employees.
  • Blue Cross and Blue Shield of Minnesota, with 3,000.
  • The U.S. Postal Service and Prime Therapeutics, each with about 2,100.
  • UPS with 1,500, Ecolab with 1,400 and the Rosemount-Apple Valley-Eagan school district with 1,075.

The Minnesota Vikings moved their headquarters and practice facility to the former Northwest Airlines site, and the Twin Cities Orthopedics Performance Center opened in 2018. The Census Bureau recorded $1.29 billion in transportation and warehousing receipts in Eagan for 2022.

Schools come from three districts: Rosemount-Apple Valley-Eagan (District 196), West St. Paul-Mendota Heights-Eagan (District 197) and Burnsville-Eagan-Savage (District 191). Eagan High School, Blackhawk Middle School and Dakota Hills Middle School belong to District 196. Confirm the district for an exact address before a listing names a school.

What do ownership and income figures show for Eagan?

A middle-of-the-road Eagan owner-occupied home is valued near $397,000, and about a third of households rent. The table lists the main figures.

Eagan ownership and income snapshot. Source: Census Bureau QuickFacts, five-year survey period ending 2024, plus the 2025 estimate.
MeasureEagan
Residents, 2025 estimate67,109
Share of homes lived in by owners67.7%
Owner-occupied home value, midpoint$397,100

Residents with a four-year degree or more54.7%

Households average 2.39 people, and 86.7 percent of residents stayed in the same house over the prior year, so turnover is modest.

Does an Eagan rental license pass to the buyer?

No. Eagan adopted its rental licensing ordinance on March 21, 2023, and licenses are issued each year and are not transferable, so a new owner must apply for a new license.

  • The 2026/27 fee is $165 per year for a single-unit rental, plus a $25 application fee and a $300 conversion fee when an owner-occupied home becomes a rental.
  • Every rental unit is inspected about once every three years or on complaint, and landlords give tenants at least 24 hours of notice.
  • Exempt rentals include units rented to the owner's qualifying relatives, state-licensed housing, rooms inside an owner-occupied home and contract-for-deed purchases recorded with Dakota County.

Late renewal costs 10 percent of the base fee in the first 30 days, 50 percent from 30 to 60 days and 100 percent after 60. Call Community Development at 651-675-5681 before you sell a tenant-occupied house. A buyer who plans to keep tenants has to apply for a license in their own name.

What permit and flood checks come up before an Eagan sale?

Eagan splits permits into two tracks. Building permits go through the online ePermits system, and Building Inspections at 651-675-5675 books inspections in 30-minute slots from 7:30 a.m. to 3:30 p.m. on weekdays. Zoning permits cover projects that need no building permit, and they are free.

Fences, patios, sport courts, driveway replacements, sidewalks, detached decks below 30 inches, one-story sheds up to 200 square feet, retaining walls under four feet and docks all fall under zoning permits. City staff generally answer within two to five business days. The city's property information page lets you view property records and check for special assessments, and most records include scanned permits, inspection history and site surveys that help a buyer see what was done.

On flood risk, the city says every property is in FEMA Flood Zone X except those in Zone AE along the Minnesota River. The maps date from December 2, 2011, so call the Planning Department or FEMA to confirm an address.

Where does an Eagan deed get recorded?

Dakota County accepts deeds only at its Administration Center in Hastings. Bring them by appointment, or mail them with a cover letter, a return envelope and a phone number to the Property Taxation and Records office at 1590 Highway 55.

The state charges deed tax at 0.33 percent of the net price (Minnesota Statutes 287.21), which on a $397,100 sale comes to about $1,310. Transfer deeds also need a $54 well certificate or a signed well statement. Most county parcels are abstract property, so a title company searches the records before closing. Tax statements and valuation notices appear in the county's Property Information Search, and Property Taxation and Records takes questions at 651-438-4597.

Before you sign, Minnesota Statutes 513.55 has you hand the buyer a written disclosure of the material facts you know.

What are the Dakota County tax dates for an Eagan house?

Dakota County bills real property in halves due May 15 and October 15. The October 2026 date has gone by, and the next deadline is May 15, 2027.

Online payment runs through Paymentus, with a 2.29 percent card fee, a $2.95 Visa debit fee or a $0.35 bank transfer fee, and the phone line is 1-844-797-9075. Walk-in payment is possible at the Hastings, West St. Paul and Apple Valley buildings until 4:30 p.m. on weekdays. A mailed payment needs a postmark on or before the due date. Free automatic payment is open to owners who do not pay through a mortgage company.

Dakota County lists December 31, 2026 as the homestead application deadline, which matters to a buyer who will live in the house. Your closing agent can walk through how the year's tax is prorated.

Which way of selling suits an Eagan house?

An agent listing, a sale by owner and a direct cash purchase are the usual paths. The fit depends on the house, the timeline and whether renters live there.

A listing reaches the broadest set of buyers and suits a house in decent condition with time for showings. A cash purchase can suit a rental owner facing a new license cycle, an owner moving on a short timeline, or a house still carrying decades-old finishes. Ask each buyer for a written price and closing date, pull your permit history and any special assessment record, and compare the net amount each offer leaves you.

More questions about Eagan, MN

Will the buyer of my Eagan rental house inherit its license?

No. Licenses run for one year and cannot be transferred, so the new owner applies for a fresh rental license. Community Development, at 651-675-5681, can walk through the steps.

Which office takes a deed for recording in Dakota County?

The Property Taxation and Records office in Hastings. Book an appointment, or send the deed by mail to 1590 Highway 55 with a cover letter, return postage and a phone number.

Is my Eagan house in a flood zone?

Almost certainly not. The city says all properties are in FEMA Flood Zone X except those in Zone AE along the Minnesota River. The maps date from 2011, so confirm an address with Planning or FEMA.

Does swapping out a fence or driveway before a sale need city approval in Eagan?

It needs a zoning permit, which is free. Fences, driveway replacements, patios, sheds up to 200 square feet and retaining walls under four feet are covered. Staff usually reply in two to five business days, and the Zoning Hotline is 651-675-5685.

What is the next Dakota County property tax deadline?

May 15, 2027 is the next first-half date, with the second half following on October 15, 2027. The 2026 second half came due on October 15, 2026.

Burnsville at a glance

Selling in Burnsville?
We buy Burnsville houses as-is, with no commission, no repairs and no closing costs to you.
Get My Cash Offer →

How can you sell a house fast in Burnsville, MN?

The quickest Burnsville sale is usually a direct purchase by an investor or cash buyer, because there is no lender appraisal or buyer financing to wait on. A traditional listing takes longer and brings more money. Selling on your own sits in the middle.

  • List with an agent when the house is in good shape and you can wait through showings and a financed closing.
  • Sell by owner when you want to keep control of price and can handle disclosures and the purchase agreement yourself.
  • Take a cash offer when the house needs work, carries a tenant, or you need a closing date measured in weeks.

Large pockets of Burnsville are ramblers and split-levels from the building boom after Interstate 35W opened, so condition and updates often drive which route pays best.

What is Burnsville like, and how did its housing get built?

Burnsville sits about 15 miles south of downtown Minneapolis in Dakota County, on a bluff above the south bank of the Minnesota River. The city covers roughly 27 square miles, about 25 of them land, and Interstate 35 splits into 35W and 35E inside its borders. Minnesota Highway 13 and County Road 42 are the other main routes.

The area was a Mdewakanton Dakota village site before Irish, Scottish and Norwegian farmers arrived in the 1850s. As late as 1950 the township held only 583 people. Interstate 35W arrived in the 1960s, the township incorporated as a city in 1964, and Burnsville Center opened in 1977 along the County Road 42 retail strip. By the late 1990s the city was nearly built out, and 2000s construction shifted to redevelopment, including four-story residential buildings and the 54-acre Heart of the City downtown with the Ames Center performing arts venue.

That history explains the resale mix. A seller in a 1970s neighborhood competes with newer condos and apartments near the downtown, and buyers can compare them all within a few miles.

What do the Census figures show for Burnsville homeowners?

Burnsville's 2025 population estimate is 65,244, up 1.4% from the 2020 base, and the owner-occupied rate is 64.7%. Median value of an owner-occupied home is $355,200 for 2020-2024, and median gross rent is $1,513.

  • Households: 25,891, at 2.47 people each.
  • Median household income: $87,024, with per capita income of $43,192.
  • Residents 65 and older: 16.9%, the highest share of the four cities in the Census comparison.
  • Bachelor's degree or higher: 39.8% of adults 25 and up.
  • Mean commute: 23.3 minutes.

Burnsville has the lowest owner-occupied rate of the four cities compared, so rentals make up a larger slice of the housing than in Chanhassen or Brooklyn Park.

Which school districts cover Burnsville addresses?

Burnsville Independent School District 191 serves most of the city, but about 20% of Burnsville students attend District 196 schools and about 10% attend District 194 schools, so the address determines the answer.

School districts that enroll Burnsville students
DistrictShare of Burnsville studentsSchools named for Burnsville students
District 191 (Burnsville-Eagan-Savage)MajorityJoseph Nicollet Middle, William Byrne, Sioux Trail, Sky Oaks, Vista View and other elementaries
District 196About 20%Apple Valley High, Valley Middle, Echo Park Elementary
District 194About 10%Lakeville North High, Kenwood Trail Middle, Orchard Lake Elementary

Good Shepherd Lutheran School, a Pre-K to 8 school, is also in Burnsville. District 191 is also the city's largest employer.

Does Burnsville require a rental license when you sell to or become a landlord?

Yes. Burnsville licenses rentals of condominiums, townhouses, single-family homes, manufactured homes and multi-unit buildings, and a license is issued only after an initial inspection. Rental licenses are renewed on a quarterly schedule, with applications due a month before the expiration date.

  • Rental properties are inspected for building and fire code compliance every three years.
  • Landlords must complete a manager training course before the license is issued.
  • A conversion fee applies when an owner-occupied unit becomes a rental, covering the first license year, the initial inspection and one follow-up.
  • Exceptions include relatives renting from the homeowner, military leave with proof of orders, snowbirds, and contract-for-deed sales registered with the Dakota County Assessor.

The city's multi-housing program adds strikes for tenant behavior. Three strikes in 12 months at one residence means the complex must move toward removing the tenants within 14 days. If you sell to an investor, expect these rules to be part of their math. The rental licensing office is at 952-895-4440.

What about short-term rentals and accessory dwelling units?

A homeowner who rents a private home or an accessory dwelling unit through Airbnb or VRBO needs a Burnsville short-term vacation rental license, renewed each year. Adjacent neighbors must be notified as a courtesy, though the city will not deny the permit over an objection, and a monthly lodging tax report is due within 25 days of month's end.

Accessory dwelling units are allowed on residential lots of at least 10,000 square feet, one per lot. They must be at least 300 square feet, hold no more than two bedrooms, stay under half the size of the main house, sit on a permanent foundation, and add one extra off-street parking space. The owner must live on the property at least 185 days a year, and the unit cannot be sold apart from the house. A garage can be converted only if a new garage of at least 440 square feet is built. If the house you sell has an unpermitted backyard unit, raise it with the city's Planning Division at 952-895-4455 before listing.

What permits and records should a Burnsville seller check?

The city's public portal handles permits for roofing, siding, windows and doors, plumbing, mechanical, electrical and solar work, and anyone can search the portal for a property's permit history. You can also call Building Inspections at 952-895-4444. Pulling that history before you list shows whether the water heater, furnace or roof work done over the years was permitted.

Burnsville also has a state-law obligation at the sale: Minnesota Statutes section 103I.235 requires the seller, before signing, to tell the buyer about known wells on the property in writing, or state that none are known. The deed must carry the well statement or a well disclosure certificate, otherwise the county will not record it.

How does recording work with Dakota County?

Dakota County Property Taxation and Records records Burnsville deeds. In-person recording is by appointment at the Administration Center in Hastings, and you can mail documents to 1590 Highway 55, Hastings, MN 55033 with a cover letter, a self-addressed stamped envelope and a phone number. Originals come back in one to two weeks.

Most property in Dakota County is Abstract rather than Torrens, which matters to the title company's search. All transfer deeds need a completed well disclosure certificate with a $54 fee, or one of the two certification statements printed on the deed. Questions go to 651-438-4597 or records@co.dakota.mn.us.

More questions about Burnsville, MN

How soon can a cash sale close in Burnsville?

Burnsville inspects licensed rentals every three years, so a former rental should come with its latest inspection results. For an owner-occupied house, the city's permit history search shows what work was inspected.

Can the buyer rent out the house they buy from me?

Yes, after getting a Burnsville rental license, which requires an initial inspection and manager training. Relatives renting from the homeowner are one of the listed exceptions.

A statement of known material facts that could significantly affect an ordinary buyer's use of the home, plus a statement on any wells. Give it honestly and in good faith.

Coon Rapids at a glance

How is Coon Rapids organized on the map?

Coon Rapids sits north of Minneapolis and ranks second in size among Anoka County cities. Its 22.61 square miles of land lie about 863 feet up, and the 2025 Census estimate counts 64,193 residents.

The Mississippi River runs along the city, and Cenaiko Lake and Crooked Lake lie within the boundaries. Two-thirds of Crooked Lake belongs to Coon Rapids, with the remaining third in Andover. U.S. Highway 10, Minnesota Highway 47 and Minnesota Highway 610 carry most of the traffic, and the BNSF mainline cuts through town. Coon Rapids Boulevard follows the old oxcart route and remains the main commercial corridor. A house a block from those roads draws a different crowd than one on a quiet street near a park, so the address shapes how a sale goes.

How did Coon Rapids grow from an oxcart route to a city of 64,000?

The name comes from Coon Creek, where settlers hunted raccoons in the 1800s. The Red River Ox Cart Trail was laid out in 1835 to link Minneapolis and Anoka, and early industry grew up beside it. One firm was the Anoka Pressed Brick and Terra Cotta Company, started by D. C. Dunham in 1881. Its clay pit, still called the Clay Hole, is a local landmark.

Work on the Coon Rapids Dam began in 1912 and finished in 1914, and the dam marks the northernmost navigable point on the Mississippi. The Hennepin County Park Board bought it in 1969, and it is now part of Coon Rapids Dam Regional Park. The place incorporated as a village in October 1952 and as a city in June 1959.

Growth after that was fast. The count was 14,931 in 1960, 30,505 in 1970, 52,978 in 1990 and 63,599 at the 2020 census. A city that more than tripled between 1960 and 1990 has many houses that are now several decades old, which matters when you think about roofs, windows and mechanical systems before listing.

Which jobs, schools and parks influence Coon Rapids home values?

Health care, schools and manufacturing anchor the local job base. The city's 2014 financial report named these employers among its largest.

  • Mercy Health, part of Allina Health, with 1,860 employees.
  • Independent School District 11, with 1,238.
  • Mary T, Inc., a health care and housing provider, with 1,120.
  • RMS Company, a medical device maker, with 672, followed by Honeywell Aerospace with 600 and Anoka-Ramsey Community College with 403.

Anoka-Hennepin District 11 runs the public schools. Coon Rapids High School is projected at about 1,935 students for 2025-26, and the middle schools are Coon Rapids Middle and Northdale Middle. Seven elementary schools serve the city: Adams, Eisenhower, Hamilton, Hoover, Mississippi, Morris Bye and Sand Creek. Charter options include Paladin Career and Technical High School and Northwest Passage High School.

Bunker Hills Regional Park, with its Bunker Beach water park, and Coon Rapids Dam Regional Park both lie inside the city limits.

How do Coon Rapids ownership figures look?

Three of every four Coon Rapids households own, and the typical owner-occupied home is valued near $306,000. The table shows the headline numbers.

Which Coon Rapids rental and vacancy rules matter when you sell?

Coon Rapids regulates rentals and empty houses more closely than many suburbs, and the rules can affect both your timeline and what a buyer may do with the property.

  • Every rental, single-family homes included, must hold a city license before tenants move in. Processing takes about 4 to 6 weeks and includes a background check for each owner, a training certificate and a passed inspection.
  • Licenses renew every year, and starting in 2026 a late renewal brings a late fee. Inspections run on a 1, 2 or 3 year cycle based on results.
  • City Code 12-904 prohibits Airbnb, Vrbo and other short-term rentals, so a buyer cannot plan on that use.
  • A vacant house needs a vacant property permit. You submit the application with the fee, then call Building Inspections at 763-767-6476 to book a one-hour inspection.

If renters occupy the house, phone the Housing Inspector at 763-767-6575 first. That call tells you where your license and inspection cycle stand.

Which Coon Rapids repairs call for a permit first?

Most of them do. The city lists windows, siding, roofing, electrical and plumbing work, drywall, demolition, framing, additions, garages, driveways, steps and decks as projects that need building permits, and some jobs also require a licensed contractor.

Unpermitted work can draw questions once a buyer's inspector looks at the house. Call the Inspections Division at 763-767-6476 before you hire anyone. If the house needs more work than you want to take on, a sale to a buyer who handles repairs after closing is an alternative, though the price will reflect the work still to do.

What does Anoka County require to record a Coon Rapids deed?

The Anoka County Recorder accepts the deed for filing. State deed tax runs 0.33 percent of net consideration under Minnesota Statutes 287.21, so a $305,800 price carries roughly $1,009.

  • Sales of $3,000 or under pay a flat $1.65.
  • An agricultural conservation fee of $5 applies to transfer documents.
  • When an eCRV applies, its filing number is written on the deed.
  • The deed names the buyer and the address for tax statements.
  • Anoka County will not record a transfer while delinquent tax remains unpaid.
  • Every transfer deed needs a well disclosure certificate with a $54 fee, or the approved well statement printed on the deed.

Most Anoka County property is abstract property, so the county advises a thorough title search before a sale. Recording questions go to 763-323-5400 at the Government Center in Anoka. Statute 513.55 adds a duty to hand the buyer a written list of known material problems before signing.

How is property tax paid when a Coon Rapids house sells?

Anoka County Property Records and Taxation collects the tax, and the county's property access site shows what is owed by parcel number or address. Call 763-323-5400 for the unpaid balance and the next due date. Your closing agent can explain the proration.

If you still owe tax before the sale, the choices are these. Online payment through PayAnokaCounty adds 2.6 percent for cards and Apple or Google Pay, or $3.50 for eCheck. A mailed check counts as on time only with a postmark dated by the due date. Paper checks paid at the Government Center counter, where weekday hours end at 4:30 p.m., carry no fee. The county's free Direct Payment Program pulls the amount from a bank account on the due date.

Which sale route fits a Coon Rapids house?

Three routes exist here: an agent listing, a sale by owner, or an offer from a cash buyer. The best match depends on repairs, the calendar and who lives in the house now.

A listing gives the most buyer exposure and suits a house in solid shape. A direct cash sale trades some price for speed and fewer conditions, which can help with a vacant house, a former rental that needs inspection work, or deferred repairs. Whichever you pick, pull together the rental license status, any open permits, the well disclosure and the tax balance first, since every buyer asks for them.

Is it possible to sell a Coon Rapids house with tenants living in it?

Yes, after you check the rental license. The city requires every rental, including single-family homes, to be licensed and inspected, so call the Housing Inspector at 763-767-6575 to confirm where your license and inspection cycle stand.

Can a Coon Rapids buyer use the house for Airbnb stays?

No. City Code 12-904 bans Airbnb, Vrbo and other short-term rentals in Coon Rapids, so a buyer with that plan cannot count on it.

What is the state deed tax on a Coon Rapids sale?

It is 0.33 percent of net consideration, or $1.65 when the price is $3,000 or less. On a $305,800 sale that is about $1,009. Anoka County adds a $5 conservation fee, and a well disclosure certificate costs $54 unless the approved well statement appears on the deed.

Does fixing up a Coon Rapids house before a sale require a permit?

For most projects, yes. Windows, siding, roofing, electrical, plumbing, drywall, decks, driveways and additions all need building permits. The Inspections Division, at 763-767-6476, can say whether a particular job is covered.

How does the city treat a vacant house in Coon Rapids?

It requires a vacant property permit. Submit the application and fee at City Hall, then call Building Inspections at 763-767-6476 to schedule the one-hour inspection. Property Maintenance at 763-767-6470 takes complaints about empty properties.

What should an Eden Prairie homeowner know before putting the house on the market?

Those boom years built most of the housing. The city had 1,384 people in 1950, 16,263 in 1980 and 39,311 in 1990. Buyers who tour your house are comparing it with many neighbors from that same stretch of construction, which makes condition and updates the deciding factors.

Who is likely to buy a house in Eden Prairie?

Mostly people tied to the area's big employers and its school district. The city's 2024 economic snapshot gives Optum 6,500 jobs, C.H. Robinson 2,500, Starkey 2,117, UNFI 1,600 and the school district 1,285.

The Census numbers for 2020 through 2024 describe the household: 76.1 percent own their home, the middle owner-occupied house is worth $473,900, and the middle household earns $130,489. Typical gross rent of $1,833 a month is a yardstick if you are comparing renting out the house with selling it. Nearly two in three adults hold a four-year degree (64.9 percent).

Buyers at that income level expect a move-in ready house. Tired kitchens, deferred maintenance and work done without permits are the situations where owners turn to a direct purchase instead of a long listing.

Which public schools serve Eden Prairie homes?

Eden Prairie Schools runs six elementary schools for pre-K through grade 5, one of them a Spanish immersion school, a single middle school for grades 6 to 8, and Eden Prairie High School with about 2,600 students. Minnesota open enrollment lets families choose schools outside their home district.

Alternatives include The International School of Minnesota and the Performing Institute of Minnesota Arts High School. Hennepin Technical College has a campus here too. Mention the district in any pitch to a buyer, since attendance is a fixed feature and families search by it.

What written disclosures does Minnesota law ask of an Eden Prairie seller?

Start with Minnesota Statutes 513.55, which has you tell the buyer in good faith about known facts that could significantly affect an ordinary buyer's use and enjoyment, before anyone signs a purchase agreement. Three narrower statutes add their own items.

  • Radon: test results, any mitigation system, the state warning and a Health Department booklet, under Section 144.496.
  • Wells: a statement that you know of none, or a description of each, under Section 103I.235.
  • Sewage: whether the property drains to a permitted facility, under Section 115.55.

Your agent or closing company can supply the standard forms for each.

How do permits affect an Eden Prairie sale?

The city keeps permit files, and a buyer's inspector may ask for them. Eden Prairie says a building permit lapses after 180 days without work or an inspection, an accessory building over 200 square feet needs a permit, and a retaining wall over 4 feet tall needs a permit plus engineering.

Owners who live in their house may do their own work, with permits still required and natural gas work excluded. Minnesota requires builders, remodelers and roofers who work on homes to be state licensed, and the Department of Labor and Industry lets you verify a contractor.

If a finished basement, deck or roof lacks a closed permit, ask the building inspections office what closing it requires. Several permits must be applied for in person at the City Center on weekdays. Beginning January 1, 2027, paying by card adds a 2.95 percent charge, minimum $2.95, and bank transfers (EFT or ACH) skip it.

Does Eden Prairie let me keep the house as a rental?

The city also offers a Housing Rehabilitation Loan Program and a First Time Homebuyer Program. Housing and Community Services, at 952-949-8394, can explain how those programs fit a buyer on your side of a sale.

What happens with taxes and county paperwork after I accept an offer?

Hennepin County bills the property tax in two installments, mid-May and mid-October. A date that lands on a weekend or holiday moves forward a business day. The tax information line is 612-348-3011, and Minnesota Statutes 279.01 sets late penalties.

The city assessor sends valuation and classification notices by mail each March, and an appraiser re-verifies physical details at least once in five years. Do not assume your homestead benefit follows the house. Eden Prairie's FAQ says the buyer applies in their own name after moving in, and under Section 272.115 the assessor drops the old classification the next year unless the buyer qualifies.

A buyer should know the timing: the city says a homestead application must be made by December 31, covering occupancy from January 2 to December 31 of the year. It also notes that Minnesota law gives a full or partial valuation exclusion for homesteads of disabled veterans rated 70 percent or higher by the Department of Veterans Affairs, which can matter to a veteran buyer.

A sale above $3,000 also requires a value certificate for the auditor, and deed tax runs 0.33 percent of net consideration under Section 287.21. At the Census median value, that tax would be about $1,560.

At a median value near $474,000, a few percentage points are large sums, so collect at least two written figures and compare what each leaves you after costs.

How soon could an Eden Prairie sale close?

It depends on the route. A financed purchase moves at the pace of the appraisal and loan approval, while a cash purchase closes on a date set with the title company once ownership is clear. Recording at the county follows either one.

Must I repair my Eden Prairie house first?

No. Minnesota asks you to disclose known material facts, and it does not require repairs. Check for open or lapsed permits, since the city retains them and a buyer's inspector can look them up.

Does the buyer inherit my homestead classification?

No. Eden Prairie's FAQ says homestead is not passed on by the seller. The buyer files a homestead application after buying and moving in, in person at a Hennepin County service center or online.

Which taxes show up at an Eden Prairie closing?

The state deed tax, 0.33 percent of net consideration, travels with the deed, and a value certificate goes to the county. How the year's property tax is prorated depends on your purchase agreement.

Can a tenant-occupied Eden Prairie house be sold?

Yes, provided the rental carries the city's license and yearly inspection. Call 952-949-8373 to check its status before marketing the property, and ask your closing agent how the lease and any deposit transfer.

What should I know before selling a house in Apple Valley, Minnesota?

Apple Valley lies in northwestern Dakota County, so a sale here involves the county's recording and tax offices in Hastings plus a few city rules on signs, parking and rentals. The paperwork looks much the same whichever way you sell.

The city is mature and mostly built out. Growth slowed after 1990 because the city had virtually used up its buildable land, and the Census Bureau's July 2025 estimate of 55,248 residents is 2.0 percent below the 2020 count of 56,374.

Owners of homes that need work, carry unpaid tax or have tenants sometimes ask for cash offers, since the buyer accepts the property as it stands. The Dakota County Community Development Agency also coordinates foreclosure assistance and home rehabilitation programs for Apple Valley, which is worth a call before you decide.

How did Apple Valley grow into the city it is today?

The land was first organized in 1859 as Lebanon Township and stayed farmland for almost a century. In the mid-1950s houses began replacing fields, led by the developer Orrin Thompson. Township voters chose incorporation in 1968, and the city incorporated in 1969, picking the name Apple Valley over Lebanon Valley by 1,376 votes to 757.

Growth came fast and then leveled off, as the table shows.

The downtown and the adjacent residential streets, the original core, sit in a shallow valley, and the land around them rolls by a hundred feet or more. The city covers about 17.6 square miles, and Farquar Lake is in the northeast.

What are Apple Valley's roads, schools and landmarks?

Interstate 35E, Cedar Avenue and County Road 42 are the three main routes. The Red Line, a dedicated bus route, links the city with the Mall of America, and the Minnesota Valley Transit Authority runs weekday commuter buses to downtown Minneapolis and Saint Paul. The Minnesota Zoo is in the city, and the Western Service Center of Dakota County is here too.

Independent School District 196 runs the public schools, including a magnet School of Environmental Studies for eleventh and twelfth graders. Families may also choose a school in another district through Minnesota's open enrollment law. The city holds Freedom Days around July 4 and a Winter Carnival in February, and the school district topped the city's 2016 employer list, ahead of Target, Uponor and Dakota County.

The 2020 census counted 21,464 households and 22,253 housing units, 3.5 percent of them vacant. A quarter of households were one person living alone, the median age was 39.4, and 16.6 percent of residents were 65 or older. Later Census Bureau estimates, covering 2020 to 2024, add this picture of owners and renters:

  • Typical owner-occupied home value: $370,400, with 73.4 percent of homes owner-occupied.
  • Median monthly owner cost with a mortgage: $2,084. Median gross rent: $1,738.
  • Households: 21,627, averaging 2.55 people. Median household income: $97,673.
  • Residents in the same home a year before: 88.4 percent.

Which Apple Valley rules should a seller know?

Short term rentals of fewer than 30 days are not allowed in Apple Valley. A council ordinance on June 8, 2023 clarified that they have never been a permitted use, so a house marketed to investors as an Airbnb or Vrbo property will not work as advertised. Owners of any residential rental property must register it with the city.

Yard and curb rules also come up during showings and open houses:

  • One for-sale sign per frontage, two on a corner lot, kept inside the property line and off the right of way, which usually reaches 13 feet behind the curb.
  • Open house signs may stand on city right of way within six blocks of the house, only on the day and during the hours of the open house.
  • Grass and weeds taller than eight inches are a public nuisance.
  • No more than four vehicles per home may be parked or stored outside, and all parking areas must be paved with concrete, asphalt or pavers.
  • Lawn watering is barred from 11 a.m. to 6 p.m. between May 1 and September 30, and public sidewalks must be cleared within 48 hours after a snowfall ends.

Trash containers go to the curb no earlier than 6 p.m. the night before pickup and come back by 10 p.m. on collection day. A garage sale may run three consecutive days, three times a year. Sheds of 200 square feet or less need no building permit, and fences over seven feet do. Code Enforcement at 952-953-2570 answers questions, and the Planning Department at 952-953-2575 handles setbacks.

What does recording a deed in Dakota County involve?

The county recorder's work sits inside Dakota County Property Taxation and Records, which holds the deeds, mortgages and liens for every parcel. Walk-in recording happens at the Administration Center, 1590 Highway 55 in Hastings, and requires an appointment. Mailed packets need the fees, a cover letter, a return envelope with postage and a phone number.

Land in Minnesota is recorded under two systems. With Abstract property, a title company searches the chain of documents. Torrens property instead carries a single certificate of title, close to final proof of who owns it. Abstract is the norm in Dakota County.

Wells matter at the recorder's counter. A transfer deed, a deed ending a contract for deed included, must come with a well disclosure certificate and a $54 fee unless the deed itself carries a statement. The statement can say the seller is unaware of any wells, or that the wells' number and status are unchanged from the last certificate on file. Staff do not assist with legal forms, so let the title company or an attorney prepare the paperwork.

How do I pay Dakota County property tax from Apple Valley?

Dakota County sets real property tax for May 15 and October 15 and says the owner answers for timely payment, whatever method is used. Manufactured homes follow August 31 and November 16, and farm second halves land on November 16.

Single online payments run through Paymentus. Fees are 2.29 percent on Discover, MasterCard or Visa, $2.95 on the Visa Debit Program and $0.35 on a bank transfer, with a $100,000 ceiling per transaction, and you are done only when an emailed receipt shows up. Alternatives include the phone line at 1-844-797-9075, a mailed check to 1590 Highway 55, Hastings, MN 55033-2343 postmarked by the deadline, or a weekday visit to the Western Service Center in Apple Valley, where a card costs 2.49 percent. The Hastings and West St. Paul offices also accept payments.

Free automatic withdrawals are open to owners without a mortgage-company escrow and without overdue tax; cancellations need 15 days' notice before a due date. Statement and payoff questions go to 651-438-4576 or taxation@co.dakota.mn.us.

More questions about Apple Valley, MN

Can I run an Airbnb in Apple Valley, MN?

No. Rentals under 30 days are barred, and the council's June 8, 2023 ordinance says they were never allowed. Longer-term rentals must be registered with the city.

Where is a deed recorded for an Apple Valley house?

Property Taxation and Records at the Dakota County Administration Center, 1590 Highway 55, Hastings. Appointments are available online, and mail recording is accepted.

What is a well disclosure certificate in Dakota County?

A filing that goes with each transfer deed for $54. A statement on the deed about unknown or unchanged wells can stand in for it.

How many cars can I park outside an Apple Valley home?

No more than four vehicles per dwelling unit, on a paved surface. An annual on-site parking permit allows two more, and the Planning Department at 952-953-2575 takes applications.

Which school district serves Apple Valley?

Independent School District 196. Some families opt into other districts under Minnesota's open enrollment statute.

Edina began as a farming and milling settlement along Minnehaha Creek in the 1860s, and its residents organized a village in 1888. It grew as a streetcar suburb, then expanded sharply as a car-oriented suburb in the 1950s and 1960s.

Which school district do Edina buyers ask about?

Edina Public Schools, district 273, enrolls roughly 8,500 students. The district has one high school, Edina High School, two middle schools (South View and Valley View) and six elementary schools: Concord, Creek Valley, Cornelia, Highlands, Countryside and Normandale.

Because the district is a main reason families look at Edina, an elementary attendance area is worth stating plainly when you describe your house. Private options include Our Lady of Grace Catholic School and Golden Years Montessori.

What do buyers see around an Edina house besides the house itself?

Edina's park department oversees 44 parks across more than 1,550 acres of parkland and open space, and the Braemar Ice Rink is part of the hockey culture. Wikipedia notes that ESPN named Edina the center of the American ice hockey universe in 2020, which explains why rink access comes up in conversations with buyers.

Commuters look at transit. Metro Transit runs daytime buses along France Avenue, and the Southdale Transit Center is one of the main hubs in the southwest metro. The city's own homepage also links to the Minnesota Department of Transportation page for the Interstate 494 Edina and Richfield project, so check it for construction that may affect a street near you.

Mean travel time to work is 20.4 minutes for Edina workers, per the Census Bureau, and 72.7 percent of adults 25 and over hold a bachelor's degree or higher. Both facts help you describe a typical Edina buyer to your agent or to a cash buyer evaluating your house.

What must I tell an Edina buyer in writing?

Minnesota's seller disclosure law, Section 513.55, applies to Edina sales. You must disclose known material facts in good faith before signing the purchase agreement. Three topics have their own statutes.

  • Radon test history and mitigation, plus the state warning, under Section 144.496.
  • Wells, or a statement that you know of none, under Section 103I.235.
  • Whether sewage goes to a permitted treatment facility, under Section 115.55.

If you have radon test reports, mitigation receipts or well records, attach them to the disclosure so the buyer sees the same documents you do.

Can I turn my Edina house into a rental or an Airbnb?

As a long-term rental, yes, with a license. As a short-term rental, no. The city's Planning Division says VRBO and Airbnb are not allowed in Edina, and a single-family house that is not owner-occupied may be occupied by a tenant only for 30 consecutive days or more.

The rental program requires an annual license for any dwelling that is not owner-occupied. The posted fees are $206 for a single unit such as a house, townhome or condo, $412 for a duplex with both sides rented, and $206 plus $17 per unit for apartments. Single-family and condo rentals are inspected every other year. Edina Public Health handles licenses at 952-826-0370.

If the license fee, inspections and the 30-day minimum make the rental route unattractive, that is a common reason owners compare a sale against holding the property.

What city paperwork can a seller ask Edina for?

Two items are useful before closing. A zoning letter confirms how a property is zoned and costs $175 per address, requested through the Planning line at 952-826-0369. The city also keeps surveys in its Building Inspections Division, and it publishes an interactive zoning map you can search by address.

If a buyer asks about boundary markers, the city explains that corner irons can be moved during utility or street work, and that fences, hedges and sidewalk edges are not reliable indicators of lot lines. Call Gopher State One Call at 651-252-1166 before anyone digs to locate the iron.

How do Hennepin County taxes and transfer costs work for an Edina sale?

Hennepin County bills Edina property tax, due May 15 and October 15, or the next business day when either date lands on a weekend or holiday. Hennepin's tax staff can be reached at 612-348-3011. Penalties for late payment come from Minnesota Statutes 279.01.

When the deed is recorded, Minnesota's deed tax is 0.33 percent of net consideration under Section 287.21. For a sale above $3,000 a Certificate of Real Estate Value goes to the county auditor under Section 272.115, and the assessor removes the seller's homestead classification for the following year unless the buyer qualifies for it.

At the Census median value of $646,300, 0.33 percent works out to roughly $2,100, so ask your title company for the exact figure early.

What are the realistic ways to sell in Edina?

  • Traditional listing: suited to a house in good order. Expect to prepare it, show it and wait for a buyer's financing.
  • For sale by owner: you set the price and handle the contract and disclosures yourself.
  • Cash sale as is: useful for an estate, a tenant-occupied house, or a home needing work the owner does not want to fund.

Whichever you choose, request written numbers and compare what you net after fees, repairs and carrying costs.

More questions about Edina, MN

Is Edina a good place to sell quickly?

Edina's median home value is $646,300 and the city is more than 95 percent developed. A house with deferred repairs, an estate sale or a tenant in place often moves faster through a direct cash purchase than through a repaired and staged listing.

Can I use my Edina house as a short-term rental while I sell?

No. The city's Planning Division says short-term rentals like VRBO and Airbnb are not allowed in Edina. A non-owner-occupied house can be rented, but only for stays of at least 30 consecutive days and with the annual rental license.

How much does an Edina rental license cost?

A single unit costs $206 per year and a duplex with both sides rented costs $412, according to the city. Apartments cost $206 plus $17 per unit. The city bills separately after it processes your application.

Do I owe deed tax when I sell my Edina house?

Minnesota imposes the deed tax when the deed is presented for recording, at 0.33 percent of net consideration. Who pays it is set by your purchase agreement, so confirm with your title company before you sign.

Who do I call about Edina property taxes?

Call Hennepin County's property tax team at 612-348-3011. Taxes are due May 15 and October 15. Your closing statement will show how the current year's tax is split between you and the buyer.

What is the quickest way to move a Minnetonka house?

Minnetonka sellers choose among three routes: an agent listing, a sale handled alone, or a purchase by a company that pays cash for the house in its present condition. Cash tends to suit a house that needs work, carries tenants, or faces a closing date that will not move.

Every route runs through the same paperwork. The parcel sits in Hennepin County, which bills the tax and records the deed. Minnetonka also keeps its own assessor, so a value question goes to city hall instead of the county offices downtown.

What shapes Minnetonka as a place to own a house?

Minnetonka lies roughly 10 miles west of Minneapolis and holds the eastern tip of Lake Minnetonka. The lake drains through Minnehaha Creek, and that creek is where the city began: a sawmill claim staked in 1852 grew into the settlement of Minnetonka Mills. Horse pasture and farms survived into the 1960s, and the township filled in as a residential suburb afterward. The city incorporated in 1956. Its 28.22 square miles include 1.29 square miles of water, and the Census Bureau puts density at 1,998 residents per square mile. Two older buildings, the 1906 Town Hall and the Burwell House on Minnetonka Boulevard, are on the National Register of Historic Places.

Three school districts cover it. Hopkins takes the central and eastern part, Minnetonka takes the west, and Wayzata reaches along the northern boundary. Minnesota's open enrollment law lets families attend elsewhere. Put the district in your listing description, since the answer shifts from one street to the next.

Employment is anchored by large headquarters. Cargill and UnitedHealth Group are both based here, along with Carlson and Radisson Hotel Group. I-494 runs through town, while I-394 and US 169 trace the northern and eastern edges.

What do the Census numbers show for Minnetonka homes?

Most Minnetonka households own, and values run high. The table lists the figures a seller usually wants beside an asking price.

That leaves about 28 percent of homes as rentals. The Bureau counts 23,515 households averaging 2.24 people, 22.8 percent of residents at 65 or older, and 88.2 percent who stayed in the same house over the previous year. Most of the city's residents stay put from year to year.

Which Minnetonka rental rules matter to a seller or a buyer?

Minnetonka requires registration for every rental property, however short the stay. The ordinance was adopted on December 18, 2023 and took effect on February 3, 2024. Each certificate lapses one year after submission, and renewal notices arrive by email.

  • Condo and townhome owners name the unit being rented.
  • Single-family houses, duplexes and triplexes need one application per unit.
  • The designated property manager must be able to respond in person when something goes wrong.

On June 8, 2026 the council adopted a short-term rental ordinance. Stays under 30 days now require both a registration and a homestead, so only an occupant who treats the home as a primary residence may rent all or part of it. An investor reading your listing will weigh that limit. Request the ordinance text from the city before telling anyone that a short-term use is permitted.

What does Minnesota require a Minnetonka seller to put in writing?

Before an agreement is signed, a seller of residential property must hand the buyer a written statement under Minnesota Statutes section 513.55. The statement lists every material fact you know of that could adversely and significantly affect an ordinary buyer's use and enjoyment. It has to be made in good faith and reflect the best of your knowledge. The buyer's licensee may receive it and pass a copy along.

A few records make the form easier to complete.

  • Older building permits, which sit in the city's records archive.
  • The location of property stakes and buried utility lines, which residents can trace with a metal detector borrowed from the city.
  • Anything you know about water, drainage or foundation trouble near the creek or the lake shore.

New permit applications, payments and plan reviews all happen online. Phone 952-939-8394 to learn how long a review is running before an open permit delays your closing.

How do Hennepin County taxes play into a Minnetonka sale?

Property taxes in Hennepin County fall due on May 15 and October 15, shifting to the following business day when either lands on a weekend or holiday. October 2026 is behind us. The next first-half date, May 15, 2027, is a Saturday, so the payment moves to Monday, May 17.

Minnetonka is among the cities that run their own valuation notices, so questions about your value or classification go to the city assessor at 952-939-8220. The county fixes values as of January 2 and mails notices in March. April and May are the window for informal talks. A formal appeal starts at the local board. After that comes the county board of appeal and equalization in mid-June. Minnesota Tax Court is the other formal option.

  • E-check payments online carry no fee. Cards, PayPal and Venmo add a service charge.
  • A mailed check must carry a postmark dated on or before the due day.
  • Counter payments are taken on the 6th floor of the Government Center, 300 South 6th Street, on weekdays. A drop box on that floor accepts checks through the early evening.
  • Lender escrow folds the taxes into the mortgage payment, so a new owner may never see the bill.

Three notices arrive each year. The valuation notice comes in March, the proposed levies notice in November, and the tax statement in March with payment stubs. The November estimate leaves out special assessments that may be added to the final bill, and it gives the dates of the truth-in-taxation meetings where residents can comment on budgets.

The county can wipe out a late-payment penalty once per ten years, for current-year taxes only. The application deadline is June 30 for a first-half payment and November 30 for a second-half payment, and the full tax must already be paid.

What should a Minnetonka owner ask before taking a cash offer?

Get the proposal on paper, showing the closing date, the check amount, and who covers each closing line. A company buying in present condition should say whether it plans any repairs, and you should be equally direct about what you know of the house.

  • Is the offer contingent on an inspection or on financing?
  • Who orders the title search, and who pays recording charges?
  • If tenants live there, what becomes of their lease?
  • May you stay a couple of weeks after closing to finish moving?

A quick sale still needs the disclosure statement, a deed and a trip to the county recorder. What it removes is months of showings. Compare the cash figure with your likely net from a listing, after repairs, commissions and months of mortgage, insurance and utilities. Then pick the route that matches your calendar.

More questions about Minnetonka, MN

Does a Minnetonka landlord need to keep the registration active during a sale?

Yes, for as long as the house is rented. The city registers every rental regardless of length, and a certificate lasts one year. Renew before the expiration printed on it.

Who decides what my Minnetonka house is worth for tax purposes?

The city assessor, reachable at 952-939-8220, and not the county office. Hennepin County still collects the money and holds the county appeal board in mid-June.

When does the next Hennepin County tax payment come due?

May 15, 2027 is the next first-half date. It lands on a Saturday, so the payment moves to Monday, May 17. The second half follows on October 15.

Could my buyer operate a short-term rental in the house?

Only as an owner living there. The June 8, 2026 ordinance requires a homestead and a city registration for any stay under 30 days.

Can a late tax penalty be removed in Hennepin County?

Sometimes. The county allows one abatement every ten years, for current-year taxes. The second-half deadline is November 30, and the tax has to be paid in full first, with no unpaid balance from earlier years.

What is different about selling a house in St. Louis Park?

St. Louis Park requires a city housing inspection whenever a property is sold or ownership is transferred. That step comes before closing, so it shapes how fast any sale can go, whether you list the house or take a cash offer.

The city is a first-ring suburb immediately west of Minneapolis, bordered by Edina, Golden Valley, Minnetonka, Plymouth and Hopkins. The Census Bureau estimates 50,027 residents for July 2025, nearly the same as the 50,010 counted in the 2020 census. Interstate 394, U.S. Highway 169 and State Highways 7 and 100 run through it, and the public schools belong to Independent School District 283.

  • Listing: the inspection is arranged by the seller, and corrections are usually made before the closing.
  • Direct sale: the same inspection applies, so book it early.
  • Cash offer: a buyer can take the house with open corrections through the city's escrow option, described below.

How does the St. Louis Park sale inspection work?

A city inspector visits for about 45 to 60 minutes to check that the siding, roof, garage and interior meet the city's property maintenance code. Appointments are usually available within one to three days.

The fee covers the first inspection and any follow-ups: $360 for a single-family house or townhouse, $460 for a duplex and $250 for a condominium. With no violations, the city issues a property maintenance certificate. It lasts one year for a house, townhouse or duplex and two years for a condo (City of St. Louis Park).

If violations turn up, the city issues a correction notice. In most cases repairs must meet the code in force when the building was built, and remodeled areas follow the code from the year of the remodel. Smoke detectors are the exception and are required in every building.

  • Seller repairs: the usual path, followed by a return visit to verify the work.
  • Temporary certificate: a buyer may take a temporary property maintenance certificate by signing an escrow agreement and finishing the work within 90 days of closing.
  • Cost and timing: the escrow agreement costs $155, must be prepared 48 hours before closing, and needs enough money held in escrow to cover the listed work.

What happened to St. Louis Park's housing stock?

Most houses here date from one building boom. St. Louis Park grew from 7,737 people in 1940 to 22,644 in 1950 and 43,310 in 1960, and about 60 percent of its homes went up between the late 1940s and early 1950s. Between 1950 and 1956 alone, 66 new subdivisions were recorded for 2,700 homes (Wikipedia).

The settlement was named for the Minneapolis and St. Louis Railway, with Park added to avoid confusion with St. Louis, Missouri. It incorporated as a village in 1886, and voters adopted a home rule charter in 1954 that made it a city with a hired manager. The Peavey-Haglin elevator from 1899 still stands as the world's first concrete tubular grain elevator.

That history matters to a seller because the inspector reads each house against the code in place when it was built. Roofs, siding, garages and interiors are the four areas the city names, so walk those first.

  • Before the visit: the city publishes a list of commonly noted property maintenance deficiencies as a PDF.
  • Permits: all open permits must be closed before an escrow agreement can be approved.
  • Questions: the city's escrow line is 952.924.2588.

Hennepin County bills property tax in two halves, due May 15 and October 15, or the next business day when either falls on a weekend or holiday. Late payments carry penalties that grow each month, and a late payment is applied to penalty first and then to tax.

St. Louis Park runs its own assessing office, so valuation notices come from the city rather than the county. You can reach it at 952-924-2535. Notices go out in March, informal discussion happens in April and May, and the county board of appeal and equalization meets in mid-June (Hennepin County Assessment).

Payment is flexible. Hennepin accepts e-checks online with no fee, up to $50,000 per transaction, and card, PayPal or Venmo payments with a service fee. Many owners instead pay through a mortgage escrow account, in which case the lender receives the payment information, so ask the servicer for the payoff before closing.

  • Penalty abatement: an owner may ask once every ten years, with applications due June 30 for the first half and November 30 for the second.

How long is the St. Louis Park property maintenance certificate good for?

It lasts one year for single-family homes, townhomes and duplexes, and two years for condominiums. It is issued once an inspector finds no code violations or confirms repairs are complete.

Can the buyer finish the repairs after closing in St. Louis Park?

Yes, through a temporary property maintenance certificate. The buyer signs an escrow agreement, funds the cost of the work, pays a $155 fee, and completes everything within 90 days of closing. Call 952.924.2588 with questions.

When are Hennepin County property taxes due for a St. Louis Park house?

They are due May 15 and October 15. When either date falls on a weekend or holiday, the due date moves to the next business day.

The city's own assessing office handles valuation notices, and its number is 952-924-2535. Hennepin County handles tax billing and collection, so keep both offices in your contact list. How can you sell a house fast in Shakopee, Minnesota?

Three routes exist here: hire an agent, handle a private sale, or take cash from a buyer who skips the lender. Speed depends on the house, the title, and how quickly the Scott County paperwork can be gathered.

The Census Bureau counted 43,698 people in Shakopee in April 2020 and estimates 49,366 for July 2025, a gain of about 5,700 people in five years. A house that needs a new roof, a tenant move-out, or an estate clean-out still sells here, but each of those problems changes which route makes sense.

What should a seller know about Shakopee itself?

Shakopee serves as seat of Scott County, set on the south bank bend of the Minnesota River southwest of Minneapolis. Thomas Holmes platted Shakopee Village in 1854 and named it after Chief Shakopee II. The city first incorporated in 1857, gave up its charter in 1861, and incorporated again in 1870 (Wikipedia).

For most of the twentieth century it was a small river town. Growth took off after U.S. Highway 169 was realigned in 1996 toward the Bloomington Ferry Bridge, and the population went from 20,568 in 2000 to 37,076 in 2010. County Highway 101 runs east and west through the historic downtown, while Highway 169 and State Highway 13 tie the city to the rest of the metro.

  • Public schools: Shakopee Public Schools, Independent School District 720, with Shakopee High School and two middle schools.
