Do Shakopee rules affect a rental house you want to sell?

Yes. The city requires every rental property, including a single-family home, to be registered, and the registration runs through the Shakopee ePortal. A house with a tenant in it carries that history into the sale.

The city's R-HOME program asks owners to finish Phase I landlord training within a year of receiving a rental certificate, and properties with four or more units must complete Phases I, II and III. Background checks on prospective tenants must be done before a tenant occupies the unit. A buyer who plans to keep the tenant will ask whether the certificate and training are current.

  • Registration: file it online through the city ePortal.
  • Training: the Phase I certificate is accepted by other cities, and the city usually hosts a session in spring.
  • Fair housing: the City Council approved a Fair Housing Policy in May 2019, and complaints go to the Minnesota Department of Human Rights, since the city does not take them in.

Questions about fair housing duties during a sale can go to the city's Department of Planning and Development at 952-233-9300. For a rented house, ask the buyer early whether they want the tenant to stay, because that decides whether you need a move-out date written into the contract.

How does Scott County value and tax a Shakopee house?

Scott County's assessor sets the value, and the tax bill follows from it. State law makes the assessor physically review 20 percent of all property each year, so your neighborhood is visited about once every five years. Value notices are mailed in or around March.

You may decline an interior inspection. The assessor then estimates the interior, and the local board of review cannot lower your value until you allow the inspection. Value can rise or fall by any amount, since the old 15 percent limit program ended with taxes payable in 2010 (Scott County Property and Taxation Services).

  • First half: due May 15, with payment by mail, drop box, online, or at the Government Center at 200 4th Avenue West in Shakopee.
  • Second half: due October 15.
  • Homestead and veteran relief: Scott County takes residential homestead applications and helps eligible honorably discharged veterans with service-connected disabilities claim the state's market value exclusion, so check whether a relief program is attached to the parcel you are selling.
  • Appeals: the county says you have until April 30 of the year the taxes are due to file with the Minnesota Tax Court.
  • Mailing: the Postal Service now postmarks the date mail is first processed, so the county suggests asking for a manual postmark or paying online.

What should you check before closing a Shakopee sale?

Start with the county's property information site, which shows the legal description, tax detail, valuation, recorded documents and the certificate of real estate value for a parcel. Searching by address works best with the house number and the first few letters of the street name.

The information refreshes weekly, so call Property and Taxation Services at 952-496-8115 for a current payoff figure, especially if the parcel is under a confession of judgment contract for past-due years.

  • Confirm the owner on record matches the person signing the deed.
  • Ask the county for the balance of both halves, including any special assessments.
  • If the house was a rental, gather the registration and training certificate.
  • If an heir is selling, ask the county recorder what must be on file before the deed can be recorded.

A closing agent normally orders these searches, but a seller who has them ready avoids delay. If the sale is a quick cash purchase, the same items let the buyer's title company move straight to a closing date.

More questions about Shakopee, MN

Is a cash offer faster than listing a house in Shakopee?

It can be, because there is no buyer loan or lender appraisal to wait on. Closing time still depends on title work, so a clean title closes sooner than one with liens or an open estate.

Do I have to let the Scott County assessor inside my house?

No. You can decline an interior inspection, and the assessor will estimate the interior. The catch is that the local board of review cannot change your value in your favor until you allow the inspection.

When are Shakopee property taxes due?

The first half is due May 15 and the second half October 15. Scott County also notes that mail postmarks now show the day USPS first processes the item, so pay online or request a manual postmark near a deadline.

Does Shakopee require rental registration when I sell a rented house?

Rental registration is required for any rental in the city, single-family homes included, and it is filed through the ePortal. Owners also complete R-HOME Phase I training within a year of receiving a certificate, so have those records ready for a buyer.

Where do I find out what I still owe on a Shakopee parcel?

Use the Scott County property information search, then call Property and Taxation Services at 952-496-8115 for a current figure. The online data updates weekly, so a phone check before closing is worth the few minutes.

Selling in Moorhead?

How does a Moorhead owner sell a house on a short timeline?

An owner who needs to move quickly can hire an agent, market the house without one, or sell to a buyer paying cash who takes it as is. Cash works best when the house has deferred repairs, a tenant in place, or a move date set by a job or a family change.

All three paths end at the Clay County Recorder, and a rental has one extra step at city hall. The notes below cover the Moorhead and Clay County rules that most often decide how quickly a closing can happen.

What is Moorhead like as a place to own a house?

Moorhead is the Clay County seat, on the Red River of the North, directly across from Fargo, North Dakota. It sits on the bed of glacial Lake Agassiz, which drained roughly 10,000 years ago and left some of the flattest farmland in the world. The city was platted in 1871 and named for a Northern Pacific Railway official. Winters are cold, and an average year brings about 53 inches of snow.

The economy mixes agriculture, manufacturing and education. American Crystal Sugar keeps its corporate headquarters and a beet processing plant here, and Busch Agricultural Resources and Pactiv have operations too. Concordia College, Minnesota State University Moorhead, Minnesota State Community and Technical College and Rasmussen University give the city four colleges and universities, with a combined enrollment of roughly 14,000 students.

Getting around is straightforward. Interstate 94 and U.S. Highways 10 and 75 cross the city, and MATBUS runs local routes. Intercity buses, trains and flights leave from the Fargo side of the river.

How expensive is it to own or rent in Moorhead?

Moorhead has added residents quickly since 2020, and renters occupy a large share of its homes. The Census Bureau figures below put numbers on both.

Moorhead snapshot, with figures drawn from QuickFacts (five-year 2020-2024 data except population)
ItemValue
Population, July 1, 202546,533 (up 4.6% from April 2020)
Owner-occupied homes58.1%
Middle home value among owners$249,000
Middle monthly cost for owners with a loan$1,807
Middle gross rent$1,033
Middle household income$72,761

Renters occupy 41.9 percent of homes, and about 80 percent of residents had not moved in the past year. Because so many homes are rentals, the city's rental rules come up in a good share of sales.

Does a Moorhead house need a rental registration before it sells?

If anyone but you or a relative lives in the house, yes. Moorhead requires owners to register single-family homes, multiplexes, condos, mobile homes and rooming arrangements, and it also covers an owner-occupied house with a room rented to an unrelated person. A house where your child's own family lives does not need it if you live elsewhere. Accepting anything in exchange for housing, even groceries or maintenance work, counts as rent.

  • Registration renews every year, with the renewal due December 31.
  • Inspections are done annually, though a high scorer may self-inspect the next year.
  • A new owner must call Neighborhood Services at 218-299-5434 and file the application before taking possession.
  • The city will not register a unit unless the owner is current on property taxes and other obligations to the city.

A buyer who wants to convert a single-family house into a rental can pay $100 for a pre-purchase inspection. If the house is currently a rental, tell your buyer up front so the registration and renewal fee are settled before the closing date.

How does Moorhead set a home's taxable value, and what changes at sale?

The city assessor sets market value as of January 2 each year, and Clay County collects the taxes. The assessor is required to view every property at least once every five years, and a building permit can trigger a visit.

Homestead status lowers the taxable value for an owner who lives in the house. Under the city's formula the exclusion is 40 percent of the first $95,000 of value, or $38,000 at most, and it shrinks by 9 percent of the value above $95,000. At the $249,000 Census median that works out to a $24,140 exclusion and a taxable value of $224,860. A buyer applies in their own name, and the city's calendar sets December 31 as the deadline to occupy the home and file for the next assessment year.

  • Valuation notices come with the tax statement in late March or early April.
  • The local board of appeal and equalization hears formal appeals in mid-April, on the date printed on the notice.
  • The county board meets in mid-June, and you must have appealed locally first.
  • Most real estate pays half of its tax on May 15 and the rest on October 15.

Call the assessor's office at 218-299-5310 with questions about a specific parcel.

What does the Clay County Recorder need to record a Moorhead deed?

The Recorder's office, at the Government Center on 12th Avenue South in Moorhead, publishes a checklist for deeds. Missing one item can send a package back. When several documents share a single check and any one is not in recordable form, the office returns all of them unrecorded and does not issue refunds.

  • The recording fee, which is $46, and the title of the document on the first page.
  • A Certificate of Real Estate Value filed online when the price is over $3,000, with a $54 well certificate that goes with it.
  • The state deed tax, a complete legal description rather than the shortened version on a tax statement, and a tax statement mailing address.
  • A drafted-by statement and a full acknowledgment, with the notary's seal, signature and commission expiration.
  • Delinquent real estate taxes paid first, through the County Auditor at 218-299-5006.
  • A septic certificate for rural residential property, which does not delay recording.

Records can be viewed at 3510 12th Avenue South on weekdays from 8 a.m. to 4:30 p.m., and the land records site is searchable around the clock. Write one check to Clay County for the fees and deed tax, and use a separate check for any delinquent taxes. Splitting a tax parcel requires current taxes in full and may need a survey. The Recorder cannot give legal advice or pick a form for you.

What should a Moorhead seller check before closing on a cash offer?

Ask when the buyer wants possession, then confirm each of these points in writing.

  • Who pays the rental registration renewal if a rental closes late in the year.
  • Who handles the well and septic paperwork, if the property has either.
  • How the buyer will treat the tenant's current lease and deposit.
  • The date money reaches you, and how any delinquent tax or special assessment is paid out of the proceeds.

You can check special assessment history and permit records on the city's property information site, which also lists sales history and valuations. Print what it shows before you talk numbers with a buyer.

More questions about Moorhead, MN

Does a family member living in my Moorhead house make it a registered rental?

No, not when the owner lives elsewhere and the occupants are related to the owner. Registration is required when unrelated people live there, including college roommates, or when you take anything in exchange for housing.

Where do I take a question about my Moorhead assessed value?

The Moorhead Assessor's Office at 218-299-5310. The city only keeps values for parcels inside city limits, so a property outside the limits goes to the Clay County Assessor.

What will Clay County charge when my deed is recorded?

The recording fee is $46, plus the state deed tax of 0.33 percent of the price when it exceeds $3,000. A $54 well certificate is also due when a Certificate of Real Estate Value is required.

What is the cutoff for homestead status on a Moorhead house?

December 31 is the deadline to occupy the home and file the application for the current assessment year. Taxes on that assessment are payable the following year, and a new buyer applies in their own name.

Can I skip the local board and appeal straight to the Clay County board?

No. You must first appeal to the local board in April to earn the right to go to the county board in June. Call the assessor early, because many questions are settled with comparable sales or corrected property details.

Selling in Mankato?

Which sale route moves fastest in Mankato?

You can go with an agent, handle the sale yourself, or accept a cash offer, and the best fit usually follows from what the house is: a rental, a student-area property or a family home. The city is the seat of Blue Earth County, where the 2025 estimate of 46,529 people sits 4.4% above the 2020 base.

Owners live in half of Mankato's homes, and a typical renter pays $1,132 a month. With that split, many Mankato houses are rented, and buyers range from first-time owners to people who plan to rent the house out. A seller with a worn rental or a vacant house may find that a buyer paying cash can close sooner than one who needs a mortgage and an appraisal.

  • Agent: the most buyers see it, and the timeline is the longest.
  • Investor purchase: few showings, and you can name the closing date.
  • Owner sale: you manage the buyer, the disclosure and the paperwork.

Which county will tax and record your Mankato house?

Mankato lies in three counties. The city extends into Blue Earth, Nicollet and Le Sueur counties, and it serves as the Blue Earth County seat. Most addresses fall in Blue Earth, but your tax statement and deed record name the county that applies to your parcel, so read them first.

Recording matters here. Minnesota Statutes 507.34 says an unrecorded deed loses to a later good-faith buyer whose deed reaches the recorder first, so closing agents file right away.

The state deed tax under section 287.21 works out to 0.33% of net consideration on any price over $3,000, collected as the deed goes to the recorder.

What do Mankato housing numbers show?

Mankato has a short commute and a lower price point than the Twin Cities. Figures for 2020-2024 put the typical owner-occupied home at $261,700 and the average drive to work at 13.9 minutes.

Mankato, 2020-2024 housing and income figures from Census Bureau QuickFacts
MeasureMankato
Typical home value (owner-occupied)$261,700
Share of homes lived in by owners50.0%
Median gross rent$1,132
Monthly owner cost, mortgaged homes$1,624
Households18,075
Persons in poverty20.6%

The 2020 census recorded 18,855 housing units in Mankato, 6.8% of them vacant, and a median age of 27.7, and 34.4% of households were made up of one person. Minnesota State University, Mankato is the second-largest university in the state by enrollment, so student demand shapes parts of the market. Of the 17,576 households counted in 2020, 23.5% included children under 18, 32.9% were married-couple households and 10.8% were a person 65 or older living alone.

What rental rules affect a Mankato house?

Mankato ties rental licenses to zoning, which matters if your house has been or could be a rental. The city's rental zoning page says low-density districts R-1 and R-2 limit occupancy to two unrelated people or a family, while R-3, R-4 and office-residential districts allow five unrelated people or a family.

  • Parking: two off-street stalls per unit in R-1 and R-2, paved with asphalt or concrete, each at least 8 by 18 feet.
  • Units: R-2 can license up to two units depending on lot size, and R-3 up to eight.
  • Grandfathered licenses: an existing license keeps its status only until it lapses, and then a new application meets current code.

A new rental application is submitted at the Intergovernmental Center, 10 Civic Center Plaza, with payment, a site plan and floor plans drawn to scale. If off-street parking cannot be met, no license is issued and no further inspections happen. If your house has a rental license, ask the city to confirm in writing whether it is grandfathered and still active, because a lapsed license means the next owner applies under current code.

How do Blue Earth County property taxes work?

The county sends bills on more than 31,000 parcels. Most real estate pays on May 15 and October 15, agricultural land pays its second half November 15, and a weekend or legal holiday pushes the deadline to the next regular business day. Manufactured homes pay August 31 and November 15. Statements are mailed by March 31 and are based on the previous year's valuation.

Valuation dates to January 2, and an appraiser walks through each property roughly every fifth year, with extra visits for new construction and improvements. The state wants the overall assessment level between 90% and 105% of market value, a range the county reports meeting. The value on January 2, 2025, produced the tax payable in 2026.

The county's online tax system lets you search by address or parcel number for current and historical tax information, special assessments and the breakdown by taxing jurisdiction, and you can pay electronically. If your mortgage company escrows your taxes, you still receive a statement, and the county reminds owners that they remain responsible for confirming the bill is paid.

If you disagree with a value after the notice, talk to the assessor first at (507) 304-4251. A formal petition over last year's value goes to the Minnesota Tax Court by April 30 of the year the tax is payable, and the county takes service by email or in person at 410 South 5th Street.

What local conditions and schools come up with Mankato buyers?

The city sits where the Minnesota and Blue Earth rivers meet, and winter is a real factor. Snow cover typically begins between mid-November and mid-December and lasts into March, with a seasonal average near 35 inches. January averages about 14 degrees Fahrenheit, so insulation, furnace condition and a sound roof are visible concerns.

Mankato Area Public Schools serve Mankato, North Mankato, Eagle Lake and Madison Lake, with two high schools, Mankato West and Mankato East, and two middle schools, Dakota Meadows and Prairie Winds. Parochial and private options include Loyola Catholic School and Immanuel Lutheran.

Mankato was organized as a city on May 11, 1858, the same day Minnesota became a state, and Parsons King Johnson had settled the township in 1852. The city counted 44,488 people in 2020, up from 39,309 in 2010.

U.S. Highways 14 and 169 and Minnesota Highways 22 and 60 are the main routes, and the Mankato Transit System runs local service.

Who is a cash buyer a good fit for in Mankato?

Selling for cash can suit a landlord leaving the business, an heir handling an estate from out of town, or an owner whose deferred maintenance would trouble a lender's appraiser. Because Mankato rental licenses turn on zoning, parking and a housing inspection, a cash buyer can weigh those factors without waiting for a mortgage commitment.

Get the offer on paper along with the closing date, the split of closing costs and proof of funds. Then set it beside what a listing would net after repairs and months of carrying costs.

More questions about Mankato, MN

Is Mankato in Blue Earth County?

Mostly. Mankato is the Blue Earth County seat, though the city also reaches into Nicollet and Le Sueur counties. Your tax statement shows which county bills your parcel.

What are the Blue Earth County tax payment dates?

May 15 for the first half and October 15 for the second half on most real estate. Agricultural land pays its second half on November 15.

How many unrelated people can rent a Mankato house in R-1 or R-2 zoning?

Two. Low-density districts limit occupancy to two unrelated individuals or a family, and the unit needs two paved off-street parking stalls.

What does the state charge on the deed for a Mankato sale?

The rate is 0.33% of net consideration for prices over $3,000, paid as the deed is recorded. Your purchase agreement decides which side covers it.

Can I appeal my Mankato property value?

Yes. Call the Blue Earth County assessor at (507) 304-4251 first. A petition for the prior year's value goes to the Minnesota Tax Court on or before April 30 of the year taxes are payable.

Where is Cottage Grove and what surrounds it?

Cottage Grove is a Washington County city about 10 miles south of Saint Paul, on the north bank of the Mississippi River just above where the St. Croix River joins it. Its land area is 33.64 square miles, and the Census Bureau estimates 43,604 residents as of July 1, 2025.

Woodbury lies to the north, Hastings to the south, St. Paul Park and Newport to the west and Denmark Township to the east. U.S. Highways 10 and 61 and Interstate 494 serve the city, and the Canadian Pacific and BNSF mainlines run between Highway 61 and the river. The Minneapolis-Saint Paul airport is about half an hour away at posted speeds, and the Wisconsin border is five miles from the southeastern edge of town. Elevation is about 810 feet.

How did Cottage Grove change from farm township to suburb?

Cottage Grove dates its founding to 1843 and was platted in 1871. It began as a rural township known for the state's first creameries and for wheat, served by rail, river shipping and grist mills. Four sites in town are on the National Register of Historic Places: the Schilling Archeological District, the 1850 Grey Cloud Lime Kiln, the 1871 John P. Furber House and the 1917 Cordenio Severance House.

The modern city is mostly a product of the last half century.

  • 13,419 residents in 1970.
  • 22,935 in 1990.
  • 30,582 in 2000.
  • 38,839 at the 2020 census.
  • 43,604 in the 2025 estimate, a 12.3 percent increase over the 2020 base.

Growth of that size is the context for pricing against nearby listings.

What shapes daily life and home demand in Cottage Grove?

3M has run a production facility in Cottage Grove since 1947, making adhesive products, industrial polymers and reflective road sign material, and doing research. The location gives a workable commute to both downtowns and to the Interstate 494 strip in Bloomington.

Public schools belong to the South Washington County School District. Park High School and East Ridge High School serve most high school students, Cottage Grove Middle School and Oltman Middle School serve most middle school students, and six elementary schools sit in the city: Armstrong, Cottage Grove, Crestview, Grey Cloud, Hillside and Pine Hill.

Recreation adds to demand. Ravine Regional Park covers 515 acres of woods, hills and prairie, River Oaks is an 18-hole municipal golf course, and the city has a three-sheet ice arena. Strawberry Fest fills Kingston Park, usually in the second week of June.

Does the 3M PFAS contamination affect a Cottage Grove home sale?

It can, mainly if the house runs on a private well. The Minnesota Pollution Control Agency says 3M chemicals containing PFOS, PFOA and other PFAS were made at the Chemolite plant in Cottage Grove, and that 3M waste disposal at four east metro sites contaminated groundwater over more than 150 square miles and affected drinking water for more than 140,000 people.

The state and 3M entered a consent order in 2007 that put investigation and cleanup of three disposal sites, including the Cottage Grove Chemolite site, under the Superfund process, and Minnesota settled its lawsuit against 3M for $850 million on February 20, 2018.

Cottage Grove is on the agency's list of communities where private wells are sampled. Sampling of eligible private wells is free to homeowners under the Settlement, and eligible wells can receive point-of-entry treatment systems that the agency installs and maintains. If you own a well, request testing through the agency's online form and keep the results with your sale paperwork.

What do Census numbers say about housing in Cottage Grove?

Cottage Grove is a city of owners, with nearly nine in ten households owning their home. The table lists the main figures.

Cottage Grove housing and household figures. Source: Census Bureau QuickFacts, 2020 to 2024 survey estimates unless noted.
MeasureCottage Grove
Population estimate, July 1, 202543,604
Owner-occupied housing rate88.2%

Median monthly owner cost with a mortgage$2,254

Households14,395
Persons per household2.84
Residents under 1825.4%

A household size of 2.84 and a quarter of residents under 18 point to a family-oriented market, where school boundaries and yard space carry weight with buyers.

What city permits and licenses should a Cottage Grove seller know about?

Cottage Grove takes permit applications online, and the Building Division at 651-458-2804 handles inspections and permits. The residential permit list covers accessory structures over 200 square feet, additions, remodels, decks, demolition, pools, solar, roofing, siding, window replacement and door replacement, plus mechanical, plumbing and electrical work.

  • Construction is allowed Monday through Friday from 7 a.m. to 7 p.m. and Saturday from 9 a.m. to 7 p.m.
  • Electrical inspections are handled by a contracted outside inspector, so schedule them separately.
  • The Code Enforcement Officer handles property maintenance concerns and runs the city's rental licensing program, so an owner with tenants should call the Building Division at 651-458-2804 before a sale.

Finishing open permits before you list keeps a buyer's lender and inspector from raising questions at the last minute.

How are city utility bills settled at a Cottage Grove closing?

Title and closing companies request a utility estimate from the city, and the final amount is collected at the closing table. Cottage Grove runs an online form for this, called the Utility Billing Request for Real Estate Closing, and it covers both current and outstanding city utility bills.

Tell your closing agent early so the request goes in before the closing date. The estimate exists so the city's share can be collected at closing.

What does Washington County charge to record a Cottage Grove deed?

The Washington County Recorder takes deeds at the Government Center in Stillwater, and a deed costs $46 to record plus state deed tax of $3.30 per thousand dollars of consideration. At the Census median value of $378,800, that tax is about $1,250.

  • A conservation fee of $5 applies.
  • A well certificate costs $54 when one is required.
  • A deed with consideration under $3,000 carries a flat $1.65 tax.
  • Some deeds also need an electronic Certificate of Real Estate Value.

Washington County says most local property is abstract property, so a thorough title search should come before a sale. The Public Research Room in the Government Center is open weekdays from 8 a.m. to 4:15 p.m. Under Minnesota Statutes 103I.235, you also owe the buyer a written statement about any known wells before you sign.

How do Washington County property taxes work for a seller?

Most real property tax is due in two equal installments, on May 15 and October 15. As of mid-November 2026, the second half for this year was due last month, and the next first-half deadline is May 15, 2027.

Value is set as of January 2 each year. The county mails tax statements by March 31 with a valuation notice for the following year, and it mails the Proposed Property Tax Notice in mid-November, so that notice is arriving about now. On a homestead, a late first-half payment picks up a 2 percent penalty on May 16, and taxes unpaid on January 2 become delinquent with 8 percent annual interest.

Homeowners with a household income under $142,490 may qualify for the state's homestead credit refund for 2025. Ways to pay include eCheck with a $0.75 fee, a card with a 2.35 percent fee, mail, bank bill pay and the drop box at the Government Center. Call 651-430-6175 to talk to an assessor about your value.

What are your choices for selling a Cottage Grove house?

A traditional listing, a for-sale-by-owner sale and a direct cash sale all work in Cottage Grove, and each fits a different situation.

With a house in good repair and time to spare, a listing aims at the highest price. A cash buyer fits an owner who needs a quick closing, who holds a house with open permits or deferred work, or who has a private well and wants fewer steps before closing. Collect the permit history, well results, the utility estimate and the tax balance before you talk to any buyer, and compare written offers against what an agent expects your house to bring.

More questions about Cottage Grove, MN

Can I get my private well tested for PFAS in Cottage Grove?

Yes. Cottage Grove is among the east metro communities where the state samples private wells, and sampling of eligible wells is free to homeowners under the 3M Settlement. Use the online request form on the Minnesota Pollution Control Agency's well sampling page.

How are Cottage Grove utility bills handled when the house sells?

The title or closing company requests an estimate through the city's Utility Billing Request for Real Estate Closing form, and any current or outstanding balance is collected at closing.

What does it cost to record a deed in Washington County?

The recording fee for a deed is $46, state deed tax is $3.30 per thousand dollars of consideration, and the conservation fee is $5. A well certificate adds $54 when it is required.

When is the next Washington County property tax due date after November 2026?

The next first-half installment is due May 15, 2027, and the second half follows on October 15, 2027. The second half of 2026 was due on October 15, 2026.

Do I need a permit to replace the roof or windows before selling in Cottage Grove?

Yes. Roofing, siding, window replacement and door replacement are all on the city's residential permit list, and applications are submitted through the online permitting site. Call 651-458-2800 or email building@cottagegrovemn.gov for help with an account.

What must the Maplewood Truth-in-Sale of Housing report include?

Single-family houses, duplexes, townhouses, condominiums and other attached one-family units need a full report before they can be shown. A duplex needs a report for each unit, and manufactured homes are not covered, according to the city's program page.

You call a city-licensed evaluator yourself, because each evaluator sets fees and availability. The evaluator files a copy with the city and gives you one, which you keep on display for buyers. A copy must go to the buyer before a contract is signed, and the report is valid for one owner or one year.

The owner also signs a statement. The city lists what it covers:

  • Flooding, sewer backup or chronic water seepage the owner knows about, and its cause and extent.
  • Pending housing orders from the city, and whether the home has a homestead classification.
  • Known wells, with a map, and whether each is in use or sealed.
  • Deed restrictions, shoreland, pipeline or floodplain rules, and an adjacent high-voltage transmission line.

The report is for disclosure and the sale does not depend on the deficiencies it lists, though city inspectors may use it to require correction of code violations.

How does the well disclosure fit in?

State law adds its own well rule. Before you sign an agreement to sell, Minnesota Statutes 103I.235 requires a written statement that you know of no wells, or a statement and map showing each well and whether it is in use, not in use or sealed. At closing, a well disclosure certificate goes to the recorder unless the deed carries the standard no-wells statement.

A county recorder collects a $54 fee for a completed certificate, and a seller who knew of an undisclosed well can owe the sealing costs and attorney fees if the buyer sues within six years of closing. Individual condominium units are exempt.

If you are unsure whether an old well exists on your lot, check your survey and deed records before you sign.

What are Maplewood's housing and income numbers?

The Census Bureau shows 20.1% of residents are 65 or older and 28.2% of residents speak a language other than English at home.

Maplewood, 2020-2024 Census Bureau QuickFacts housing and income figures
MeasureMaplewood
Typical home value (owner-occupied)$323,200
Share of homes lived in by owners71.8%
Median gross rent$1,406
Median household income$91,394
Households15,210
Bachelor's degree or higher35.3%

Maplewood totals 17.99 square miles, of which 16.98 is land, and highways crossing it include U.S. 61, Highway 36 and interstates 35E, 94, 694 and 494.

What local landmarks and employers matter to Maplewood buyers?

Maplewood is home to the corporate headquarters and main campus of 3M, whose first central research laboratory buildings were completed there in 1955. The city also has Maplewood Mall, which opened in 1974 on 125 acres, and St. John's Hospital, which opened in 1985. Together they draw workers, shoppers and patients to the area every day. Aldrich Arena hosted the 1993 NCAA Division III men's ice hockey tournament, which drew just under 14,000 fans.

Before European settlement in the 1840s, the area was home to several Indigenous peoples, with Dakota settling in the 18th century. A stagecoach line between Saint Paul and Duluth stopped here from 1856 to 1870, and in 1858 the land was organized under McLean and New Canada townships. The name is a puzzle: according to the local historical society's director, there were no maple trees when the area was organized, only prairie and oak savanna.

The city's unusual L shape comes from Saint Paul's annexation of surrounding land in the 1890s. It extends 5.9 miles east to west and 10 miles north to south, with a southern leg about 7.5 miles long and nearly a mile wide. Neighborhoods built from the 1950s onward replaced farmsteads, and the original Gladstone town site was platted in 1887.

How do Ramsey County taxes work on a Maplewood sale?

Ramsey County splits the bill into a May 15 payment and an October 15 payment, and a weekend due date rolls forward to the next business day. Real property tax of $100 or less must be paid in full by May 15. Penalties for a homestead start at 2% on the day after the first half is due and climb to 4% on June 1.

Ramsey allows a one-time penalty waiver once every ten years for each parcel, applying to either the first or the second half. Hardship abatement requests go to the Auditor/Treasurer's office at 651-266-2222. Valuation questions go to the county assessor at 651-266-2131.

The assessor's estimated market value is set as of January 2 for taxes payable the following year. If you are selling in the second half of the year, ask the closing agent how the October installment will be divided, since the purchase agreement controls it.

What if you own a rental in Maplewood?

Since 2019 Maplewood has required a rental license before tenants move in, with a background check on each owner, an on-site inspection and an annual fee of $150 plus $50 per unit. Properties are placed on a one-, two- or three-year inspection cycle, and the first inspection and first re-inspection are free. A second re-inspection costs $250, and each later one $500.

If you are selling a licensed rental, bring your inspection history to the table, because a buyer who plans to keep renting will want it. A cash buyer who already manages rentals may find that useful, but call the city at 651-249-2300 to confirm what a new owner must file.

More questions about Maplewood, MN

Does Maplewood require an inspection before I can list my house?

Yes. A city-licensed evaluator must complete a Truth-in-Sale of Housing report before the property is shown. It covers houses, duplexes, townhouses and condominiums, and you call the evaluator directly to book it.

How long does a Maplewood TISH report last?

One owner or one year. The city's director can also require a new inspection if there is substandard maintenance or later damage to the building.

Do I have to repair everything on the Maplewood report before selling?

No. The city says the sale does not depend on the deficiencies listed, though inspectors may use the report to require correction of code violations later.

What are the Ramsey County payment dates for a Maplewood home?

May 15 and October 15. A homestead pays a 2% penalty if the first half arrives after May 15, and Ramsey offers a one-time waiver per parcel every ten years.

What does a Maplewood rental license cost?

The annual fee is $150 plus $50 per unit, and each owner passes a background check and an inspection before the license is issued.

What should a seller know about Inver Grove Heights, Minnesota?

Inver Grove Heights is a Dakota County city of 36,873 residents in the Census Bureau's July 1, 2025 estimate, with a land area of about 27.9 square miles. It lies roughly nine miles southeast of Saint Paul, and Newport and Saint Paul Park sit across the Mississippi River from it.

Irish and German farmers claimed land here after the 1851 Treaty of Traverse des Sioux, and the township took its name from the Irish village of Inver and the German town of Grove. By 1880 there were 240 farms, four churches and four school districts. The village of Inver Grove and Inver Grove Township merged to form the city on March 9, 1965, and the population climbed from 6,266 in 1960 to 29,751 in 2000.

Notable local landmarks include District 7 School, Dakota County's first public school (1854), the 1894 Rock Island Swing Bridge, now a park, and the site where a B-52 bomber crashed on September 16, 1958. Southern Inver Grove Heights also holds the Pine Bend Bluffs Scientific and Natural Area, where a roughly 500 million year old impact crater was identified in 2022.

What do Census figures say about Inver Grove Heights homes?

The city has an older population and a mix of owners and renters. About 76.9 percent of units are owner-occupied and the median home value is $363,400 for 2020-2024, while 17.9 percent of residents are 65 or older. Older owners downsizing or heirs handling an estate are common sellers here.

Retail sales per capita are the highest of the four cities in the Census comparison, ahead of Fridley at $25,831 and Lakeville at $15,970.

What are the ways to sell an Inver Grove Heights house quickly?

Most owners choose among a traditional listing, a sale without an agent, or an as-is cash purchase. The right choice depends on the house and your timeline.

  • A listing works well for an updated house in a school area buyers ask for, such as Simley High School's attendance area, but it adds showings, inspection requests and loan approval time.
  • A for-sale-by-owner sale keeps the commission with you, though you handle disclosures, the purchase agreement and negotiation yourself.
  • A cash buyer purchases without repairs or cleaning, which suits estate houses, tenant-occupied properties and homes with deferred maintenance.

With a median home value of $363,400 and 17.9 percent of residents over 65, estate and downsizing sales are a regular part of the local market. Whichever path you take, line up the final water read, the deed tax and any county clearance steps early so the closing date holds.

Can I rent out or list an Inver Grove Heights house on Airbnb?

Not for stays shorter than 30 days unless the home is owner-occupied. Inver Grove Heights changed its short-term rental rules effective April 1, 2025, so properties that are not the owner's residence may only be rented for 30 days or more, including those listed on Airbnb or Vrbo.

Long-term rentals need a city rental license. In October 2025 the city sent license holders a letter about proposed amendments: a one-year license term, a January 31 renewal deadline with an April 1 through March 31 license period, a property manager living within 75 miles, and a three-tier fine structure. The final vote was expected after a November 10, 2025 reading. Ask the city clerk for the terms in force today if you are selling a house that is currently rented.

Buyers who plan to keep the house as a rental will want the license history, so gather it before you list.

Which Inver Grove Heights code rules can slow a sale?

The city's code enforcement office publishes the rules most often cited on residential lots, and a pre-listing walk-around helps.

  • Grass must stay under eight inches, and brush piles are not allowed.
  • Fences need a permit before installation, with a 48 inch limit in the front yard and seven feet in side and back yards.
  • Vehicles stored outside need current tabs and must run. Inoperable vehicles belong in a garage.
  • Roll-off dumpsters cannot sit in the street and may stay on a lot only three months out of twelve unless an extension is granted.
  • Parking on any city street is banned from 3:00 to 6:00 AM between November 1 and April 1.

Home businesses must be run entirely inside the dwelling with no visible signs, which matters if you are selling a house that doubles as a workshop. Violations are reported through the city's RequestTracker, and the Code Compliance Division answers questions at 651-450-2491.

Which schools and employers shape the Inver Grove Heights market?

Most of the city belongs to Inver Grove Heights Community Schools, Independent School District 199. It runs Simley High School, Inver Grove Heights Middle School, and Hilltop, Pine Bend and Salem Hills elementary schools. The western part of the city is in District 196 (Rosemount-Apple Valley-Eagan), and a small northwest piece is in District 197. Inver Hills Community College is also inside the city.

CHS, Inc. keeps its headquarters here, and the city's 2021 financial report listed Cenex and CHS Cooperatives as the largest employer with about 1,600 workers. The Pine Bend Refinery, the largest in Minnesota, straddles the border with Rosemount, and Gertens Greenhouses is a major garden center. The main roads are I-494, US 52, and Minnesota Highways 55 and 3.

How do I handle city water, deeds and disclosures when selling in Inver Grove Heights?

For water and sewer, call Utility Billing at 651-450-2520 well ahead of your move; the city asks newcomers for at least one week of notice to arrange a meter reading, and sellers should set the final read the same way.

Dakota County Property Taxation and Records records the deed. State deed tax at 0.0033 of the net price comes to about $1,199 on the city's $363,400 median home value. Dakota County's selling-property page flags extra steps for manufactured homes, for properties with wells or septic systems, and for owners on Medical Assistance, who may need a certificate of clearance from the county at 651-554-6555.

If sewage on the property does not go to a permitted facility, state law requires a written septic disclosure before the purchase agreement is signed, and a seller who knew of the system and failed to disclose it can owe the buyer the cost of bringing it into compliance (Minnesota Statutes 115.55, subdivision 6). Dakota County's 2026 open book appeal period ran March 11 to May 1 and the board of appeal met June 8, so any value challenge for this year has closed.

More questions about Inver Grove Heights, MN

Can I sell an Inver Grove Heights house that has tenants?

Yes. Give the buyer the lease and the city rental license details. Because the city has been revising its rental licensing ordinance, ask the City Clerk what the license term and renewal rules are before you list.

How much notice does Inver Grove Heights utility billing need?

The city asks for at least one week of notice to schedule a water meter reading, and its number is 651-450-2520. Contact them before closing so the seller's final bill is accurate.

What is deed tax on an Inver Grove Heights sale?

State deed tax is 0.0033 of the net consideration when it is above $3,000. At the Census median home value of $363,400 that is about $1,199. Dakota County collects it when the deed is recorded.

Do I need a septic disclosure when selling in Inver Grove Heights?

Only if sewage on the property does not go to a permitted facility. Under Minnesota Statutes 115.55, you must then describe the system and map it before the purchase agreement is signed. If the house is on city sewer, the disclosure is a simple statement to that effect.

Are there special steps if the owner is on Medical Assistance?

Dakota County says residents on Medical Assistance have requirements when selling, and it runs a certificates of clearance office at 651-554-6555. Call before you accept an offer so the paperwork does not delay closing.

Selling in Richfield?

What must I do before closing on a house in Richfield, MN?

Richfield requires a city housing inspection before title passes on any single-family home, two-family home or condominium. The council adopted the Point of Sale program in 1989 for transfers after October 1, 1990, and the city issues a Certificate of Housing Maintenance that has to be in hand at closing.

That rule shapes every sale in the city, whether you list the house, sell it yourself or sell directly to an investor. The inspection has to happen before closing, and any repairs it turns up must be finished and re-inspected before closing and within one year of the first visit. The city recommends scheduling the inspection before the house is listed or advertised, and the owner, not the agent, is responsible for arranging it. A city housing inspector does the work. You apply online, pay the fee, and only then call the inspections line at 612-861-9882 to book a time.

Richfield Point of Sale inspection fees (include one initial inspection and one re-inspection)
Property typeFee
Single-family home$190
Two-family home$270
Condominium$140

No inspection is needed when a name is only being removed from title after a divorce or a death and no sale is happening.

What do Richfield inspectors look for, and who pays for repairs?

The inspector looks at the roof, foundation, doors and windows, exterior covering, electrical, plumbing, chimney and heating and cooling, then gives you a written list. The program does not force older houses up to today's code. It requires fixes for violations of the code in force when the house was built and for anything unsafe.

  • Missing or dead smoke detectors, loose or absent handrails, and first-floor windows without locks.
  • Bare wood or peeling paint, damaged window screens, cracked glass and clogged or missing gutters.
  • Furnaces more than 15 years old or installed without a permit, which need certification by a licensed heating contractor.
  • Electrical or plumbing changes with no permit on file, which need a licensed electrician's or plumber's certification.
  • Ungrounded three-prong outlets, extension cords used as permanent wiring and vinyl or foil dryer vents.

An owner who lives in the home can often do the repairs personally, as long as the work meets code. If you would rather not do them, the buyer can take over the work order, submit a schedule, agree on when hazards will be removed and sign a Housing Cash Escrow Agreement with the city. The certificate is not a warranty, and the city says it is no substitute for a private inspection.

How does Richfield's housing stock affect a sale?

Richfield is an inner-ring suburb that touches Minneapolis on the north, the airport and Fort Snelling on the east, Bloomington on the south and Edina on the west. Most of its roughly 10,000 single-family houses went up in the 1950s, and its 5,000 or so apartments date from the 1960s and early 1970s.

The city's own list of common corrections, covered above, is heavy on wiring, furnaces and windows. Several remodeling programs can help owners get ahead of that. A Fix Up loan through the Center for Energy and the Environment runs from $2,000 to $35,000. The Transformation Home Loan covers 15% of a project that costs $50,000 or more, up to $25,000, with no payments and no interest.

Those loans matter when you sell. The Transformation Home Loan comes due on sale of the home or is forgiven after 30 years, and Hennepin County's Deferred Loan, up to $30,000 for qualifying households, is also due on sale or forgiven after 15 years. Check your records for either loan so the payoff shows on the title company's closing statement.

What do Census numbers say about Richfield?

Richfield is the renter-heavy city among its neighbors. Only 61.6% of homes are lived in by their owners, against 75% in Plymouth, and the typical household is small at 2.19 people.

The Census Bureau estimates 36,593 residents for July 2025, which is 1.1% fewer than the 2020 base, packed into 6.78 square miles of land at about 5,458 people per square mile. Owners value the middle home at $344,000, renters pay a median of $1,393 and the median household earns $85,132. About 24% of residents speak a language other than English at home, and 16.9% were born abroad. RDLS Elementary teaches in both English and Spanish.

Richfield Public Schools (ISD 280) serve about 4,200 students in Richfield and part of Edina. Four elementary schools, Centennial, Sheridan, R-STEM and RDLS, cover kindergarten through grade 5, and Richfield Middle School and Richfield High School follow. Best Buy's headquarters, which moved to the city in 2003, is the largest local employer.

Is my Richfield house a rental, and what do I owe the city?

Every residential rental in Richfield must be licensed and inspected each year under City Code Section 407. License renewals are due by December 31, so a rental sold in the fall or winter needs a renewal plan.

  • Apply to the city for the license.
  • Schedule an inspection of the interior, exterior and common areas.
  • Correct any violations within the timeframe the report gives.
  • Renew each year.

The rental license fee covers two inspections. Further visits cost more, starting at $50 for the third inspection of a one- or two-unit building and climbing to a cap of $1,500, and $100 to $3,000 for buildings with three or more units.

Section 409 gives tenants in affordable units a three-month protection period when a building changes hands, and the new owner's notice is due a month after the transfer. Owners of one- to three-unit buildings are also responsible for unpaid organized trash collection charges once balances reach $100, which the city can assess to property taxes. Settle that account before the closing date.

How does Hennepin County handle the deed and taxes on a Richfield sale?

Hennepin County records the deed and bills the property tax. Property tax arrives in two installments, with deadlines on May 15 and October 15. Hennepin shifts a deadline forward when the 15th is a weekend or holiday, and the October 2026 deadline has already passed.

When the sale closes, your title company submits the deed along with the electronic certificate of real estate value, a statement naming where tax statements go and the well statement or certificate. Hennepin County says parcels with delinquent taxes cannot be transferred. The recording fee is $46 per document and the well certificate is $54. Under Minnesota Statutes section 513.55, you also give the buyer a written disclosure before the purchase agreement is signed. Title companies and lenders can use the county's eRecord system, which records documents within one to three days. You can read the county's full fee list on its recording page.

More questions about Richfield, MN

Can I sell my Richfield house to an investor and skip the city inspection?

No. The Point of Sale requirement applies to the transfer of title, so it covers every sale of a single-family home, two-family home or condominium, whoever the buyer is. The buyer can take over repairs under a Housing Cash Escrow Agreement.

How long is a Richfield Point of Sale inspection good for?

Repairs must be completed and re-inspected before closing and within one year of the first inspection. Plan the inspection so your closing date falls inside that year.

What does the Richfield Point of Sale fee include?

It covers one initial inspection and one re-inspection. The fee is $190 for a single-family home, $270 for a two-family home and $140 for a condominium.

Does Richfield's rental license transfer with the house?

The city requires every residential rental to be licensed and inspected annually, and renewals are due December 31. Confirm with the city's rental inspections line, 612-861-9882, how the license is handled after a sale.

What if I have a Richfield remodeling loan on my house?

Check the terms. The Transformation Home Loan is due when you sell, or forgiven after 30 years. The county Deferred Loan is likewise due on sale or forgiven after 15 years. Your title company will include any balance in the closing figures.

What kind of city is Roseville, Minnesota?

Roseville is an inner-ring suburb in Ramsey County that touches both Saint Paul and Minneapolis, a position shared in the metro with only Lauderdale. It covers 13.84 square miles in total, and the 45th parallel crosses it, marked near Cleveland Avenue and Loren Road.

The area was settled by Dakota and Ojibwe people, and the first settlers of European descent came in 1843. Rose Township was organized in 1858 and named for an early settler, Isaac Rose. It once included land that is now Lauderdale, Falcon Heights and parts of the two big cities. Rapid growth in the 1930s and 1940s led Roseville to incorporate as a village in 1948, after which the township ceased to exist.

The Census Bureau's July 1, 2025 estimate of 35,663 residents is 1.7 percent lower than the 2020 base of 36,268, a small decline. The age mix leans older: 22.5 percent of residents are 65 or over, and the average household has only 2.20 people.

What do Census figures say about Roseville housing?

Two thirds of Roseville households, 66.4 percent, own the home they live in, and the median value is $352,100.

The land area is 13.02 square miles, which works out to roughly 2,785 people per square mile, so Roseville is densely settled for a suburb. Census estimates also show 95.5 percent of adults 25 and older with a high school diploma and 7.5 percent of residents below the poverty line, and 5.9 percent of residents are under five.

Which employers, shopping centers and roads define Roseville?

Retail is the signature. Rosedale Center and Har Mar Mall are both here, and the Census Bureau's 2022 figures show $1.83 billion in retail sales, about $51,361 for every resident. The first Target opened in Roseville on May 3, 1962, and Minnesota's first McDonald's opened here in 1957.

Public employers matter too. The Minnesota Department of Education has its headquarters in Roseville, as does the Metropolitan District of the Minnesota Department of Transportation. Health care adds about $718 million in receipts, and transportation and warehousing about $440 million.

Interstate 35W and Minnesota Highways 36, 51 (Snelling Avenue) and 280 are the four main routes. The average trip to work is 20.7 minutes.

Which schools and parks serve Roseville homes?

Roseville Area Schools, district 623, serves the city. Its elementary schools include Brimhall, Central Park, Emmett D. Williams, Edgerton, Falcon Heights, Little Canada and Parkview Center School for kindergarten through eighth grade. Roseville Area Middle School covers grades 7 and 8, and Roseville Area High School covers 9 through 12.

  • Private choices include Concordia Academy, King of Kings Lutheran Church and School, and St. Rose of Lima.
  • The University of Northwestern, Saint Paul is in the city.
  • Central Park, at 225 acres, is the largest park and holds Bennett Lake.
  • The John Rose Oval is billed as North America's largest outdoor artificial ice sheet, and the Roseville Library is described as the busiest in Minnesota.

Check with the district about the elementary school for your address before you advertise it.

Do I need to register a rental house in Roseville?

Yes. A 2008 ordinance requires owners of rental properties with one to four units to register them with the city every year, and each registration expires 365 days after it is issued. Single-family homes, condominiums, townhomes, twinhomes, duplexes, triplexes and fourplexes are all covered, as are short-term rentals, which also need a separate license.

  • Post the registration certificate inside the rental unit.
  • A late fee applies to renewals more than 30 days overdue.
  • Renting to relatives is registered without a fee, and so are state-licensed group homes.
  • Buildings with more than four units, hospital units, hotels, on-campus college housing and owner-occupied homes with unrelated boarders are exempt from this program.

Renewals are done through the city's ePermits site, and the city also points owners to the Minnesota Attorney General's guide on landlord and tenant rights. A landlord who sells should confirm with Community Development how the registration is closed out.

What does Ramsey County do when a Roseville deed is recorded?

Real estate documents for the county are kept by the Recorder and Registrar of Titles Office, reachable at 651-266-2050. A recorded document stays on the record for good. A mistake is repaired by recording a corrective document with fresh signatures and acknowledgments and a correction note.

Ramsey County has two systems side by side. Torrens land is registered by court order or by the Examiner of Titles and has a certificate of title, while abstract land does not. A document covering both kinds must be filed with each office separately, either as two sets of originals or by recording one first and then taking the recorded copy to the second office.

  • A transfer deed needs a well disclosure certificate and a $50 fee, or a qualifying statement on the deed.
  • Notary service for real property in the county costs $5 per notarial certificate, and the signer must be present with ID.
  • The office does not give legal advice or blank forms.
  • Liens are released by recording a satisfaction, and both stay on the record.

What happens if a Ramsey County tax payment is late?

Ramsey County owners with a tax bill over $100 pay in two parts, ahead of May 16 and October 16. Minn. Stat. 279.01 sets the cost of lateness: 2 percent on a homestead and 4 percent on other property the day after a missed date, the same again if the balance is still open on the first of the next month, then 1 percent a month through December. Totals top out at 8 percent for homestead and 12 percent otherwise.

The Ramsey County Assessor's Office sets market value as of every January 2 and views each parcel at least once every five years. It also assigns the classification, such as residential homestead or nonhomestead, and the legislature sets a different percentage for each class. The county also posts a yearly Assessor's Report online.

What must a Roseville seller tell the buyer?

Minn. Stat. 513.55 has the seller put in writing, before any agreement is signed, the material facts known to the seller that could badly affect an ordinary buyer's use of the house. The statement must be honest and based on what the seller actually knows, and it may go to the buyer's licensee. Past water in a basement or an addition built without a permit are the kinds of facts to put in writing.

More questions about Roseville, MN

Does a Roseville landlord pay a registration fee to rent to a relative?

No. The city lists rental properties in which all renters are related to the owner as registered without a fee, and owners no longer need to notarize the exemption affidavit.

How long does a Roseville rental registration last?

It lasts 365 days from the date of issue. The owner renews online through ePermits, and a late fee applies once a renewal is more than 30 days past due.

Which Ramsey County office records my deed?

The Ramsey County Recorder and Registrar of Titles Office does, and its number is 651-266-2050. Abstract land goes to the Recorder and Torrens land goes to the Registrar of Titles.

What penalty applies if I miss the May tax payment on a Roseville home?

Two percent of the unpaid amount for a homestead, four percent for nonhomestead. More accrues month by month until the statutory cap.

Who needs to hand over a written disclosure when a Roseville house sells?

The seller does, before signing, and the paper can be passed to the buyer's licensee. Minn. Stat. 513.55 is the rule.

What are my choices for selling a house in Andover, Minnesota?

Owners in Andover have three paths: hire an agent and list, sell the house yourself, or take a cash offer from a buyer who accepts the property in its present condition. All three finish with a signed purchase agreement and a deed recorded in Anoka County.

One duty follows you down every path. Before you sign to sell a home, Minnesota Statutes 513.55 has you hand over a written disclosure of known material facts that could significantly hurt a typical buyer's enjoyment of the house, stated in good faith. Giving it to the buyer's agent counts as giving it to the buyer.

Before you choose, pull together four items:

  • Your latest Anoka County tax statement and parcel number.
  • Permit records for plumbing, mechanical, roofing, basement or deck work done on the house.
  • The city rental license, if tenants live there.
  • A draft of the written seller disclosure.

A cash offer tends to appeal to owners who want a short timeline, face repairs, or hold an inherited house or tenants. Get any offer in writing, and see that the number allows for tax owed and any open permits.

What is Andover like?

Andover is a city of about 33,874 people in Anoka County. That July 1, 2025 estimate from the Census Bureau is 3.9 percent above the 32,601 counted in 2020. Andover spans about 34.8 square miles, and in 2020 nearly 23 percent of residents lived in areas the census labeled rural. Median age was 39.8, with 25.8 percent of residents under 18.

The area was organized in 1857 as Round Lake Township and renamed Grow Township in 1860 after Representative Galusha Grow, who was prominent in passing the Homestead Act. For a century the population stayed small, with 757 people in 1950 and 1,402 in 1960. Then it leapt to 3,830 by 1970, 9,387 by 1980, 15,216 by 1990 and 26,588 by 2000, so nearly all of the city's growth came after 1960.

The 2020 census counted 10,782 households in Andover, and 39.4 percent of them had children under 18. The city's annual summer celebration, held in early July around City Hall, Andover Elementary and Sunshine Park, includes a 5K run, a parade and fireworks.

County Roads 9, 18, 78 and 116 are the main routes, with U.S. Highway 10 close by. Crooked Lake, on the southern border and mostly inside Coon Rapids, is the only fully recreational lake. Most of Andover belongs to Anoka-Hennepin School District 11, whose schools inside the city include Andover Elementary, Crooked Lake Elementary, Rum River Elementary, Oak View Middle School and Andover High School. A narrow northern strip falls under St. Francis Area Schools, District 15, so confirm the address before naming a district to a buyer.

How does Andover compare with the country on housing?

Andover is overwhelmingly owner-occupied, and its households are larger than the national norm. This table sets Census Bureau 2020 to 2024 estimates for the city against the country.

Andover housing figures against the United States, 2020 to 2024 (source: Census Bureau QuickFacts)

Which Andover permits matter before I sell?

The city's Building Department warns that work done without a needed permit has to be disclosed at sale and that code violations can delay or devalue a deal. Before listing, check your past projects against the permit list.

  • Permits are required for new construction, remodeling, additions and alterations, basement finishing, decks and porches, roofing, siding, irrigation systems and solid fuel fireplaces.
  • Plumbing permits cover water heaters and water softeners. Mechanical permits cover furnaces, air conditioners, boilers and gas fireplaces. Electrical work needs its own permit.
  • Septic systems need an installation permit and work by a Minnesota Pollution Control Agency licensed designer and installer. Pumping a septic tank takes a $20 permit that the pumper obtains.
  • No permit is needed for detached accessory structures under 200 square feet, sidewalks and patios, painting, flooring, cabinets, or normal maintenance such as replacing deck boards.

Homeowners may pull permits themselves, but the city says a licensed residential contractor is usually the better choice. Residential permits are typically approved right away or within one or two days, and about a third of permits are applied for and paid online. The Building Department is at 1685 Crosstown Blvd NW, reachable at 763-755-8700 or building@andovermn.gov.

Does Andover regulate rental houses?

Yes. Single family and multifamily rentals both need a city license and inspections. A license lasts two years, each rental gets at least one inspection in that span, and a new owner cannot take over the old license.

This matters when you sell a house with tenants in it. A buyer who plans to keep renting must obtain a fresh license, so mention the tenancy early. The city's rental page links to Chapter 8 of the Andover ordinances and to the Minnesota Attorney General's landlord and tenant information.

How do Anoka County property taxes work when an Andover house sells?

Anoka County prints a single statement for each parcel, mailed in mid-March. A deed recorded after January 1 does not prompt a second mailing, so the bill goes to the earlier owner, and a duplicate must be requested. A missing statement is no excuse for a late fee.

The county sets May 15 and October 15 as the dates and allows no grace period; a deadline on a weekend rolls to Monday. Online payment goes through PayAnokaCounty, with card payments at 2.6 percent and ACH e-checks at $3.50. Checks go to Property Records and Taxation, 2100 3rd Avenue, Anoka, MN 55303, or to the counter at the Government Center. A free direct payment program is explained at 763-323-5400. For mailed checks, the postmark decides timeliness, so the county advises a hand-applied one from a post office clerk.

To see what a parcel owes, search the county's property information by parcel number or by house number plus the first three characters of the street name, for example 4th rather than 4th Street. If the street shows as unassigned in the tax system, use the parcel number printed on the statement. The Government Center counter in Anoka is open 8:00 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. on weekdays, and a tax drop box sits beside it.

Two sale steps are easy to miss. A homestead owner who sells should report it to the assessor inside 30 days, or the county can strip the homestead and add penalties. At recording, a certificate of real estate value also goes to the county auditor (Minnesota Statutes 272.115). Next year's proposed statements land in mid-November and become final only after levies are approved in December.

More questions about Andover, MN

How fast can I sell a house in Andover, MN?

It depends on the route. A listed sale waits on showings, financing and inspections, while a cash purchase removes the lender from the timeline. Either way, the written seller disclosure comes before your signature.

Is a permit required to swap a water heater in Andover?

Yes, a plumbing permit covers water heater and water softener replacement. A furnace or air conditioner falls under a separate mechanical permit.

Which school district serves Andover?

Most of Andover is in Anoka-Hennepin School District 11. A small strip along the northern edge belongs to St. Francis Area Schools, District 15.

Who sends the Andover property tax statement?

The county does, each March, and its Property Records and Taxation office takes payment. If nothing arrives by April 1, call 763-323-5400 for a duplicate.

Must I tell the county when I sell my Andover home?

If it was your homestead, yes: report the sale to the assessor within 30 days to avoid lost homestead status and penalties. The county auditor also receives a certificate of real estate value.

Where is Savage, Minnesota, and how did it get its name?

Savage lies in Scott County on the Minnesota River's south bank, some 15 miles south-southwest of downtown Minneapolis. The river forms its northern boundary, and the Credit River runs north through the city to meet it. The Census Bureau lists 15.61 square miles of land.

Traders set up a post where the Credit and Minnesota rivers meet in 1852. Irish and Scottish settlers built a landing named Hamilton, and the town was incorporated in 1892 as the village of Hamilton. In 1902 a Minneapolis businessman, Marion Willis Savage, bought the racing horse Dan Patch and trained him at a farm inside the village limits. The town was renamed for him in 1904, and in 1906 Dan Patch set a world pacing mile record at the Minnesota State Fair.

During World War II the city housed Camp Savage, a military intelligence language school, and Cargill built Navy ships at Port Cargill on the river. Roughly 17 blocks of the late 19th century town still make up downtown along Highway 13.

How fast has Savage grown, and what do its housing numbers look like?

Savage stayed small for decades because the river cut it off and no interstate reached it. Upgrades to Highway 13 in the 1980s and the Bloomington Ferry Bridge in 1996 changed that, and the Census Bureau counted 26,911 people in 2010 and 32,465 in 2020. The July 1, 2025 estimate is 32,970, a 1.6 percent rise over the 2020 base of 32,463.

Roughly 93 percent of residents stayed in the same house for the previous year. With households averaging 2.74 people and a quarter of residents under 18, Savage skews toward families.

Which roads, schools and open land shape a Savage sale?

Highway 13 and County Road 42 carry most traffic across Savage, while I-35W and U.S. 169 pass just outside its borders. Savage still has undeveloped land, including parts of the Minnesota Valley National Wildlife Refuge and the Murphy-Hanrehan Park Reserve.

Three school districts serve Savage, which is easy to overlook when you describe a house:

  • Prior Lake-Savage District 719, with Redtail Ridge, Hamilton Ridge and Glendale elementary schools feeding Prior Lake High School.
  • Burnsville-Eagan-Savage District 191, with Harriet Bishop and Hidden Valley elementaries and Eagle Ridge Middle School feeding Burnsville High School.
  • Shakopee District 720.

Buyers ask which district covers an address, so confirm it before listing. The Census Bureau's 2022 figures show about $399.3 million in retail sales and $94.7 million in health care receipts in the city.

Is Savage rental registration mandatory, and does it cost anything?

Registration is mandatory and free. Savage's residential rental ordinance, Title 11, Chapter 121, requires owners to register with the city so emergency services and the city have a contact for each rental. The city describes the ordinance as a partnership with owners and ties it to Crime Free Residential Rental Property training offered at several Minnesota locations.

An owner of a rental who plans to sell can do the following:

  • Read the registration ordinance before you fill out the form.
  • Ask the city how to close out or update your registration once the house is sold.
  • Pass the registration and training information to the buyer so they can register under their own name.

The city's property protection pages are the place to start with questions.

How do Scott County property taxes and appeals work for a Savage house?

Scott County's second-half 2026 installment fell due on Thursday, October 15, so no 2026 payment is outstanding on a current account. Owners pay through eNotices Online (a $1.50 charge for an e-check, 2.3 percent for a card), by mail, in a Government Center drop box, or at a county library box in the weeks before a deadline. Property and Taxation Services is at 952-496-8115.

Postal postmarks now show the day mail is first processed, not the day it was dropped off. The county suggests paying electronically, requesting a hand postmark, or mailing several business days early.

A Savage owner who thinks the value is high should bring evidence, such as an appraisal or recent comparable sales, to the city assessor. The next stop is the open book or local board session named on the value notice, and after it the county board of appeal. Tax Court is the final stage, with an April 30 filing cutoff.

What does the Scott County Land Records office do for a Savage seller?

The Scott County Land Records Department records deeds, mortgages, assignments, releases and satisfactions. Its number is 952-496-8150, and plats and priority documents such as sheriff foreclosures or certificates of redemption require an appointment. Electronic, mail and drop-box recordings are processed.

  • Property Watch is a free service that emails the owner when any document is recorded under their name and parcel number.
  • RecordEASE is the paid portal for searching documents by parcel, by document number, by plat or lien, or by tract index.
  • The office checks that a document is in recordable form but does not supply legal forms or advice, and it points people to the state's Uniform Conveyancing Blanks, an attorney or a title company.

Signing up for Property Watch is useful on the day you close, because you can see when the deed is recorded.

How does a sale change a Savage property's homestead status?

State law ties homestead status to the certificate of value. A sale above $3,000 requires one at the auditor's office when the deed is recorded, and without it the property cannot be classified as homestead (Minn. Stat. 272.115).

The assessor also removes the homestead classification for the next assessment year when a property is sold, unless the new owner completes a homestead application and qualifies. Scott County's Taxation page explains the homestead requirements and takes the application materials. That means a buyer who forgets the application can see a higher tax bill the following year, which is worth mentioning during negotiations.

What should I do first when a Savage house needs to sell quickly?

A short list of local checks saves time once you decide to move.

  • Find your parcel number on the Scott County property information site and print the current tax statement.
  • Confirm which of the three school districts covers the address.
  • Check whether a rental registration is on file with the city and whether any document is waiting to be recorded.
  • Ask a title company or attorney to prepare the deed on a Uniform Conveyancing Blank, since the county does not.

Most Savage homes are lived in by their owners, so many sales are plain family moves. A house with deferred repairs, a tenant or an estate history can still go to a buyer willing to take it in its present condition.

More questions about Savage, MN

Does Savage charge to register a rental property?

No. The city says there is no charge for registering, but registration is mandatory under Title 11, Chapter 121 of the city code.

Which school district serves my Savage house?

It depends on the address, since Prior Lake-Savage District 719, Burnsville-Eagan-Savage District 191 and Shakopee District 720 all cover parts of the city. Contact the districts to confirm before you advertise.

How do I get alerts when a document is recorded on my Savage property?

Sign up for Scott County's Property Watch. It is free and needs only your name, property ID and email address, and it sends an alert when a document with your name and parcel number is recorded.

Can I still appeal my Scott County valuation this year?

The Minnesota Tax Court is the last step, with its cutoff on April 30 of the payable year. The meetings on your value notice come first, so read the notice each spring.

What does the Scott County Land Records office not do?

It does not provide legal forms, help completing them or legal advice. Staff refer people to an attorney or title company and to the state's Uniform Conveyancing Blanks.

Where is Rosemount, Minnesota, and how did it grow?

Twenty miles south of Saint Paul, Rosemount marks the southern fringe of the metro in Dakota County, with the Mississippi River touching its northeast corner. The Census Bureau lists 33.25 square miles of land. About 7 percent of residents lived in rural areas at the 2020 census.

Settlers began arriving after the 1851 Treaty of Mendota. A postmaster appointed in 1854 named the post office after a town in Ireland, and the township was organized in 1858. Dodd Road, one of the state's early roads, crossed the western part of the township, and a railroad station and elevator in the 1860s pulled a commercial center toward the tracks. The village was platted in 1866 and incorporated in 1875.

The 20th century added two large land uses. A wartime gunpowder plant, the Gopher Ordnance Works, was later partly acquired by the University of Minnesota in 1947 and is now known as UMore Park. The Pine Bend refinery, built in 1955 on the border with Inver Grove Heights, is now owned by Flint Hills Resources and is the area's largest private employer.

How big has Rosemount become, and what do Census figures say about its homes?

Growth here has been fast. The Census Bureau's July 1, 2025 estimate is 31,881 residents, which is 24.3 percent above the 2020 base of 25,651 and far above the 21,874 counted in 2010.
