What do the roads, schools and employers mean for a Rosemount seller?

U.S. Highway 52, Minnesota Highways 3 and 55, and County Road 42 are four of the main routes. The Census Bureau puts the average commute at 28.1 minutes, so buyers weigh drive times to Saint Paul, Minneapolis and Dakota County job centers when they look.

Independent School District 196, the Rosemount-Apple Valley-Eagan district, serves the city. Its Rosemount schools include Emerald Trail, Rosemount and Shannon Park elementaries, Rosemount Middle School and Rosemount High School. Dakota County Technical College is also in the city, and Saint Joseph Catholic School and Rosemount First Baptist School are private options.

Transportation and warehousing is a sizable sector here. The Census Bureau's 2022 figures show $271.7 million in transportation and warehousing receipts, compared with $140.8 million in retail sales.

Does Rosemount require a license to rent out a house?

Yes. The City Code requires a rental dwelling license under Title 9-8-4, and the housing official may inspect the property under Title 9-8-8. The city's application asks whether the building is a single-family home, duplex, townhome or multi-family structure, and whether the license is new or a renewal.

  • An owner who rents out properties in other Minnesota cities must list them on the form.
  • A false statement on the application can lead to suspension or revocation.
  • The application lists a fee of $100 per unit when mailed, so call City Hall at 651-322-2024 to confirm the current amount.

For a house sold with a tenant inside, ask City Hall what happens to the license. The city's website now sits at rosemountmn.gov, and City Hall is at 2875 145th Street West.

How are Dakota County values set, and when can a Rosemount owner appeal?

The county says the road from sales data to a final tax bill takes more than three years. Sales from October 1, 2024 through September 30, 2025 formed the basis for the 2026 assessment, which uses a January 2, 2026 market value for taxes payable in 2027. Notices went to every owner in March 2026, and the appeal window ran March through May.

Once the special county board adjourned on June 8, 2026, state law barred Assessing Services from changing the 2026 value. What remains is a Minnesota Tax Court petition, which has an April 30 deadline in the year the tax is payable. The county takes service of petitions at taxpetitions@co.dakota.mn.us or in person in Hastings.

Gather recent sales of similar houses if you plan to question next year's value, and call Assessing Services at 651-438-4200.

What does Dakota County need when a Rosemount deed is recorded?

Recording for Dakota County happens at Property Taxation and Records, 1590 Highway 55, Hastings. The office takes deeds at an appointment or through the mail, and a mailed package needs a cover letter, a stamped return envelope and a daytime phone number. Expect the originals back within one to two weeks.

  • The county lists a $46 fee for an abstract document, plus a $5 conservation fee on instruments where deed tax was paid.
  • Card payments for recordings carry a 2.49 percent service charge.
  • Every transfer deed needs a well disclosure certificate, or one of two statements about wells printed on the deed.

Most Dakota County land is abstract property, which means a title company searches the records at sale. Torrens property instead has a certificate of title. The county's property search shows which type applies to your parcel. Dakota County staff will not help fill in legal forms, so rely on a closing agent or an attorney.

What is the certificate of real estate value?

Minn. Stat. 272.115 requires a certificate of value for any sale over $3,000. The seller, buyer or an agent files it with the Dakota County auditor as the deed is presented, and it reports financing terms and nets out personal property sold along with the house.

The same section blocks homestead classification in the years after a sale when no certificate was filed, so ask your closing agent to confirm it goes in with the deed.

What are the ways to sell a Rosemount house?

The Dakota County paperwork above applies on every route, and three are common in a city like this one.

  • An agent listing suits a ready house and a calendar that allows for showings.
  • A sale handled without an agent leaves the disclosure, certificate of value and well disclosure to the seller.
  • An as-is cash purchase fits a rental, an estate property or a house that needs more work than the owner wants to do.

Whichever route you take, write down material facts for the buyer, learn whether the parcel is abstract or Torrens, and have the closing agent send the deed, well disclosure and certificate of value together.

More questions about Rosemount, MN

Do I need a rental license to sell a house I have been renting out in Rosemount?

The license applies to operating a rental, so ask City Hall at 651-322-2024 what to do with it when the house changes hands. Rosemount's Title 9-8-4 requires the license, and the housing official can inspect under Title 9-8-8.

Is the 2026 Dakota County assessment still open to appeal?

Not through the county, since its special board finished on June 8, 2026. A Tax Court petition stays possible until April 30 of the payable year.

Where do I record a deed for a Rosemount house?

Dakota County Property Taxation and Records in Hastings records it. You can book an appointment, or mail the deed, the fees, a cover letter and a self-addressed stamped envelope to 1590 Highway 55.

What is a well disclosure on a Minnesota deed?

Dakota County wants to know about wells on every parcel that changes hands. The deed travels with a completed certificate and fee, or with a printed sentence saying the seller knows of no wells or that nothing has changed since the last certificate.

When will my next Dakota County property tax statements arrive?

Proposed statements for 2027 go out in November 2026, and the final statements follow in March 2027. The first half is due in May 2027 and the second half in October 2027.

You need one to operate the rental, and the buyer of a rental will ask to see it. Brooklyn Center has licensed rental property since June 1, 1975, and the rule covers any housing that is not owner-occupied, whatever the tax status or whether rent is charged. Short-term rentals such as Airbnb need a rental license too, but an owner-occupied house renting one or more rooms and approved accessory dwelling units do not.

In May 2026 the city adopted a two-year rental license. Every license is now issued for two years and must pass an inspection that uses city codes, the 2018 International Property Maintenance Code and applicable Minnesota codes. Operating without a license is a misdemeanor and can bring administrative citations and fines. If you are selling a licensed rental, give the buyer the license, the inspection results and the lease files and ask the city whether the buyer must apply for a new license.

What if the house is vacant when you sell?

Brooklyn Center requires a vacant building registration, and the fees climb the longer the house sits empty. Residential fees listed on the city's application, revised June 27, 2025, are shown below.

  • Single-family or townhome, vacant up to one year: $595 total ($195 re-occupancy inspection plus $400 registration).
  • Condo, up to one year: $515.
  • Duplex, triplex or fourplex under one owner: $675, $815 or $950.
  • Any residential type vacant one to three years: $1,000 a year.
  • Vacant more than three years: $3,000 a year.

The registration fee can be reduced by up to $300 if the property has no code violations, but you must call 763-569-3330 and meet the inspector on site before applying. The form says the first year of vacancy needs both the registration and a re-occupancy inspection, that sellers must tell buyers about correction orders, and that the buyer can take over responsibility for corrections by contacting the city. The ordinance's purpose is to protect neighborhoods from hazards and blight, and failing to comply is a misdemeanor.

How do utilities and special assessments work at sale?

Brooklyn Center bills water, sanitary sewer, storm drainage, street lights and recycling quarterly, and it generates a final bill when a property is sold. The city says final bills are produced several times a month. Delinquent utility bills are certified to property taxes each year as special assessments, with a $50 certification fee added, so a balance you ignore can follow the parcel onto the buyer's tax bill. The minimum residential bill for 2026 is $227.17 a quarter, or $174.43 with the senior sewer rate.

Special assessments for city projects are paid through the Community Development Department at 763-569-3330 before they roll over to county taxes. Ask that office for a payoff figure, and confirm it with your title company before the closing date.

Who handles assessing, taxes and recording for Brooklyn Center?

Hennepin County does all three, not the city. The county assesses the roughly 8,986 parcels in Brooklyn Center, sets estimated market value and classification, reviews each property in person every five years, and takes homestead applications at its assessor's office at 612-348-3046. A new owner has to file for homestead to receive the reduced taxable value, and the application asks for Social Security numbers of owners who live there and the Certificate of Real Estate Value.

Property tax is due May 15 and October 15, and Hennepin accepts payment online, by mail, at the Government Center or by direct payment. Taxes can be included in a mortgage payment through escrow. For recording, Hennepin County Recorder fees are $46 per document, a well disclosure certificate is $54, and an eCRV is required for deeds with taxable consideration over $3,000. Minnesota Statute 513.55 requires you to give a buyer written disclosure of material facts before the agreement is signed.

More questions about Brooklyn Center, MN

Does Brooklyn Center require an inspection when I sell my home?

Inspections apply to licensed rentals and to vacant buildings, which need a re-occupancy inspection. For an owner-occupied house, call Community Development at 763-569-3330 to confirm whether anything applies to your address.

What does a vacant house cost to register in Brooklyn Center?

A single-family house vacant up to a year costs $595 in total. The fee rises to $1,000 for one to three years and $3,000 beyond three years, and up to $300 can come off the registration with a clean inspection.

Can a buyer take over code violations on a Brooklyn Center house?

Yes, the city's form says buyers can assume responsibility for corrections by contacting the city, and the sellers must tell buyers about correction orders. A buyer must also meet all city codes and the conditions of the approved property plan.

Is an Airbnb in Brooklyn Center covered by the rental license rule?

Yes. The city's rental page says short-term rental properties are required to hold a rental license. Renting out a room in an owner-occupied home is the exception.

Who do I call about homestead after I sell?

The Hennepin County Assessor's office at 612-348-3046 processes homestead for Brooklyn Center. The new owner files a homestead application with the Certificate of Real Estate Value, so give them the sale documents promptly.

Where is Fridley, Minnesota, and what does its housing stock look like?

Fridley is a first-ring suburb in the southern tip of Anoka County, directly north of Minneapolis, with 30,829 residents in the Census Bureau's July 1, 2025 estimate. It became a village in 1949 and a city in 1957, and most of its growth came between 1950 and 1970. That timing means a large share of Fridley's housing dates from the postwar decades.

The city is long from north to south and narrow from east to west, following the Mississippi River and the highways beside it. It borders Minneapolis, Columbia Heights, New Brighton, Mounds View, Spring Lake Park, Blaine, Coon Rapids, Brooklyn Park and Brooklyn Center. Rice Creek crosses the middle of town, and East Moore, West Moore and Locke lakes sit inside the city limits. Land area is about 10.2 square miles.

The area was first called Manomin, after the Ojibwe word for wild rice. John Banfill became the first settler in 1847, and the Legislature renamed the township for Abram Fridley in 1879. East River Road still follows the old Red River oxcart trail.

What do the Census numbers show about Fridley homeowners and renters?

Fridley has a larger share of renters and lower home values than the other three cities in this part of the metro that the Census compares. The Census Bureau lists 63.0 percent of units as owner-occupied and a median value of $302,900 for 2020-2024. That leaves roughly 37 percent of households renting, so investors and landlords are a regular part of the buyer pool.

A median gross rent of $1,326 against median owner costs of $1,793 with a mortgage shows why some owners keep an inherited or outgrown house as a rental before deciding to sell.

Which Fridley city code rules should a seller check before listing?

Fridley enforces exterior and yard standards that a buyer's inspector or the city may flag, so walk the property first. The city's code enforcement page lists the items it sees most often.

  • Grass and weeds taller than an average of ten inches draw a ten-day notice, and the city mows and bills the owner if it is not cut.
  • Driveways must be paved or hard-surfaced, and gravel driveways are not allowed.
  • Garbage, recycling and compost containers belong behind the front setback and may sit at the curb only from 5:00 PM the day before collection to 9:00 PM on collection day.
  • Vehicles parked outside need current tabs and must be street operable, and cars cannot park on grass.
  • Fences top out at four feet in the front yard and seven feet in side and rear yards.

When a violation is not fixed, the city can have a contractor correct it and add the cost to the property's taxes, or issue a citation with court fees of at least $300. An owner can appeal in writing to the City Clerk within 14 business days. Clearing open notices before a buyer's walk-through avoids last-minute credits.

Does a Fridley rental house need a city license when it sells?

Fridley licenses rental property, so a buyer who plans to keep the house as a rental should expect to apply for a license. The city uses two license subtypes: single family covers one to three units, and multi-family covers four or more. Applications go through the CitizenServe portal.

The owner must list a physical address, not a PO box. If the owner lives more than 50 miles from the property, a local contact is required. New owners can upload their purchase documents with the application because the owner shown in the portal comes from Anoka County records, which update every one to two months. Questions go to Fridley rental licensing at 763-572-3616.

If you are selling a rental and want the transaction to move smoothly, bring a copy of the current license certificate and any inspection results to the table.

How do I stop and transfer the Fridley water account at closing?

Tell the city's Utility Billing Division before your closing date, using the Moving In/Out form or by phoning 763-572-3529. Staff need a meter reading on the day of closing to prepare the seller's final bill, and the account switches to the new owner as of that date.

  • Residential water has a fixed charge of $26.01 per quarter plus tiered volume rates in the city's 2026 schedule.
  • Sewer is billed on winter-quarter water use, and recycling is $11.60 per quarter for homes.
  • Weekly garbage service comes from a private hauler licensed by the city, separate from the city bill.

Unpaid utility charges can become a lien and be sent to Anoka County to be collected with next year's property taxes. Notices go out on or before October 1 for balances billed through July 31. A 10 percent late fee can apply to past-due accounts.

What schools, roads and employers draw buyers to Fridley?

Fridley Public Schools, Independent School District 14, run Fridley High School, Fridley Middle School, Hayes Elementary and Stevenson Elementary. Parts of the city fall in other districts: a small northern area is in Anoka-Hennepin District 11, an eastern area is in Columbia Heights District 13, and much of the north-northeast belongs to Spring Lake Park District 16. Check the district for the exact address when you write the listing.

Interstate 694 and Minnesota Highways 47 and 65 are the main roads, and the Northstar commuter rail line stops at the Fridley station. The Medtronic operational headquarters, Unity Medical Center, a Target distribution center and the BNSF Northtown rail yard are among the larger employers and landmarks. Only about 21 percent of residents worked in the city in 2000, and the Census puts the average commute today at 22.6 minutes.

What does recording a Fridley deed cost in Anoka County?

Anoka County records Fridley deeds, and its fee schedule effective July 1, 2025 lists a $46 recording fee for abstract property, a $5 conservation fee and a $54 well certificate. State deed tax is 0.0033 of the net consideration over $3,000. On a sale at Fridley's $302,900 median value, that is about $1,000.

Property tax payments go to Anoka County Property Records and Taxation at 2100 3rd Avenue, Anoka, or online through PayAnokaCounty. The online system adds a 2.6 percent fee for cards and a $3.50 fee for e-checks, while checks and in-person payments at the Government Center carry no fee. State law splits the year's tax into two halves due before May 16 and October 16 (Minnesota Statutes 279.01), so the second half for 2026 has already come due.

More questions about Fridley, MN

Can I sell a Fridley house that has code violations?

Often, yes, but check the notice first. The city can add abatement costs to the property's taxes, and buyers often ask for credits. A cash buyer takes the property as-is, while a retail buyer may ask you to fix flagged items first.

Who do I call to close my Fridley water account?

Call the Fridley Utility Billing Division at 763-572-3529 before closing. The city needs a meter reading on the closing date, and the closing date ends the seller's account and starts the buyer's.

How much is deed tax on a Fridley home sale?

It is 0.0033 of the net sale price once consideration exceeds $3,000. At $302,900, that is roughly $1,000. Anoka County collects it with a $5 conservation fee when the deed is recorded.

Does the buyer of my Fridley rental need a rental license?

The city licenses rentals of one to three units and of four or more units, and a new owner applies through CitizenServe. The owner of record comes from Anoka County, so the application lets new owners upload purchase papers while that record catches up.

Do I have to disclose problems with my Fridley house?

Yes. Before you sign a purchase agreement, Minnesota Statutes 513.55 requires a written disclosure of material facts you know that could significantly affect a buyer's use and enjoyment of the property. The disclosure must be made in good faith.

Sell My House Fast in Oakdale, MN: Options, Costs and Cash Offers

Cash Home Buyers in Minnesota
Cash Offer in 24 Hours

  • No fees, commissions or closing costs on a Oakdale, MN sale
  • Turn the Oakdale, MN offer down and you owe us nothing

Sell Your Oakdale House for Cash

Tell us about your Oakdale house.

Call or Text  (424) 435-2326


Last updated November 14, 2026.

Oakdale at a glance

Selling in Oakdale?
We buy Oakdale houses as-is, with no commission, no repairs and no closing costs to you.
Get My Cash Offer →

Where does an Oakdale owner start when a sale has to close soon?

Start by choosing between an agent listing, a sale you manage yourself, and a cash purchase by a company that takes the house as is. Cash is usually quickest because it skips showings and buyer financing, and it suits a house with repairs, a tenant, or an inherited property that nobody wants to maintain.

Whichever you pick, the deed is recorded in Washington County, the well question has to be answered in writing, and a rented house needs an Oakdale license. Those three points are covered below.

What is Oakdale, and why does location matter to buyers?

Oakdale is a suburb of Saint Paul in Washington County, covering about 11.3 square miles. It is bounded by Highway 120 on the west, County Road 13 on the east, Interstate 694 on the north and Interstate 94 on the south. Highway 36 and Hadley Avenue North cross it as well, and the city calls Hadley its signature street because it runs the full length of town. The 45th parallel, halfway between the Equator and the North Pole, passes along Upper 35th Street North, and it crosses the home plate at Tilsen Park.

The city came together in the 1970s when Oakdale and Northdale Townships consolidated, and it kept annexing land into the 1990s. The whole city lies in the North St. Paul-Maplewood-Oakdale district, ISD 622. Tartan Senior High School is inside city limits and serves the south half, while the north half goes to North High in North St. Paul. Many residents work at 3M, whose headquarters is nearby.

Does the Oakdale Dump Superfund site affect a house sale?

It can matter to a buyer who asks, so be ready to answer. The Environmental Protection Agency lists the Oakdale Dump at North Hadley Avenue and North Granada Avenue as a Superfund site. It covers three separate properties that served as dumps in the late 1940s and 1950s: a 55-acre site, a 5-acre site and a 2-acre site. Waste disposal there contaminated soil and groundwater with hazardous chemicals.

The agency says cleanup has been carried out and that operation and maintenance work continues. After the cleanup, the area was converted into a city park. If your house is near that corner of the city, read the EPA site profile before you list, and keep your private well statement accurate if the property has a well.

What do Census figures show for Oakdale housing?

Oakdale is growing and mostly owner-occupied. The table shows the figures that most often frame a price discussion.

Oakdale at a glance, per Census Bureau QuickFacts (population is the 2025 estimate, the rest are 2020-2024 averages)
TopicResult
Residents30,588, up 8.1% since April 2020
Homes occupied by owners77.5%
Midpoint home value$318,100
Midpoint owner cost with a mortgage$1,793 per month
Midpoint gross rent$1,481 per month
Midpoint household income$93,772

The Bureau counts 11,566 households of about 2.45 people each, and 92.5 percent of residents lived in the same house a year earlier. Workers average a 23.5 minute trip to work, and 35.6 percent of adults 25 or older hold a bachelor's degree or higher. Rentals still exist in town, which is why the city runs a licensing program.

What does the City of Oakdale require for rentals and permits?

The city licenses all rental property, and the license term runs from January 1 to December 31. Applications go through the online permitting portal. Staff review the application, send an email to collect payment, and then schedule an inspection before the license is issued. The housing standard is the current International Property Maintenance Code.

  • Building permits that need no plan review take three business days, and those needing review take ten, according to the city's posted timeline.
  • Inspection requests should be filed five business days ahead of the date you want.
  • Call 811 at least 48 hours before digging a fence post or planting bed.
  • Most Oakdale lots carry an easement, so sheds, play structures and raised beds should stay out of it.

Permit and license records completed after February 6, 2023 can be searched by address on the online portal. The inspections office at 3200 Granada Avenue North answers questions at 651-739-5150, which helps if a buyer asks whether an older deck or addition was permitted.

What must an Oakdale seller say about wells?

Before an agreement to sell real property is signed, Minnesota Statutes section 103I.235 requires the seller to give the buyer a written statement. It says either that the seller knows of no wells, or it gives the legal description, the county and a map, and states whether each well is in use, not in use or sealed.

  • At closing, a well disclosure certificate goes to the county recorder, or the deed carries the no-wells statement.
  • The recorder collects a $54 fee for a completed certificate.
  • Individual condominium units are excluded.
  • A seller who knew or should have known of an undisclosed well can owe the buyer the sealing cost and reasonable attorney fees, if the buyer sues within six years of closing.

Skipping the certificate does not undo the deed between the parties, but a county recorder may not record a deed that lacks either the no-wells statement or the certificate. Settle the answer before the closing table.

How does Washington County handle the deed and the tax bill?

Washington County records real estate documents at the Government Center, 14949 62nd Street North in Stillwater. The county's service chart lists real property records at that building only, while tax payments are accepted at all five service sites, including the Woodbury center at 1261 Woodlane Drive and the Stillwater location. Documents can also be recorded online through state-recognized vendors.

The county's fee table lists $46 for a deed or mortgage, $54 for a well certificate, and a state deed tax of $3.30 per thousand dollars of consideration. On a sale at Oakdale's $318,100 Census median that tax comes to about $1,050. At $3,000 or less in consideration, the deed tax is a flat $1.65.

On the tax side, state law requires half to be paid before May 16 and the rest before October 16. A late first or second half adds a penalty of 2 percent on homestead property or 4 percent on nonhomestead property, with a matching increase the next month and 1 percent more each month through December. The cap is 8 percent for homestead and 12 percent for other property.

  • Property Watch is a free email alert that tells you when a document is recorded under your name.
  • Racial covenants still found in old deeds can be discharged for free.
  • A tax parcel split needs all taxes paid in full, plus surveys and deeds bearing city approval stamps.

What should I confirm with a cash buyer for an Oakdale house?

Ask for the terms in writing and check each of these against the Oakdale and Washington County steps above.

  • Who completes the well statement or certificate, and who pays the $54 recording charge?
  • If the house is licensed as a rental, who finishes the current license year and how is any tenant handled?
  • Whether unpermitted work such as a deck, fence or finished basement will change the price or delay the closing.
  • The amount you receive after the deed tax and any unpaid taxes are paid at closing.

A short written list keeps the closing on schedule, and it gives you a plain way to compare a cash offer with a listing that would take months.

More questions about Oakdale, MN

Do I need a license before renting out my Oakdale house?

Yes. Oakdale licenses all rental property for a January 1 to December 31 term. You apply on the online permitting portal, pay when the city emails you, and pass an inspection.

How long does Oakdale take to review a building permit?

Three business days when no plan review is needed, and ten when it is. The city posted that timeline because of heavy workload, so call 651-739-5150 to confirm it before you schedule closing-related repairs.

What happens if I forget to disclose a well on my property?

You may owe the buyer the cost of sealing it plus reasonable attorney fees, when you knew or had reason to know of the well and the buyer sues within six years. The deed itself stays valid.

How much extra do I pay if my Washington County tax is late?

A homestead payment takes a 2 percent penalty right away and the total is capped at 8 percent, while nonhomestead property starts at 4 percent and is capped at 12 percent. A mailed payment postmarked within one business day of the due date can have the penalty abated once.

Is the Oakdale Dump a reason to avoid buying near Hadley Avenue?

That is for each buyer to decide with the facts in hand. The EPA reports that cleanup occurred and ongoing maintenance continues, and the area was converted into a city park afterward. Share the EPA profile if a buyer asks.

Selling in Chaska?

How do you sell a house fast in Chaska, MN?

Selling fast in Chaska means choosing a buyer who does not depend on a lender: an investor or cash buyer who purchases as-is. A conventional listing usually brings a higher price but takes longer, and selling without an agent leaves the paperwork to you.

  • Choose a listing when the house is in showing condition and the calendar is flexible.
  • Choose a private sale when you already know who will buy.
  • Choose a cash sale when the house needs repairs, comes with tenants, or is part of an estate that has to settle.

Chaska has several housing types to sell: detached houses, townhomes and duplexes, apartments and condominiums, and homes in manufactured home parks. Each has its own buyers, so match the sale route to the type of home you own.

What is Chaska, and how did it grow?

Chaska is the county seat of Carver County, about 21 miles southwest of Minneapolis, with downtown on the Minnesota River. The city covers 17.77 square miles, 16.97 of them land. Chaska Boulevard, Pioneer Trail, U.S. Highway 212 and Minnesota Highway 41 are the main routes, and the Highway 212 freeway carries a bus rapid transit route toward the Twin Cities.

Treaty land opened to settlement in 1851, and the townsite was platted in 1857. Local clay started a brick industry that same year, and Guardian Angels Catholic Church in town was built of the yellow Chaska brick. The city incorporated as a village in 1871 and as a city in 1891. The railway arrived in 1873. Population averaged about 2,000 through the first half of the twentieth century, then the 1966 Jonathan new town design brought land, jobs and people. Hazeltine National Golf Club, which hosted the 2016 Ryder Cup and was announced as the site of a second in 2028, is part of the local identity, as is the Chaska Curling Center. It opened in December 2015 and was named a USA Curling National Training Center in 2018, which brings visitors to the downtown restaurants and shops.

What kinds of homes does Chaska have?

Detached single-family houses make up the largest share of Chaska's housing, and townhome and apartment growth since 2010 has been modest. The city's 2040 comprehensive plan tracks the stock by type.

Chaska housing units by type, 2010 and 2017
Type20102017
Single-family detached4,9685,700
Single-family attached1,6051,699
Manufactured homes682669
Multi-family2,0352,227
Total9,29010,295

The plan adds that just over 25% of homes were built before 1980, about 8% before 1960, and more than 40%, some 4,132 units, since 2000. The manufactured homes sit mainly in two parks. In 2018 the Metropolitan Council counted 68.6% of units owner-occupied and 27.6% rented.

What do current Census figures say about Chaska?

Chaska's July 2025 population estimate is 30,513, a gain of 9.7% over the 2020 census count, the fastest growth among the four cities in this comparison. Median value of owner-occupied homes is $404,700 for 2020-2024.

  • Owner-occupied rate: 67.6%.
  • Median gross rent: $1,553 a month.
  • Median household income: $110,956, with 11,051 households averaging 2.58 people.
  • Persons in poverty: 5.8%.
  • Bachelor's degree or higher: 46.6% of adults 25 and older.
  • Mean travel time to work: 23.0 minutes.

The 2020 count showed 10,788 housing units with 3.2% vacant and a rental vacancy rate of 4.0%, the tightest rental market of the cities compared where a 2020 figure was available.

Which schools serve Chaska homes?

Chaska belongs to Eastern Carver County Schools, Independent School District 112. Elementary schools in the city include Clover Ridge, Jonathan and La Academia Spanish Immersion. Chaska Middle School East, Chaska Middle School West and Pioneer Ridge Middle School are the district's middle schools, and Chaska High School is the city's high school. Southwest Christian High School is a private option, along with church-affiliated grade schools such as St. John's Lutheran and Guardian Angels Catholic School.

All of Chaska is in the one district, so the district name in a listing does not change from street to street. Two of the middle schools, Chaska Middle School East and West, share the city's name, while Pioneer Ridge Middle School also draws Chanhassen students.

What does Chaska require of rental homes?

Every rental dwelling in Chaska must be licensed with the city and pass an initial inspection, a program run by the Chaska Fire Department's Bureau of Fire Prevention. Annual license renewal is due in January, and inspections repeat every two years after the first one. To book one, owners, managers and tenants can call 952-227-7458 during the posted Monday, Wednesday and Thursday windows.

Inspectors look at wiring and safety items that a house can fix before sale:

  • Extension cords may power portable appliances only, and multi-plug adapters or daisy-chained power strips are prohibited.
  • Smoke alarms must work, and a carbon monoxide alarm must be within 10 feet of each sleeping room.
  • Handrails are needed on steps with three or more risers, and guardrails on porches more than 30 inches above grade.
  • Each unit needs a fire extinguisher rated 1-A:10:B:C or better, and bedrooms need egress windows.

The city also grants transient accommodation licenses; a council approval in August 2025 shows the license can carry conditions such as an occupancy certificate and payment of outstanding utility bills. Ask city licensing staff if you are thinking about short stays.

How do building permits work in Chaska?

Chaska's Building Inspections Department enforces the state building code. Permits that do not require plan review, including roofing, siding, window and door replacement, plumbing, mechanical and fireplace work, are filed online through the SmartGov portal. Permits that need plan review go by email to inspections@chaskamn.gov as PDFs, and inspections are scheduled at 952-448-9395. Counter hours at One City Hall Plaza run 8 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. on weekdays.

If you replaced a roof or windows recently, keep the permit and the final inspection record. A buyer's inspector or title agent may ask for them.

How is a Chaska deed recorded?

Deeds go to Carver County Land Records and Vitals at 600 East 4th Street in Chaska, which is also the county seat's recording office. The counter is open Monday to Friday, 8:00 to 4:30, and the phone is 952-361-1930. The Minnesota deed tax is 0.33% of the net consideration under section 287.21, collected when the deed is presented for recording. On a sale at the city's $404,700 median value, that is about $1,336.

The county also collects a $5 agricultural conservation fee, requires a certificate of real estate value for sales over $3,000, well information, and the sewage treatment disclosure on every transfer. Property tax questions go to 952-361-1910, and assessment and homestead questions go to 952-361-1960.

More questions about Chaska, MN

Can I sell a Chaska manufactured home quickly?

Yes, but the buyer pool differs from detached houses, and park rules and financing can slow a conventional sale. Ask the park operator what its resale rules require before you set a closing date.

Does Chaska inspect rentals before I sell a landlord property?

Yes. Licensed rentals pass an initial inspection and are reinspected every two years, with renewal due each January. Have the latest inspection report ready for any buyer who will keep tenants.

Which county handles recording for a Chaska house?

Carver County. Land Records and Vitals at 600 East 4th Street, Chaska, takes the deed, deed tax, conservation fee, certificate of real estate value and disclosures.

Are there Chaska permits I should check before listing?

What is the fastest way to sell a house in Ramsey, MN?

The fastest route is a direct sale to a buyer who accepts the house in its present state, because it skips showings, repair negotiations and a lender's appraisal. A listing with an agent takes longer but reaches the widest group of buyers, and a sale you run yourself sits between the two.

Ramsey is a suburb in Anoka County about 22 miles north-northwest of downtown Minneapolis. U.S. Highways 10 and 169, which share a roadway here, and State Highway 47 are its main routes. The city covers 28.85 square miles of land, and much of it is less dense than the inner suburbs, with about 958 people per square mile. Many Ramsey houses are not on city sewer, and the city says about 4,200 private septic systems operate within its limits. That matters at sale time, as a later section explains.

  • Direct sale: no repairs asked of you, a closing date you set, and a price that reflects the work.
  • Agent listing: more exposure, plus preparation, showings and the buyer's financing timeline.
  • Selling alone: you save the commission and handle every form and negotiation yourself.

What do the Census Bureau figures say about Ramsey homeowners?

Ramsey is growing and family-heavy. Census figures put Ramsey at 29,624 residents in mid-2025, a rise of 7.2% over the April 2020 base of 27,636, and the city had 27,646 people in the 2020 count.

About 85% of homes are lived in by their owners, and the typical household has 2.66 people. Owners put the middle home's value at $359,600 for 2020 to 2024, while median gross rent is $1,826. Median household income is $116,415, and the average commute to work is 28.2 minutes. About 26% of residents are under 18. Some 92% of residents stayed in the same house for a full year.

If your Ramsey house has a big lot, a finished lower level or a three-car garage, put those points first in your listing or your pitch to a direct buyer.

Does Ramsey require a septic inspection before I sell?

Yes, if the house is on a private septic system. Ramsey City Code section 113-23 requires a compliance inspection on any sale or transfer of property served by an individual sewage treatment system. The city administers Minnesota Rules Chapter 7080 and says about 4,200 of these systems operate within its limits.

  • An MPCA-certified inspector must perform the inspection and report on the state's approved form. City inspectors cannot do it.
  • You give the buyer a Certificate of Compliance at or before closing, and a copy of the inspection goes to the city's Building Division within 15 days.
  • If the sale falls between November 1 and April 30 and the inspection cannot be completed, the seller and buyer may agree in writing that it will be finished by the following June 1.
  • A system that fails normally has to be brought into compliance within 12 months.

Recent pumping does not replace the inspection, since pumping only addresses the tank and the inspector examines the entire system, including the drainfield. Each sale needs a new inspection even if you had one last year. Ask the Building Division at 763-433-9850 for the point-of-sale handout.

Owners of these systems also check for leaks and measure sludge and scum accumulations at least once every three years, and the city requires a septic pumping permit each time a tank is pumped. Keeping those permits and pumping records in a folder gives the inspector and the buyer a clear history of the system.

What should I know if my Ramsey house is a rental?

All residential rental properties in Ramsey must be licensed every year. Single-family rentals are inspected every three years, and multi-family buildings every year, against the 2021 International Property Maintenance Code, the city's rental code and its zoning code.

An inspection takes between 15 minutes and an hour. The inspector checks heating, plumbing and electrical systems, doors and windows, and exterior upkeep such as mowing, debris and vehicle licensing. A property that fails gets a correction list, and the license fee covers one follow-up visit. A third visit on the same issue can cost a $150 reinspection fee.

Two exceptions come up in sales. A house rented to a relative needs no license if it qualifies for Relative Homesteading with the Anoka County Assessor and you have applied for it. A contract for deed avoids licensing only if it is recorded with Anoka County and requires real principal payments, because an interest-only contract is treated as a rental. If you are selling with a tenant in place, give the buyer the latest inspection report and the license dates.

City utility accounts are another loose end. A tenant may hold the account in a tenant's name, but the property owner stays responsible for any unpaid balance, and bills arrive quarterly. Bring the account current before closing, and call Utility Billing at 763-576-4343 if you need to add a second name or fix the billing address.

Which Anoka County charges apply when a Ramsey deed is recorded?

Anoka County's Land Records office records the deed. Its fee schedule, effective July 1, 2025, lists the following charges that apply to a typical sale.

Anoka County recording charges for a house sale (fees effective July 1, 2025)

Attested copy$2.00

The county also asks for a completed electronic certificate of real estate value, an eCRV number on the deed and a "send tax statements to" line naming the buyer. Any delinquent taxes have to be cleared before a transfer, and a split of a tax parcel requires current-year taxes to be paid. Instead of the $54 well certificate, a deed may carry the statement that the seller does not know of any wells on the property. Minnesota Statutes section 103I.235 sets that rule, and section 513.55 requires your written disclosure to the buyer before the purchase agreement is signed.

Where did Ramsey come from, and who serves its schools?

Thomas Holmes and James Beatty built the Old Log Trading Post here in 1849, and Itasca Village was platted in 1852 with the first post office in Anoka County. The area became a township, was renamed Dover and then Ramsey, and the city incorporated on November 12, 1974 with about 8,000 people. Ramsey borders Andover, Anoka, Nowthen, Oak Grove, Dayton and Elk River.

Two school districts serve the city, Elk River and Anoka-Hennepin, and PACT Charter School operates inside Ramsey. Confirm which district applies to your address before you print a school name in an advertisement.

More questions about Ramsey, MN

Do I need a septic inspection if I sell my Ramsey house in winter?

Yes, but the timing can shift. For sales between November 1 and April 30, the seller and buyer can close and agree that the inspection will be completed by the following June 1, if the inspection cannot be completed.

Who can perform a Ramsey point-of-sale septic inspection?

Only an MPCA-licensed septic inspector. City inspectors do not perform these inspections, and the seller gives the buyer the Certificate of Compliance at or before closing.

Does a contract for deed make my Ramsey property a rental?

It can. If the contract is recorded with Anoka County and sets reasonable principal payments, the city does not require a rental license. An unrecorded or interest-only contract is treated as a rental.

What are the recording charges for a Ramsey deed?

Anoka County charges $46 to record a deed and $5 as a conservation fee, plus state deed tax of the net price times 0.0033. A well certificate costs $54 unless the deed carries the no-wells statement.

What is Ramsey's current population?

The Census Bureau's July 2025 estimate is 29,624, a gain of 7.2% over the April 2020 base. The 2020 census counted 27,646.

How do I sell my house in Prior Lake, MN?

A Prior Lake owner can go to market with an agent, handle the sale alone, or sell directly to a home-buying company. Which one makes sense usually comes down to condition, timing and whether the house sits on the water.

The city lies about 20 miles southwest of Minneapolis in Scott County, beside Savage and Shakopee. Wikipedia calls it an exurban city on the south-southwest fringe of the Twin Cities area and credits the upgraded State Highway 13 for easy commuting. A well-kept house on a street near the lakes usually does fine on the open market. A house with a failing roof, an estate attached or a tenant who will not leave tends to suit a direct sale, where the buyer accepts the property in its present state and you pick the closing day.

  • Listing with an agent: broad reach, but you prepare the house and wait for a buyer's lender.
  • Selling it yourself: you keep the commission and take on the contract work.
  • Direct sale: little prep, a quick closing, and an offer that accounts for repairs.

What do the Census numbers show about Prior Lake homeowners?

Prior Lake is a family-and-owner city. About 86 of every 100 homes are lived in by the people who own them, and the typical household has 2.79 people. The Census Bureau's QuickFacts page gives the following picture.

The city's estimated population reached 28,140 on July 1, 2025, up 1.9% from the 2020 base of 27,616. Households earned a median of $134,255 over 2020 to 2024. Owners put the middle home's worth at $450,700, and renters paid a median of $1,654. Some 91% of residents were in the same home a year earlier. The city covers 16.31 square miles of land, which works out to roughly 1,693 people per square mile.

Those figures describe a settled, family-oriented city where most households have owned for some time.

Can I rent out a Prior Lake house, and what does that mean for a sale?

Prior Lake permits only rentals of at least 60 days and no more than 180 days in its residential districts. Rentals shorter than 60 days are prohibited there, and a permit with a $250 application fee is required for the permitted range.

The rules live in City Code Sections 4-380 through 4-388. A permit expires each December 31 and cannot move to a new owner or a different dwelling, so a buyer of your house cannot inherit it. A named local agent who lives and works within 30 miles has to answer calls around the clock while the home is rented, and the dwelling must have off-street parking equal to the number of bedrooms. At most two restricted watercraft may be moored at the property. The ordinance caps overnight guests by lot size and floor area:

Overnight occupant limits for Prior Lake short-term rentals (City Code 4-384)
Lot sizeMain building under 1,500 sq ft1,500 to under 2,000 sq ft2,000 sq ft or more
One-half acre or more6812
Under one-half acre468

Children under three do not count toward these totals. A seller with a tenant under lease should pass along the lease and the permit file, and explain that the permit ends with the seller's ownership.

Which city rules can trip up a Prior Lake seller?

The Code Enforcement Division enforces a long list of ordinances, and several of them come up while a house is being readied for the market. Fixing these items before a buyer's inspection saves you from last-minute credits.

  • Grass and weeds: growth taller than 12 inches is unlawful during the April 1 to November 1 growing season.
  • Snow on sidewalks: owners must clear public sidewalks within 48 hours after a snowfall ends.
  • Junk vehicles and debris: unlicensed or inoperable vehicles must be inside a building, and piles of boards or tires count as nuisances.
  • Recreational equipment: winter equipment may sit by the driveway from November 1 to April 1, and summer equipment from April to November 1, if licensed and operable.
  • Driveways and decks: replacing or widening a driveway takes a permit, and structures need a building permit.

Work near the shore carries lower limits. Moving more than 10 cubic yards of material, or disturbing more than 500 square feet, on steep slopes or in the bluff, shore impact or shoreland zones needs approval, while the threshold elsewhere is 50 cubic yards. A person who skips a required permit and applies afterward pays double the stated fee. Call Code Enforcement at 952-447-9811 before you start any project you plan to disclose or finish ahead of a sale.

What is special about Prior Lake's lakes and neighborhoods?

Prior Lake takes its name from two connected lakes. Lower Prior Lake covers about 810 acres and Upper Prior Lake about 354, linked by a navigable channel under Eagle Creek Avenue. Spring Lake, 290 acres, lies partly within the city along Scott County Road 12. Together they make Prior Lake the largest lake in the southern metro, and the water is the reason many buyers look here.

Lakefront and lake-access homes are priced as a separate market from interior streets. Zebra mussel shells were found on the lower lake's shore in 2009, and the Department of Natural Resources confirmed the mussels in the upper lake as well, so lake-property buyers sometimes ask about docks, lifts and invasive species. The city was incorporated as a village in 1891, one of the older cities in the south metro.

Schools are run by Prior Lake-Savage Area Schools. Two private options, St. Michael Catholic School and St. Paul's Lutheran School, also serve families in the city.

What does Scott County require when a Prior Lake house closes?

Scott County's Land Records Department records deeds, mortgages, assignments, releases and satisfactions. It reviews each document for recordable form, but its staff cannot supply legal forms or advice, so use your title company or an attorney.

Under Minnesota Statutes section 513.55, you hand the buyer a signed statement of known defects ahead of the purchase agreement. Section 103I.235 adds a well statement on or with the deed. Sales above $3,000 also need a value certificate filed with the county, and the county and state websites list the deed tax rate and recording fees.

Scott County offers a free Property Watch alert that emails you whenever a document is recorded under your name and parcel number. Sign up before you sell if you want a record of when the deed lands. The county assessor values each parcel as of January 2, mails a notice each March, and does not count bank sales, short sales, foreclosures, auctions or sales between relatives in its sales analysis. Appraisers also walk about 11,000 parcels a year, so every property is viewed at least once every five years. The second half of 2026 property tax was due October 15, so confirm it was paid before you close.

More questions about Prior Lake, MN

Can I rent my Prior Lake house by the weekend?

No. Prior Lake prohibits rentals shorter than 60 days in every residential district. The city permits stays of 60 to 180 days with a permit and a $250 fee.

Does a short-term rental permit transfer to a buyer?

No. The permit cannot be transferred to another person or another dwelling, and it expires each December 31. A buyer who wants to rent the house must apply separately.

Which pre-sale fixes in Prior Lake need a city permit?

Building work, driveway replacement or widening, and some grading near the shore all need city permits. Starting without one means applying afterward at double the fee.

Where does a Prior Lake deed get recorded?

The Scott County Land Records Department does. Your title company normally handles the filing.

What is the sidewalk snow deadline in Prior Lake?

Forty-eight hours after the snowfall ends. Do not push snow into the street. Keep the walk clear while the house is listed, because showings continue all winter.

Where does Elk River sit relative to Minneapolis and St. Cloud?

Sherburne County's seat is Elk River, roughly 34 miles northwest of Minneapolis and 37 miles southeast of St. Cloud, at the point where the Elk River empties into the Mississippi. The city covers 42.33 square miles of land, far more than the compact suburbs closer in, so a house here may sit in town, near the river or on a larger lot toward the edge.

As of July 2025 the Census Bureau estimates 27,896 residents, which is 8.0 percent above the 25,840 counted for the 2020 base. That is a faster pace than the Census shows for Eden Prairie or Faribault, so the city is adding residents.

  • U.S. 10 and U.S. 169 meet here and run together for about 12 miles toward Anoka.
  • Minnesota Highway 101 links the city to Interstate 94, about seven miles south.
  • Many residents commute to the Twin Cities, and the average trip to work takes 27.4 minutes.

What does the Elk River housing market look like in the Census numbers?

Survey data covering 2020 through 2024 put the typical Elk River owner-occupied house at $370,100. Four in five households, 79.2 percent, own. Renters pay about $1,283 a month, and household income lands near $108,741. The city has 9,835 households of about 2.66 people each.

Children under 18 are 24.8 percent of residents. Owners with a mortgage spend a median $2,075 a month, while owners with no mortgage spend $796. That $1,283 rent figure is the yardstick if you are thinking about keeping the property as a rental.

How did Elk River grow, and which schools do buyers mention?

The city was platted in 1865 and replatted in 1868, incorporated as a village in 1881 and reincorporated as a city in 1911. Its location at the river junction and on the old Red River Trail made it a trading point first. The city's water tower won a National Register listing in 2012.

The public schools belong to Independent School District 728. Wikipedia lists Elk River High School, Ivan Sand Community High School, Spectrum High School, the Salk and VandenBerge middle schools and four named elementary schools. St. Andrew's Catholic School and Solid Rock Christian Academy are private options. When you describe your house, mention the school district number, since parents search by it.

Does Elk River's climate affect how I should prepare my house?

It affects what inspectors and buyers look at. Wikipedia's 1981 to 2010 climate table lists 31.9 inches of annual precipitation, about 39.5 inches of snowfall, January afternoon highs near 23 degrees and an all-time low of minus 40.

That is a long heating season. Roof, attic insulation, furnace age and any ice-dam or basement-water episodes are the questions to expect, so pull your service records first. They help whichever way you sell.

What disclosures does Minnesota require when I sell in Elk River?

Before the purchase agreement is signed, you must disclose material facts you know under Section 513.55. Separate rules cover radon (144.496), wells (103I.235) and sewage (115.55, subdivision 6).

The sewage rule is worth reading if your Elk River property is not on city sewer. You must say whether sewage goes to a permitted facility. If it does not, the disclosure must describe the system, include a map as far as practicable, note any abandoned system and attach any prior inspection report. A seller who knew of a problem and failed to disclose can be liable for the cost of bringing a system into compliance, with a two-year window for the buyer to sue.

The Minnesota statute also says a certificate of compliance for an existing septic system is valid for three years, which can matter if you have a recent inspection.

What are Elk River's rules for rentals and permits?

The city requires a license for every rental dwelling, including single-family houses, and licenses must be renewed and inspected annually. The rule that matters at a sale is Section 30-198 of the city code: a rental license is nontransferable and ends automatically within 30 days after closing unless the new owner applies for and receives a license.

A house you rent on a platform like Airbnb needs a rental license when you are not on site with the guests. Renting a room does not need one if the owner and no more than two tenants share all living space. The Rental Dwelling Licensing Division is at 763-635-1075.

For repairs, the city says a shed over 200 square feet needs a permit and permits lapse after 180 days without work or inspections. Residential permits that need plan review take about one to two weeks, and over-the-counter permits for roofing, siding or windows usually issue in one to two business days. The city's FAQ adds that an owner who intends to sell needs a state contractor license when performing work on more than one property in a two-year period. Elk River also says buyers can examine its permit records.

Elk River rental dwelling license fees, posted by the City of Elk River
License typeFee

Multi-unit, new license$150 per building
Multi-unit, yearly$100 per building plus $10 per unit

Reinstatement after suspension or revocation$1,500

How do Sherburne County taxes and recording work when I sell?

Sherburne County's auditor-treasurer collects tax on real estate in two halves, falling on May 15 and October 15, and it applies the postmark to penalty decisions. Farm property pays in May and November instead. Questions go to 763-765-4350.

The recorder's office is at 13880 Business Center Drive NW in Elk River, phone 763-765-4420. Recording a deed brings the state deed tax of 0.33 percent of net consideration (Section 287.21), plus a value certificate for any sale over $3,000 (Section 272.115). Your purchase agreement decides which side covers each.

Which sale routes are open to an Elk River owner?

  • Agent listing: reaches the widest group of buyers, takes weeks, and may involve repair requests after the buyer's inspection.
  • Private sale: you handle pricing, showings, disclosures and the contract.
  • Cash sale as is: the buyer takes the property exactly as it stands today, which can suit a rental with a license problem, a house needing roof or furnace work, or an inherited property.

Request a written net-proceeds estimate from each route so the comparison is fair.

More questions about Elk River, MN

What is the timeline for an Elk River sale?

Condition, price and financing drive it. A listing waits on showings and a buyer's loan, while a cash buyer can close as soon as title is ready. The Sherburne County recorder files the deed afterward.

What happens to my rental license when I sell in Elk River?

It ends. Elk River's code says a rental dwelling license cannot be transferred and terminates within 30 days of closing unless the new owner applies for and is granted one. Report the sale to the Rental Dwelling Licensing Division at 763-635-1075.

Do I need to disclose my septic system?

If the property has one, yes. Minnesota requires you to state in writing whether sewage goes to a permitted facility, and for a private system to describe it, show where it is and attach any earlier inspection report.

When are Sherburne County property taxes due?

Real estate pays in two halves, on May 15 and October 15, and farm property on May 15 and November 15. The county counts the postmark, so mail early. Call 763-765-4350 for payment options.

Can I sell an Elk River house that failed a rental inspection?

Yes, as is, with open violations disclosed to the buyer. The city accepts written extension requests before the abate-by date on a notice, and the licensing division at 763-635-1075 can list what is outstanding.

What are your options for selling a house fast in Shoreview?

Shoreview sellers can go through an agent, find a buyer privately, or accept a cash offer for the house in its present condition. The right pick depends on how much work the house needs and how soon you must close.

Shoreview is a mature suburb. The city had 25,043 residents in 2010 and 26,921 at the 2020 count, and the Census Bureau's July 2025 estimate of 26,906 shows almost no change since. Growth has been flat for years, so most sales are of existing houses.

  • List with an agent when the house is clean, updated and you can accept showings for several weeks.
  • Sell directly when you already have a buyer in mind and can handle the purchase agreement and disclosures.
  • Choose cash when the house needs work, is a rental, sits in an estate, or you need a firm closing date.

What is Shoreview like for a seller?

Shoreview is a second-ring suburb north of Saint Paul in Ramsey County, incorporated as a city on April 23, 1957. It has seven lakes, led by Turtle Lake, Snail Lake, Lake Owasso and Island Lake, and Rice Creek crosses the northwest corner. Interstate 35W, Interstate 694 and County Highway 96 are its main routes (Wikipedia).

The city covers 10.77 square miles of land, about 2,500 people per square mile. Two school districts serve it, Mounds View (District 621) and Roseville (District 623), so a buyer's school assignment depends on which side of the district line a house sits.

Shoreview has nine city parks and three county parks, and the Shamrock Park site was a rest stop for travelers as early as the late 1840s. The city's 2025 year in review shows what is being built around you. Nearly 2,000 permits were issued through September 30, with more than $36.5 million in construction value, including the Seven Lakes office buildings and several new apartment projects such as the Aloma Apartments, the third building beside Emrik and Loden SV. The city also approved the subdivision of a former apple orchard into 13 single-family homes, and it is rewriting its development code, with changes on grading and erosion control and on ground-mounted solar arrays.

Which Shoreview city rules matter before you sell?

Shoreview's permit and rental rules decide how much cleanup a sale needs. Any open or missing permit is easier to settle before a buyer's inspection than after.

  • Permits: contractors apply online for residential roofing, siding, windows, doors, electrical, mechanical and plumbing work. Homeowners email applications to permits@shoreviewmn.gov or bring them to City Hall.
  • Plan review: permits that need plan review typically take up to 10 working days.
  • Smaller jobs: fences, driveways, patios and sheds of 200 square feet or less go through Community Development at 651-490-4680.
  • Safety items: the city publishes handouts for decks, egress windows, finished basements, smoke alarms and carbon monoxide alarms.

If a sale involves a lake lot or a sloped yard, ask Community Development whether the erosion and sediment control handout applies to your project, since the city is updating its grading standards. Overnight street parking is not allowed from 2 to 5 a.m. A permit covers up to seven days and five vehicles, which helps during a move-out, though dumpsters and storage pods may not sit on the street.

Does Shoreview license rental houses, and what happens when one is sold?

Yes. Every rental property in Shoreview needs a rental license, and the city issues one only when the unit meets city regulations and municipal utility bills and real estate taxes are paid in full. The city lists more than 600 rental locations.

There are three license types: a general dwelling license for a single-family home with an inspection every other year, a short-term rental license for stays of 30 days or less with an annual inspection and extra parking rules, and a multiple dwelling license for four or more units. Licenses expire December 31 and renew each year. The 2025 year in review notes the city began licensing short-term rentals and inspected over 300 rental homes that year (City of Shoreview).

If you sell a rented house, the city provides a form to void the license once the property is sold. Settle that, and any unpaid utility bill, at the closing table so the next owner starts clean.

How do Ramsey County notices and records affect a Shoreview sale?

Ramsey County sends two mailings each year. The first arrives in mid-March and holds the tax statement, which shows both half-year amounts, plus a notice of valuation and classification that sets next year's taxes. The second comes in November and lists proposed taxes and the dates of levy and budget meetings.

The county's Property Tax Services office is at 90 Plato Boulevard West in Saint Paul, reachable at 651-266-2222. Deeds and mortgages are recorded with the Ramsey County Recorder and Registrar of Titles at 651-266-2050. The office does not help complete legal forms, and a recorded document is permanent, so have the deed reviewed before it goes in.

  • Ask Property Tax Services for the amount due on both halves of the current year.
  • Ask the Recorder which document types the sale needs, since fees and requirements differ by document.
  • For an estate sale, confirm who has authority to sign before scheduling the closing.
  • Watch the November mailing: it previews next year's taxes and the budget meetings where residents can comment, which a buyer may ask about.

More questions about Shoreview, MN

How fast can a Shoreview house sell for cash?

A cash sale can close in a few weeks when the title is clear, since there is no lender underwriting to wait on. A lien, an unpaid utility bill or an unsettled estate can lengthen that. In a suburb where about four in five homes are owner-occupied, a seller who is renting out the house should also settle the tenant's move-out date first.

Does Shoreview require a rental license for a single-family house?

Yes. A single-family rental needs a general dwelling rental license, which includes an inspection every other year, and the license renews each December 31. The city issues it only when utility bills and real estate taxes are paid in full.

What happens to a Shoreview rental license when I sell?

You can void the license with the city's form once the property has sold. Doing it promptly stops renewal notices and shows the city the unit changed hands. The city's rental license page lists the fee schedule on page 2 of its PDF if you need to check what a license cost.

When does Ramsey County mail property tax notices?

The tax statement and value notice go out in mid-March, and the proposed tax notice arrives in November. The statement shows the first and second half amounts for the year.

Is a permit needed to fix up a Shoreview house before listing?

Often yes. Roofing, siding, windows, doors, electrical, mechanical and plumbing work all need permits, and fences, driveways and small sheds go through zoning. Call building inspections at 651-490-4683 to confirm before starting.

Sell My House Fast in Austin, MN: Options, Costs and Cash Offers

Cash Home Buyers in Minnesota

  • Austin, MN: inherited, behind on payments, tenants or repairs, we buy the house as-is
  • No fees, commissions or closing costs on a Austin, MN sale

Sell Your Austin House for Cash

Tell us about your Austin house.

Call or Text  (424) 435-2326


Last updated November 14, 2026.

Austin at a glance

Selling in Austin?
We buy Austin houses as-is, with no commission, no repairs and no closing costs to you.
Get My Cash Offer →

How fast can you sell a house in Austin, MN?

Speed in Austin depends on the route you pick and on how clean the paperwork is. A cash buyer can close in a matter of weeks, while a listing runs on the buyer's lender and inspection calendar. Austin, population 26,689, is the seat of Mower County in southeast Minnesota, so most of the paperwork runs through the Mower County offices on First Street NE.

Before any buyer walks through, a seller can shorten the timeline by sorting out four things: the permit history of the house, the property tax status, any city charges tied to the parcel, and whether the lot sits in an area that flooded in the past. The sections below cover each of them with the Austin and Mower County rules in mind.

  • Sell on the open market and wait for financing and appraisal.
  • Sell privately to a neighbor, relative or investor and handle the paperwork yourself.
  • Accept a cash offer from a buyer who takes the house with every repair left to them.

What is Austin like, and who looks at houses there?

Austin is a meatpacking and healthcare town on the Cedar River, and its buyers are mostly local workers, first-time purchasers and investors. The town was platted in the spring of 1856, became a village in 1868 and a city in 1871. It grew around mills on the river, then around the butcher shop George Hormel opened in 1891, which became Hormel Foods.

Hormel is still the largest employer, and the city is known as SPAM Town USA because the corporate headquarters, a SPAM plant and the Spam Museum are all here. The Hormel Institute, a University of Minnesota cancer research center, is also in town. Austin Public Schools (ISD 492) and Riverland Community College are other large employers, and the hospital is part of Mayo Clinic Health System.

Geography matters for a seller as well. Austin is about 41 miles southwest of Rochester, 20 miles east of Albert Lea and 12 miles north of the Iowa line, with Interstate 90 on the east side. Those distances shape who answers a listing here: people tied to the plant, the hospital and the college, plus investors who look at small-town rents.

How do Austin's housing figures look?

Austin's typical owner-occupied home is valued at $163,900, far below the figures in the Twin Cities suburbs. The table lists the figures a seller is most likely to compare against an offer.

Austin city, Minnesota, Census Bureau QuickFacts (2020-2024 estimates unless noted)
MeasureAustin
Residents (2025 estimate)26,689
Change since April 2020 base1.9%
Typical home value (owner-occupied)$163,900
Owner-occupied housing rate71.5%
Median gross rent$953
Households10,110
Median household income$68,057
Average commute18.0 minutes
Land area13.33 square miles

Source: Census Bureau QuickFacts for Austin. The same-house rate is 87.0 percent, so the market turns over slowly and a well-priced home stands out.

At $953 a month, median rent is low as well, which is why some Austin owners keep a house as a rental and others decide to sell it. If you are weighing that choice, the rental registration rules below are worth reading first.

Does a flood history affect selling a house in Austin?

Yes, it can, because many Austin homes were built in the Cedar River floodplain and buyers and lenders ask about it. The city's flood history lists major floods in July 1978, 1983, 1993, spring 2000 when the Cedar River crested at 23.4 feet, September 2004 and 2010. Dobbins Creek and Turtle Creek also run through town.

The city answered with buyouts. Flood-prone homes were purchased and demolished using a Community Development Block Grant and the Hazard Mitigation Grant Program, low areas were turned into parks, dikes were added after 2004, and a flood wall protecting downtown was finished in 2014. Should your lot be near the river or one of the creeks, ask City Hall at 500 4th Avenue NE for the parcel's floodplain status before you list, and ask your insurance agent what flood coverage costs.

Tornadoes are the other weather risk on record. An EF2 tornado crossed the northwest and north side of Austin on June 17, 2009. Roof age, siding and tree condition are the details a buyer's inspector will notice after a storm-prone stretch of years.

What permit and yard rules should an Austin seller check first?

Check your permit record first. The city's own FAQ warns that if you sell a building with modifications done without a permit, you may be required to tear the addition down, leave it unoccupied or pay for costly repairs. Permits are usually needed for additions, decks, garages, fences, pools, water heaters, re-roofing and electrical, plumbing and heating work.

Two routine ordinances also generate liens against sellers who ignore them.

  • Grass and weeds. City Code 10.13 sets an 8 inch height limit. After a notice from the weed inspector you have seven days to comply, then the city cuts it and certifies the cost to the Mower County Auditor as a special assessment collected like real estate taxes.
  • Sidewalk snow. Chapter 7.04 requires owners to clear public sidewalks within 12 hours after snow stops, and the city may clear them after 24 hours and bill the owner.

Deal with both before closing, since an unpaid assessment is collected the way real estate taxes are. Austin also does not allow chickens, which matters if you kept hens and a buyer asks about the coop.

Do Austin rental registration rules apply when you sell?

They apply if the house is a rental, and they can affect the buyer. Austin requires residential rental property to be registered under City Ordinance 4.29, and the city's rental program FAQ says a Change of Ownership form must be filed when a rental is sold. Ask the city whether the same tenants will stay with the new owner, because that decides which form is used.

If you live elsewhere for part of the year, the program also asks you to name a local rental manager who handles emergencies and inspections. Anyone planning to keep the tenants will want to see the rental registration and any inspection results, so pull those documents together before a deal is signed.

How do Mower County property taxes work at closing?

Mower County bills property tax in two halves, due May 15 and October 15, and second-half agricultural tax is due November 15. The Auditor-Treasurer's office is in the Government Center at 201 First Street NE, Suite 7, in Austin, and the phone is 507-437-9535.

  • The county does not mail second-half statements, so a buyer should ask for the amount.
  • Mail payments are judged by postmark, and a private postage meter mark does not count.
  • The county will not accept post-dated checks.
  • A missing statement does not excuse a late payment.

On the deed side, Minnesota Statute 287.21 sets the state deed tax at .0033 of the net consideration when the price is above $3,000, and the Hennepin County recorder's checklist adds that an eCRV is required for sales over $3,000 and that a deed cannot pass title while taxes are delinquent. A well statement or well disclosure certificate also has to accompany a transfer deed. Ask the Mower County recorder for the local filing steps and fees.

What must you tell a buyer in writing?

Minnesota Statute 513.55 requires a written disclosure of material facts you know before the purchase agreement is signed. It covers facts that could adversely and significantly affect an ordinary buyer's use and enjoyment of the property, made in good faith and to the best of your knowledge. A separate radon statute, section 144.496, adds a written radon disclosure and a copy of the Minnesota Department of Health booklet.

For an Austin house, the facts buyers care about most are basement water, past flooding, roof and furnace age, and any work done without a permit. Writing these down early keeps negotiations short, and it matters even more in a quick sale where the buyer is not hiring an inspector.

More questions about Austin, MN

Do I need an inspection from the city before selling in Austin?

Ask the building department at City Hall, 500 4th Avenue NE, whether any sale-time step applies to your address, and gather your permits and any rental registration so a buyer can see them.

What happens if I have unpermitted work on my Austin house?

A buyer may be able to require you to remove it, leave it unoccupied or pay for repairs. The city's FAQ says exactly that about modifications made without a permit, so ask the building office whether the work can be permitted after the fact before you list.

What are the due dates for Mower County tax?

May 15 and October 15, with second-half agricultural tax due November 15. The county does not mail second-half statements, so request the figure from the Auditor-Treasurer at 507-437-9535 if you need it for closing.

Can a high weed or grass notice block my sale?

It will not block the sale by itself, but unpaid mowing costs become a special assessment on the parcel. Austin allows 8 inches of grass and gives seven days after notice, so cut it early and ask the clerk for any pending charges.

Is Austin a good place to sell to a landlord or investor?

Often yes. Median rent is $953 and 71.5 percent of homes are owner-occupied, so investors look at the town. Registered rentals must follow Austin's rental ordinance, and a sold rental needs a Change of Ownership form filed with the city.
