Owatonna at a glance

Selling in Owatonna?
We buy Owatonna houses as-is, with no commission, no repairs and no closing costs to you.
Get My Cash Offer →

How can an Owatonna homeowner sell without a long wait?

The shortest path is usually a cash purchase from a buyer ready to take the property exactly as you leave it. The alternatives are a traditional listing with an agent and a sale you arrange yourself, and both depend on open houses and on a lender approving the buyer.

Owatonna is the Steele County seat, so the recorder, the treasurer and the county finance office are all in town. That keeps a closing simple, as long as the house has no rental license problems, no delinquent taxes and a clear answer about flooding.

What should a buyer know about the Owatonna area?

Owatonna is named for the Straight River. Settlers arrived in 1853, the town was platted in September 1855, and the city charter followed on February 23, 1865. Downtown and the oldest neighborhoods occupy low ground along the Straight River's eastern side, running south from Maple Creek. The city has since grown in all directions and now sits on both sides of the river, with newer homes along the Maple Creek ravine and beside Brooktree Golf Course.

The city also keeps Kaplan's Woods, a hardwood preserve on its southern edge with more than 6 miles of trails and Lake Kohlmier, a 35-acre lake. The Straight River dam, once used to power a mill, now includes a fish ladder, and the former state school grounds have become the city's West Hills administration complex.

Interstate 35 and U.S. Highways 14 and 218 are the main routes. The Steele County Free Fair fills the fairgrounds each August. Federated Insurance and Viracon both have headquarters here, and Bosch, Jostens, Gopher Sport and Daikin Industries also employ local workers.

Local history is easy to find. The Steele County Historical Society, founded in 1949, runs the Village of Yesteryear on part of the fairgrounds, and Cinder Hill, a steep 60-foot rise on Linn Avenue above downtown, is a familiar training spot for local athletes. Forest Hill Cemetery on the ridge north of Maple Creek marks the line between the oldest neighborhoods and the newer ones.

Schools are a selling point in recent years. Voters approved a bond in 2015 that brought $77.9 million for repairs and security at all seven public school buildings, and a $104 million bond in 2019 paid for a new 317,000 square foot Owatonna High School in the southeast. It opened to students on September 5, 2023.

Has flooding affected Owatonna houses?

It has. Record rain from September 22 to 24, 2010 sent the Straight River and Maple Creek over their banks, and developments built in the floodplains of both streams were completely inundated. Ask the county or city about a parcel's floodplain status if you are unsure.

If your property sits near the river or the creek, write down any water in the basement, drainage fixes or insurance claims you know about before you list. State law requires a seller to give the buyer written disclosure of known material facts, and past flooding is exactly the sort of fact buyers look for. Keep receipts for sump pumps, regrading or waterproofing, because they help show that a problem was handled.

How do Owatonna's housing numbers compare for owners and renters?

Owners occupy three of every four Owatonna homes. The Census Bureau supplies the figures below.

Owatonna by the numbers (QuickFacts; 2020-2024 five-year data unless a date is shown)
IndicatorNumber
Population, July 1, 202526,633 (0.8% above the 2020 base)
Owner-occupied homes75.6%
Median value, owner-occupied$245,200
Median monthly cost, owners with mortgage$1,661
Median gross rent$1,067
Median household income$80,750

There are 11,018 households here, averaging 2.36 people. Workers spend a mean 17.7 minutes getting to work, and 88.3 percent of residents stayed in the same house for a year. Owners with a mortgage pay about $594 a month more than the median gross rent.

What does Owatonna require for a rental property?

Every rental in the city must be registered and licensed through the Fire Department under Chapter 115 of the city code. An inspection is scheduled, and the license is issued once the property passes and the fees are paid. A license is valid for two years.

  • Use one application per rental address.
  • A new application is needed when a property is rented for the first time, when a license expires, or after a change of ownership.
  • Renting without a valid license is a misdemeanor, and every day of renting counts as a separate violation.

If your Owatonna house is rented, make sure the license is current before the closing date. A buyer planning to keep tenants has to apply for a license after the sale. The Fire Department's number is 507-444-2454.

What does the Steele County Recorder charge, and what is the deed tax?

The Steele County Recorder charges $46 to record a document and $54 for a well disclosure statement. Mailed or dropped-off documents are turned around in 10 business days or less, and appointments are available during business hours. A split of a tax parcel carries a $100 fee payable to the county treasurer.

The state deed tax is set by Minnesota Statutes section 287.21. It is 0.33 percent of the net consideration when that exceeds $3,000, and the county collects it when the deed arrives for recording. For a sale at Owatonna's Census median of $245,200, the tax would be $809.16. When there is no consideration, or $3,000 or less, the tax is a flat $1.65.

Before closing, request an itemized settlement statement from the title company that shows the fee, the tax and any unpaid property tax.

When are Steele County property taxes due this year?

Steele County mails real estate tax statements each March, and every owner receives one even if a lender pays the bill. The 2026 schedule has two real estate deadlines, and a weekend due date rolls to the next business day.

  • May 15, 2026 was the first-half deadline for real estate, and October 15, 2026 was the second. Both have passed.
  • Agricultural second-half taxes are due Monday, November 16, 2026.
  • Unpaid 2025 taxes became delinquent on January 1, 2026.

Owners can pay in person at the Finance office in the County Administration Building, 630 Florence Avenue, mail a check to Steele County Finance, P.O. Box 890, or use the drop box out front. The drop box is cleared at 8 a.m. the next business day, and later deposits must include a penalty. Cards add 2.5 percent with a $1.50 minimum, a Visa debit card adds $3.95, and e-checks add $1.50 under $10,000. Direct debit carries no fee, and the authorization forms must reach the Finance office by April 30 for the first half and September 30 for the second.

What should an Owatonna seller ask a cash buyer?

Request a written offer and go through it line by line.

  • Which party orders the title work and pays for recording?
  • How will the buyer handle past flood or drainage issues in the disclosure?
  • If a rental license is active, who finishes the term?
  • What is the exact payout after deed tax and any county balance?

A direct offer lets you set the move date, and that is its main benefit over a listing. Weigh that against what an open-market sale would leave once repairs and months of upkeep are paid.

More questions about Owatonna, MN

Does my Owatonna rental license transfer to a buyer?

A change of ownership calls for a new application, so the buyer applies for a license in their own name. The city issues two-year licenses once an inspection is passed and fees are paid.

How much is the state deed tax on a typical Owatonna sale?

Around $809 for a house priced at the $245,200 median, because the tax equals 0.33 percent of the price once that passes $3,000. The county collects it at the recording stage.

Where do I pay Steele County property tax in person?

Go to the Finance office in the County Administration Building at 630 Florence Avenue, on the ground level, during weekday business hours. A drop box stands out front by the flagpoles.

What does a well disclosure cost in Steele County?

The recording office charges $54 for a well disclosure statement or certificate. The $46 deed recording fee is separate.

Should I mention the 2010 flood when selling an Owatonna house?

Yes, if your property is near the Straight River or Maple Creek and you know of water damage, mention it. The disclosure covers material facts you know of, and a buyer will look for flood history in that area.

Winona at a glance

Selling in Winona?

What is it like to sell a house in Winona?

Selling in Winona means selling into a small river city with a large student population and a lot of rental property. Houses here are far less expensive than in the Twin Cities suburbs, and the local rules that matter most are about rentals, permits and short-term stays.

Winona sits on the Mississippi River in the Driftless Area, about 44 miles from Rochester and 30 miles from La Crosse. A seller can list with an agent, sell privately or take a direct cash offer. Which one makes sense usually depends on the condition of the house and how soon you need to close.

What do the Census numbers say about Winona housing?

The Census Bureau counted 26,530 residents on July 1, 2025, up 2.1% from the April 2020 base of 25,997. The city had lost people between 2010 and 2020, so the recent gain is a reversal.

  • 10,786 households averaging 2.13 people
  • 58.0% of homes owner-occupied (2020 to 2024)
  • Median owner-occupied value: $201,800
  • Median gross rent: $882
  • Median household income: $56,337, with 23.1% of residents below the poverty line
  • 18.9% of residents 65 or older, and 12.5% under 18

The 2020 census found a median age of 31.6 and 39.2% of households with one person living alone. Many Winona sellers are older owners downsizing or heirs handling a parent's house, and many buyers are first-time buyers or investors.

How did Winona grow, and why does it matter for older houses?

Settlers laid out the town in 1852 and 1853 on land the Dakota had known as the village of Keoxa. Population jumped from 815 in December 1855 to 3,000 a year later. Steamboats, lumber, wheat milling and railroads built the economy, and more than 1,300 steamboats stopped in 1856.

German immigrants arrived in 1856, and between 1859 and 1900 about 5,000 Poles and Kashubians settled in the city, roughly a quarter of the population. That history left two historic districts on the National Register of Historic Places that combine into one local historic district under the city's Heritage Preservation Commission. If your house is in that district, ask the city's planning office what review applies before you promise a buyer changes to the exterior.

What local conditions affect a Winona house?

The land is hilly bluff country with a river on one side. The city covers 24.32 square miles, of which 19.03 are land and 5.29 are water, and Lock and Dam 5A crosses the river here. Latsch Island, connected by bridges and part of the city since 1998, holds a community of houseboat residents.

The weather station at Winona records the warmest normal temperature of any in Minnesota, a yearly average of 48.9 degrees Fahrenheit. The January mean is 17.6 and the July mean is 75.8, so houses face hot humid summers and cold snowy winters. Buyers commonly ask about basements, furnaces and roofs, and about whether a property near the river sits in a mapped floodplain. Ask the city's inspections office or your insurer to confirm the status of your address.

How do Winona's rental license rules affect a seller?

Any rental unit in the city must hold a license before tenants move in, and Chapter 33A of the housing code requires an inspection every five years. If you rent out the house you are selling, the inspection and license status will come up in the buyer's due diligence.

The licensing steps on the city page are short:

  1. Planning and Zoning confirms that the property may be a rental.
  2. The owner submits a rental license application.
  3. The Building Inspections Department inspects the unit.
  4. The fee is paid, due upfront for a new rental.
  5. The property must meet the housing code before the license is issued.

The city also provides a Rental License Transfer of Ownership application, which a buyer of a rental house will need. Call Planning and Zoning at 507-457-8250 to ask whether your property qualifies as a rental, and the inspections office at 507-457-8231 to schedule.

How much does a Winona rental inspection cost?

The city charges an inspection fee once every five years for certification. The schedule below took effect January 1, 2026, under City Code Chapter 51.

Winona rental housing inspection fees effective January 1, 2026, from the City of Winona Inspections Department
Property typeCalculationTotal
Single-family dwelling$100 per unit plus $100 per building$200
Duplex$200 for two units plus $100 per building$300
Owner-occupied duplex$100 for one unit plus $100 per building$200
Sleeping room$45 per room plus $100 per building$145 for one room

The owner's own unit in an owner-occupied duplex is not certified, which is why it is charged for one unit only.

Can a buyer use a Winona house as a short-term rental?

Only with a license and a public hearing. The city calls short-term rentals Tourist Homes and defines them as buildings that provide sleeping accommodations to transient guests for up to 29 consecutive days. There are two classes, owner-occupied and non-owner-occupied, each with its own regulations.

  • Every short-term rental must be inspected and licensed
  • Residential zoning districts require a Planning Commission public hearing before licensing
  • A 4% hotel and motel tax on monthly rent has applied since July 1, 2018

If your house has been used for Airbnb-style stays, gather the license paperwork for the buyer. If it has not, assume a new owner cannot start without the hearing.

What repairs and permits come up before closing in Winona?

A building permit is required for additions, alterations, new construction, remodeling and most replacements. Work that does not need one includes painting, cabinets, countertops, floor coverings, tiling, storage sheds under 200 square feet, retaining walls up to 4 feet and decks not over 30 inches above grade, unless attached to a permanent structure.

Fences usually need no permit, but ask Planning and Zoning at 507-457-8250 first. Fences may reach 6 feet in the rear and 4 feet on the street side, and anything over 7 feet needs a variance and a permit. The city does not issue electrical permits, so electrical questions go to the state electrical inspector. An unpermitted deck or finished basement is something a buyer's inspector will notice, so close out any open permits before you list.

What taxes and paperwork apply when a Winona house sells?

The county auditor receives a certificate of real estate value for any sale above $3,000, and Minnesota Statutes 272.115 bars homestead status for the buyer if it is missing. The assessor drops the homestead classification after a sale until the new owner applies and qualifies.

Property sits in Winona County, so the deed is recorded with the county recorder there. Ask the county for current recording fees and the deed tax calculation, and have your title company confirm who files the certificate. Minnesota also lets a seller pass the required disclosure to the buyer's agent instead of the buyer directly.

Who works and studies in Winona, and who buys homes there?

The city's 2022 financial report lists Fastenal as the largest employer at 1,618 people, followed by Winona State University at 1,050, Winona Health at 975 and Winona Area Public Schools at 684. Saint Mary's University of Minnesota, WinCraft, RTP Company and Winona County government also employ hundreds.

Winona State, Saint Mary's and Minnesota State College Southeast bring students and staff who rent, which explains the large rental license program. Highways 14, 61 and 43 lead into the city, Amtrak's Empire Builder and Borealis stop at the old Milwaukee Road depot, and Winona Transit Service runs buses six days a week. Mean travel time to work is 13.8 minutes.

More questions about Winona, MN

Does Winona require an inspection before I sell my house?

Winona's inspection program covers rental units, which need a license renewed through an inspection every five years. For a house you live in, ask the inspections office at 507-457-8231 whether anything applies to your address.

How much is a rental inspection in Winona?

A single-family rental costs $200 total, made of $100 per unit and $100 per building, under the schedule effective January 1, 2026. A duplex is $300.

Can I sell a rental house to a new owner in Winona?

Yes. The buyer files a Rental License Transfer of Ownership application, and the property must still meet the housing code. Planning and Zoning at 507-457-8250 can confirm that the property is eligible.

Are Airbnb stays allowed in Winona?

They are allowed with a license. The city treats them as Tourist Homes for stays up to 29 days, requires an inspection and a hearing in residential districts, and charges a 4% hotel and motel tax.

What is the typical home value in Winona?

The Census Bureau puts the median owner-occupied value at $201,800 for 2020 to 2024. Your own number depends on condition and location, so get a written offer or a local agent's estimate before you decide.

Chanhassen at a glance

Selling in Chanhassen?

What are your options for selling a house in Chanhassen, MN?

Chanhassen owners can market the house through an agent, find a buyer privately, or accept a direct offer from a cash buyer. Values here run higher than in Brooklyn Park, Burnsville or Chaska, so the spread between a polished listing and an as-is sale can be wide enough to justify getting both numbers.

  • An agent listing suits a house that is updated and a calendar with room for open houses.
  • A private sale works when you already know the buyer, such as a neighbor or relative.
  • A cash buyer fits an estate house, a property with a failing septic system, or a move that cannot wait for a school year or a new job.

Owners occupy 84.1% of Chanhassen's homes, so the neighbors a buyer meets are mostly long-term residents rather than tenants.

Where is Chanhassen, and what is it known for?

Chanhassen is mostly in Carver County, about 15 miles southwest of Minneapolis, with a small eastern piece reaching into Hennepin County. The city covers 22.88 square miles, of which 20.44 are land and 2.44 are water. U.S. Highway 212 and Minnesota Highways 5 and 41 are the main routes.

The first settlers arrived in 1852, mostly German farm families. The name comes from a Dakota word for the sugar maple, and it became official in 1858. The village proper held roughly 200 to 250 people near the Church of St. Hubertus, and by the 1940s the township had two general stores, two bars, a feed mill, a lumber yard and a bank. Chanhassen merged with its township and became a city on May 8, 1967, with about 4,200 residents. Population has risen 123.5% since 1990. The Minnesota Landscape Arboretum, Paisley Park, Chanhassen Dinner Theatres and the headquarters of Life Time sit here, and the National Weather Service's Twin Cities forecast office is in town. Five public beaches on Lake Ann, Lake Minnewashta and Lotus Lake and 70 miles of trails give the listing photos plenty to work with.

How do the housing numbers compare to nearby cities?

Home values here lead the four-city comparison by a wide margin: the median owner-occupied value for 2020-2024 was $566,300, against $336,200 in Brooklyn Park.

Chanhassen housing and income, Census Bureau
MeasureChanhassen
Population, July 2025 estimate25,748

Housing units, 2020 census10,020, with 3.8% vacant

Bachelor's degrees belong to 64.1% of adults, and just 2.9% of residents are in poverty. Vacant rentals ran at 8.5% in 2020, versus 5.5% in Brooklyn Park and 4.0% in Chaska, which matters if you are pricing a rental house.

Who is likely to buy a house in Chanhassen?

Buyers skew toward established families. The 2020 count found a median age of 40.9, married couples heading 64.9% of households, and children in 36.8% of them. Per capita income is $76,879, and 90.1% of residents stayed put for a full year, so listings tend to come from owners with long tenure and substantial equity.

The average commute is 22.3 minutes, and 15.4% of residents are 65 or older, which feeds a steady supply of downsizers. If you are selling an inherited house, buyers will compare it with updated listings at much higher prices, so an as-is price reflects the work the buyer takes on rather than the neighborhood's median.

Which school districts serve Chanhassen?

Most of Chanhassen lies in Eastern Carver County Schools, District 112. Typical attendance for those students runs through Bluff Creek and Chanhassen Elementary, Pioneer Ridge Middle School and Chanhassen High School.

The northern sections belong to the Minnetonka School District, District 276, with students usually attending Clear Springs or Excelsior Elementary, Minnetonka Middle School West and Minnetonka High School. Private options in the downtown area include Chapel Hill Academy and St. Hubert Catholic School. The district line can run through a neighborhood, so confirm the specific address with the district before it goes into a listing.

Do septic systems and wells affect a Chanhassen sale?

Yes, for the part of the city that is not on city sewer or water. About 3.9% of residents live in areas the Census classifies as rural, and rural parcels are the likeliest to have private systems. Minnesota law sets two separate disclosures for them.

  • Sewage: a seller must state in writing, ahead of the purchase agreement, whether household sewage goes to a permitted facility or to a subsurface treatment system, and must attach any earlier inspection report (Minnesota Statutes section 115.55, subdivision 6). Staying quiet about a known system can leave the seller paying for compliance work if the buyer sues within two years of closing.
  • Wells: the seller must disclose known wells in writing, and the deed needs a well statement or a certificate with a $54 fee (section 103I.235). Liability for an undisclosed well can run six years from closing.

Carver County lists the subsurface sewage treatment disclosure as required on all property transfers. If you are unsure what is buried in the yard, ask the city's building staff and your title company early.

Can you rent your Chanhassen house short-term before you sell?

Only with a license. Chanhassen's ordinance, in effect since January 1, 2023, requires a license for any property rented for fewer than 30 consecutive days, even if it happens only a couple of times a year. Month-to-month leases do not trigger it.

The license costs $200 a year, is renewed by February 1, and requires a Minnesota state lodging license. License terms set the maximum number of overnight guests and vehicles and require compliance with the nuisance ordinance, including a 10 p.m. to 7 a.m. limit on amplified sound. Three notices of violation within 365 days mean revocation, and the owner cannot hold a short-term rental license again for seven years. Neighbors can report problems to a 24/7 hotline at 952-260-4995. An owner who is listing a house should remove any active short-term listing before the first showing.

How are Chanhassen deeds recorded?

Carver County Land Records and Vitals, 600 East 4th Street in Chaska, records deeds for most of the city; its phone is 952-361-1930, and the counter is open weekdays from 8 to 4:30. The Hennepin County sliver is recorded through Hennepin County, so look at the county printed on your tax statement.

A Carver deed package carries the recording fee, state deed tax, a $5 agricultural conservation fee, a certificate of real estate value for consideration above $3,000, well information, the sewage treatment disclosure, a full legal description, a complete notary acknowledgment, a drafted-by statement and a send-tax-statements-to line. Staff cannot choose a form or give legal advice, so lean on your title company or attorney. The deed tax under section 287.21 is 0.33% of net consideration.

More questions about Chanhassen, MN

Will a cash buyer take a Chanhassen house with a septic problem?

Many will, because they buy as-is and subtract the repair from the offer. The written sewage disclosure is still yours to provide, along with any inspection report in your files.

Which county records a Chanhassen deed?

Carver County, for almost the whole city. The small eastern portion is in Hennepin County, and your tax statement names the county for your parcel.

Can I run Airbnb stays at my Chanhassen home while it is listed?

Only with the $200 annual city license plus a Minnesota lodging license, since any stay under 30 consecutive days counts. Skip it during showings and avoid the enforcement risk.

What is the deed tax on a Chanhassen sale?

The rate is 0.33% of net consideration. On the city's $566,300 median home value that works out to roughly $1,869.

Which school district covers a Chanhassen address?

District 112, Eastern Carver County Schools, covers most of the city, and Minnetonka's District 276 covers the north. Look up the exact address before advertising a school.

Selling in Farmington?

How would you describe Farmington, Minnesota, to someone selling a home there?

Farmington sits in southern Dakota County on the metro's outer rim, and nearly nine in ten homes are owner-occupied. Mid-2025 Census estimates count 25,425 people, up 7.4 percent from the April 2020 base. Roughly 14.6 square miles of land make up the city, which touches Lakeville on its west side, Empire Township on the east, and Castle Rock and Eureka townships to the south.

Locals split town along County Highway 50. The older downtown lies south of that road, where only a couple of large projects have gone in over two decades. North of it, subdivisions are newer, and a third growth area spreads east into Empire Township. A trail along the Vermillion River ties downtown, uptown and the Empire-side neighborhoods together, a feature worth mentioning in a listing or an offer conversation.

The city got its charter in 1872, making it the second-oldest community in Dakota County after Hastings. A fire on November 22, 1879 destroyed several houses, stores, a hotel and a grain elevator downtown. Growth came late: the 2000 count was 12,365, and by 2010 it had reached 21,086.

What do Farmington's housing numbers say about my sale?

The median owner-occupied home in Farmington is valued at $366,200 in five-year survey data covering 2020 through 2024, and 86.5 percent of housing units are lived in by their owners. A seller here is usually competing with other single-family houses, with few apartments in the mix.

Farmington, MN housing and household figures (Census QuickFacts, five-year data for 2020-2024 unless noted)
MeasureFarmington
Population estimate, mid-202525,425
Households8,313
Persons per household2.85
Share of homes lived in by owners86.5%
Typical home value (median)$366,200
Median monthly owner costs with a mortgage$2,175
Median gross rent$1,241

At 27.7 minutes, the average commute is the longest of the four cities in the Census comparison, so many households drive a good distance to their jobs.

Another number worth knowing: 29.1 percent of Farmington residents are under 18, the highest share among the four cities in that comparison, against 24.2 percent in Fridley and 20.8 percent in Inver Grove Heights. Families with children are a large part of the local population, which is worth keeping in mind when you describe the house. Owners without a mortgage report median monthly costs of $781, which is a useful benchmark when a buyer asks what it costs to carry the house.

How do I close out the Farmington city water account when I sell?

Call Farmington Utility Billing at 651-280-6883 before closing to book a final meter reading. The city does not shut water off when someone moves out, so the account keeps running until you close it.

  • Utility bills come quarterly, and the city bills water, sewer, storm water and street lights.
  • Trash and recycling are billed separately by Dick's Sanitation, which handles cancellations at 952-469-2239.
  • Any unpaid final utility bill is certified to the property as a special assessment, so a buyer's title company may hold money back at closing if the account is open.

Landlords selling a rental should know that Farmington keeps rental utility accounts in the owner's name, so the owner has to close the account, not the tenant. A late fee of 10 percent applies to rental accounts that fall behind. Ask Utility Billing for the exact balance on your closing date rather than estimating it from the last bill.

Which schools, roads and employers matter to Farmington buyers?

Farmington Area Public Schools, Independent School District 192, enrolls about 6,900 students. Its attendance area takes in Farmington, eastern Lakeville, and Castle Rock, Empire and Eureka townships. A Lakeville address can therefore sit in a different district, so confirm the district for the exact street before you write a listing.

Main routes are Minnesota Highway 3, Minnesota Highway 50, and Dakota County Roads 31 and 50. A federal air traffic control center for the upper Midwest operates here, and a Kemps packing plant is another long-standing employer. The Dakota County Fairgrounds, about 360 acres with gates on 220th Street and Highway 3, report the highest county fair attendance in the state.

  • Price point: the $366,200 median value compares with $452,500 in neighboring Lakeville.
  • Commute: the 27.7 minute average drive to work is long for the metro.

What are the quickest ways to sell a Farmington house?

Three routes exist: an agent listing, a sale handled on your own, or an as-is purchase by a cash buyer. Each one trades speed against price and effort.

  • Agent listing: strongest when the house shows well and you can ride out inspections and a buyer's loan approval.
  • Do it yourself: skips the commission, though marketing, forms and haggling fall to you.
  • Cash buyer: fits inherited houses, deferred repairs, tenant-occupied rentals and owners behind on payments, since the buyer accepts the house in its present state and the closing date can follow your schedule.

Whatever you choose, Minnesota Statutes 513.55 obliges you to hand the buyer a written disclosure of known material facts before a purchase agreement is signed. Condition questions differ by area: subdivisions north of County Highway 50 are mostly under twenty years old, while downtown houses are older.

What happens at the Dakota County recorder when a Farmington deed is filed?

The county's records office in Hastings handles every Farmington deed. Walk-in filing is by appointment at the Administration Center, and mailed packets go to 1590 Highway 55 in Hastings with a return envelope. Most parcels countywide are abstract property, so your title company will search the record before closing.

Minnesota's deed tax equals the net sale price times 0.0033. At Farmington's $366,200 median, expect about $1,208. A deed also has to carry a well disclosure certificate, or a line stating the seller knows of no wells (Minnesota Statutes 103I.235). Before a deed is accepted, the county auditor looks for delinquent taxes (Minnesota Statutes 272.12). Recording charges are fixed by state law and posted on the county's fee page, so your title company can quote the total.

When are Farmington property taxes due, and who pays at closing?

Dakota County bills in two installments, May 15 and October 15 in 2026, and the autumn one is now behind us. A missed half costs 2 percent on a homestead and 4 percent otherwise, with monthly additions through December (Minnesota Statutes 279.01).

Settlement statements normally split the current year's bill between buyer and seller by closing date. Check the county's parcel search for open balances ahead of listing. The next homestead application deadline is December 31.

If you owe back taxes, ask Dakota County Property Taxation and Records for the payoff amount. Keep your latest tax statement handy so you can confirm the parcel number and the amounts already paid.

More questions about Farmington, MN

How quickly can I close on a Farmington house?

A cash purchase can close on a date you choose, frequently within a few weeks, since no lender appraisal is involved. Listing with an agent generally runs longer. For either path, book the water meter reading with Farmington Utility Billing in advance.

Are repairs required before I sell in Farmington?

The disclosure statute asks for a written statement of material facts you know before a purchase agreement is signed, and it does not list required repairs. Cash buyers take the house as it stands. Retail buyers often negotiate fixes after an inspection.

What becomes of an unpaid Farmington utility bill after a sale?

It stays attached to the property. The city certifies unpaid water, sewer, storm drainage and street light charges as a special assessment, so buyers' title companies usually want the last bill settled. A final read keeps the number accurate.

Who files the deed for a Farmington sale?

Dakota County's records office in Hastings, normally through your title company. The state sets the fees, the deed tax is 0.0033 of the net price, and the deed needs either a well certificate or a no-wells statement.

Can I sell Farmington rental property while tenants live there?

Yes. Go over the lease terms with the buyer and your title company. Farmington keeps rental utility accounts in the owner's name, so plan to close that account on the sale date.

Sell Your Faribault House for Cash

Faribault at a glance

Selling in Faribault?

What kind of city is Faribault for a home seller?

Rice County's seat, Faribault, lies about 50 miles south of Minneapolis and Saint Paul, at the confluence of the Straight and Cannon Rivers. Population stood at 25,040 in July 2025, up 2.3 percent from the 2020 base, according to the Census Bureau. Interstate 35 runs along the western edge, with Minnesota Highways 3, 21 and 60 serving the city.

It is an older city by Minnesota standards: the town was founded in 1855 and incorporated in 1872, and the Alexander Faribault House from 1853 still stands near downtown. Sellers who can state their own house's age and the dates of major updates answer buyer questions faster.

Faribault's nickname is the Athens of the West. A fur trading post on the Cannon River in 1826, moved to the Straight River by 1834, grew into the town site, and the first steam-powered sawmill in early 1854 helped take the settlement from about 20 buildings to more than 250 the next year. That long record means many properties carry decades of ownership history, so it pays to order the title search and a current survey early. Rice County's Property Tax and Elections Office and the recorder, both in Faribault, are the offices a closing agent will deal with.

How does Faribault's housing market compare with the Twin Cities suburbs?

The gap is wide. A typical owner-occupied Faribault house is valued at $241,500 in the 2020 to 2024 survey, against $473,900 in Eden Prairie and $646,300 in Edina. Two of every three households own (66.1 percent), rent runs $1,074 a month, and household income is $61,449 at the median.

  • Households: 8,938, averaging 2.48 people.
  • Adults holding at least a bachelor's degree: 17.6 percent.
  • Persons in poverty: 16.4 percent.
  • Average commute: 19.0 minutes, shorter than in Elk River.

A lower price point means repair costs weigh heavily. A roof or foundation repair takes a bigger share of the sale price here than in a suburb where the median house costs two or three times as much, which is why many owners price a repair against an as-is sale.

What jobs, schools and landmarks shape buyer demand?

Faribault's economy mixes retail, services and light manufacturing. The Faribault Woolen Mill, founded in 1865, closed in 2009 and reopened in 2011. The Tilt-A-Whirl amusement ride was invented in the city in 1926. SAGE Electrochromics, a window glass developer, is based here, and the Minnesota Correctional Facility sits on the former state hospital campus. Most of the commercial block along Central Avenue, the main street, carries National Register status.

Faribault Public Schools covers the whole city with an early childhood center, four elementary schools, a middle school, Faribault High School and an Area Learning Center. The Minnesota State Academies for the Deaf and for the Blind, Shattuck-Saint Mary's boarding school and a South Central College campus are also in town.

What do buyers find around a Faribault house?

The rivers and trails are the draw. The Sakatah Singing Hills State Trail starts at a trailhead on the old White Sands site and runs to Mankato, and Sakatah Lake State Park and Nerstrand-Big Woods State Park are nearby. Interstate 35 was finished around 1975, after which through traffic bypassed downtown, so Central Avenue has become a place for restored historic storefronts and the Paradise Center for the Arts.

Winters matter as well. Wikipedia's 1991 to 2020 normals list roughly 35.5 inches of annual precipitation and 43.3 inches of snowfall, and records run from minus 40 to 110 degrees Fahrenheit. Expect an inspector to study the roof, gutters and basement, and keep receipts for recent work.

What must I disclose in writing when selling in Faribault?

The general duty sits in Section 513.55, covering material facts you know about. Layer on radon under Section 144.496, wells under Section 103I.235 and sewage under Section 115.55.

The well disclosure certificate matters at the county office. Rice County's recorder page says that any transfer needing a value certificate also needs well information, and a deed for a well-free lot must say so. Filing a well disclosure certificate costs $54, and the Health Department's database, or 800-383-9808, shows whether one is already on file.

What are Faribault's rental rules if I want to hold the house instead?

All residential rental properties in Faribault must be registered, licensed and inspected. The city's July 2022 ordinance update ended the requirement for landlords to run criminal background checks, though it still recommends them, and it confirmed an occupancy limit of no less than two times the number of legal bedrooms plus one, with children under age two not counted.

Owners and managers of one or more rental units must hold Crime Free Multi-Housing Phase I certification before a rental license renews. The Building Code Division is at 208 First Avenue NW, phone 507-333-0359, and the rental division can be emailed at rental@ci.faribault.mn.us.

If the training, registration and inspection steps feel like too much for a house you inherited or moved out of, selling is the simpler path.

Where do Rice County taxes get paid, and what is due at recording?

Pay at the Property Tax and Elections Office, second floor of the Government Services Building, 320 Third Street NW in Faribault. The county's schedule is in the table below. A small bill, $100 or less for the year, must be paid whole on the first date.

When a deed goes in for recording, Rice County wants two checks made out to the county: one for recorder fees, one for deed tax and mortgage registration tax, which that tax office handles. The deed tax rate is 0.33 percent (Section 287.21), and the auditor receives the value certificate required by Section 272.115. Reach the recorder at 507-332-6114.

What are a Faribault homeowner's choices?

  • Agent listing: works for a house in sale-ready shape when you can wait for a buyer and a loan.
  • Private sale: you set the price, run showings and manage the contract.
  • Cash purchase as is: often picked for inherited houses, rentals with violations, or homes where repairs would cost more than a retail buyer will pay.

Ask each buyer or agent for a written estimate, and subtract commissions, repairs and holding costs to see what lands in your pocket.

More questions about Faribault, MN

How much is a typical house worth in Faribault?

The survey median is $241,500 for owner-occupied homes. Your house can land above or below that depending on its condition and street, so treat the figure as a rough benchmark.

Can I sell a Faribault rental that is behind on its license?

Yes. Contact the city's rental division at rental@ci.faribault.mn.us or 507-333-0359 to learn what is open, and disclose any known problems to the buyer. A new owner who rents the house will need to register and meet the city's inspection and certification rules.

Who handles recording a Faribault deed?

The Rice County Recorder at 507-332-6114 records deeds, and deed tax is handled by the Property Tax and Elections office. The county asks for separate checks for recorder fees and for deed tax, both payable to Rice County.

Do I need a well disclosure certificate?

If the property has a known well, yes. If you know of no wells, the deed can carry the statement that the seller does not know of any wells on the property. The county charges $54 to file a certificate.

When are Rice County taxes due?

Non-agricultural real property pays on May 15 and October 15, while agricultural parcels pay on May 15 and November 15. A bill of $100 or less for the year is due entirely on May 15.
